title: About this publication
points: This online edition is the official one. Past years are in the archived eCalendars and Course Catalogues.
McGill may change anything here without notice, including fixing errors and altering fees, admission schedules and credit requirements, or revising and cancelling courses and programs.
Senate has the final say on what academic regulations mean.

You are responsible for knowing McGill's procedures, policies and regulations and your program's requirements, and registering means you agree to follow them. Advice is there when you ask, but choosing the right courses to graduate is up to you.
Not every course runs every year. Check the Minerva Class Schedule for what is offered.
The publication year runs from the start of Fall to the end of Summer. If you start at any point in it, you follow the edition that took effect that Fall.

McGill isn't responsible for providing courses, programs, housing or other services when events such as utility failures, fire, flood, strikes, labour disputes, war, insurrection or the law reasonably prevent it.
Throughout, "you" means students newly admitted, readmitted or returning to McGill.

title: University Regulations
points: This part of the catalogue collects the rules for the 2026–2027 year: policies, personal information, registration, fees, student records, exams and services. It can change during the year.

title: Undergraduate
points: The undergraduate regulations cover general policies, personal information, registration, fees, aid, records, exams, advising, exchanges and graduation. Check them from time to time along with related publications.

title: General Policies and Information
points: Keeping up with university rules, and any changes to them, is your own responsibility.

title: McGill Modalities of Instruction
points: Credit courses are in person unless stated otherwise.
Asynchronous: material is prepared ahead and done at a time you choose, sometimes within a set window.
Blended: both online and in-person activities are needed to reach the outcomes.
Distance: you and the instructor are apart and you're off campus; often used to mean the same as online.
Hybrid (hyflex): some attend in the room and others online at the same moment, with equal opportunities.
Online: designed so that being on campus isn't needed.
Remote: a course normally held in person is moved online because of a situation, as in the pandemic.
Synchronous: scheduled live activity, online or in person.
A different modality applies to the whole class, or to a planned subset stated in the outline. It can't be an ad hoc accommodation for one student.

title: Authorization, Acknowledgement, and Consent
points: Applying means agreeing to follow McGill's statutes, rules and policies, and that obligation runs from registration onward.
Check what you submit: wrong or false information can cost you your admission, and McGill can revoke an offer based on it.

title: Student Rights and Responsibilities
points: The Student Rights and Conduct site, run by the Dean of Students and the Secretariat, sets out the rules on your rights and responsibilities. The Secretariat's website has more.

title: Support for Students: Office of the Dean of Students
points: The Dean and Associate Dean of Students lead on advising, academic integrity, discipline, recognition programs and outreach to families and the community.
Office: Brown Student Services Building, 3600 McTavish St., Suite 2100.

title: Office of the Executive Director, Services for Students
points: Coordinates all student services and helps with most non-academic matters. Academic concerns go to the relevant person, office or department.
Office: Brown Student Services Building, 3600 McTavish St., Suite 4100.

title: Recognition of Degrees
points: McGill is a publicly funded institution under a royal charter from 1821, amended in 1852, and incorporated under Québec law.
It was a founder of what is now Universities Canada and belongs to the American Association of Universities and the Association of Commonwealth Universities, among others.
All its degree programs are approved by the Québec government, and its degrees have long been recognized worldwide.

title: Language Policy
points: Teaching is mainly in English, but you may write essays, exams and theses in English or French, unless knowing a language is itself a goal of the course.
To strengthen your English, take an intensive English as a second language course before or as you begin. Continuing Studies and the French Language Centre list options.
Education has special language requirements (p. 691). Continuing Studies students should look at Global and Strategic Communications.
Law: work and exam answers may be in either language, moot courts too, and exam questions may contain material in both whatever the course's language.
Graduate students: see Courses Taken as Extra to a Program in the graduate regulations.
Health Sciences: clinical programs need a working knowledge of both English and French, so see the health sciences language rules and McGill's French proficiency guidelines.

title: Academic Integrity
points: Learn what counts as plagiarism and cheating before you hand anything in. Ask the instructor about referencing, and use Fair Play, the student guide on the subject.
Having unauthorized material in a test or exam is cheating.
Multiple-choice exams are normally screened by computer for unusually similar answers, and the result can be used as evidence in a cheating case under Article 17 of the Code of Student Conduct.
New students must finish an online academic integrity tutorial, in Minerva, during their first semester. Otherwise a hold blocks registration until it's done.

title: Policy on Assessment of Student Learning
points: PASL sets shared principles for assessment across McGill's faculties, for equity, consistency and integrity.
It applies to all credit courses, graduate and undergraduate, that end with a grade on the transcript. Units may add their own guidelines if they agree with it.
It's on the Secretariat's website in both languages.

title: Policy Concerning Access to Records
points: McGill writes to you directly and won't send reports to parents or sponsors unless you ask in writing. Staff can see relevant parts of your record for legitimate use.

Your information is handled under Québec's Access Act and McGill's Privacy Notice. It covers what you submit and your student file: name, contact details, birth date, citizenship, ID, program, status and record.
You can ask to see or correct your information, and object to some releases with an Opposition Form.

McGill may archive your file permanently two years after you finish, exchange data with a home institution, get transcripts from Québec, Ontario and BC bodies, check your immigration and health insurance status with government, and contact you through alumni offices.

It may share data with student associations, schools you attended, professional bodies, ministries, university associations, libraries, funders, other universities if there's evidence of misconduct, volunteers helping you settle in, authorities as required, and McGill's network services.

Referees are told your name, program and term so that they can write for you. Law, Medicine, Dentistry and Music applicants consent to further sharing, such as with LSAC, hospitals or the use of images in concerts.
You accept that admission based on false or incomplete information can be revoked at any time, and that you'll follow McGill's rules once registered. The agreement falls under Québec law.

title: Undergraduate Leave of Absence Policy
points: Possible for parenting, personal or family health, professional development, military service, or immigration status problems. Travel, time off and money are not grounds.
Ask term by term, for up to 52 weeks in all, through your faculty's advising or student affairs office with documents. It appears on your transcript, and you pay no tuition during it.

You keep your ID, McGill mail and libraries but can't register, do internships or research, and normally can't study elsewhere. After a year without returning you become withdrawn, and you may need to show you're ready to resume.
You should normally be in Satisfactory Standing. Services are limited during a leave and fees or scholarships may be affected, so see Student Accounts and Scholarships and Student Aid.
Health coverage takes arrangements with your student society and International Student Services, and may cost extra society fees. International students should talk to ISS first.
Professional programs may limit leaves. M.D.,C.M. students have their own policy. Continuing Studies has no leaves but allows two missed terms in a row, and a year away means reapplying.

title: Health Resources for McGill Students
points: The Student Wellness Hub is where to get physical or mental health care and advice. Your insurance can be used off campus too.
For barriers caused by disability, injury or illness, see Student Accessibility and Achievement for an accommodation plan, on either campus or in Continuing Studies.
UGME and PGME students go to Medical Learner Affairs. Nursing, Physical and Occupational Therapy, and Communication Sciences students go to the WELL Office.

title: International Students (Non-Canadians or Non-Permanent Residents of Canada)
points: All international students and their dependants must join the compulsory International Health Insurance plan, as Québec and immigration authorities require proof of cover. Rates are on the ISS site.
Private insurance doesn't exempt you, but you may qualify for an exemption request in Minerva with documents uploaded to the IHI portal. It lasts one year and must be renewed.
Minors can register for Québec's provincial plan (RAMQ). Continuing Studies students in credit courses are billed for IHI as well.

title: Canadians Residing in Canada
points: Students starting in Fall are automatically in their society's (SSMU, MCSS or PGSS) health and dental plan, valid only with provincial coverage or IHI. Studentcare has the details.
Coming from outside Québec? Make sure your home province's coverage stays valid.

title: Canadians Who Have Been Residing Outside Canada
points: Register for RAMQ on arrival if eligible. If not, you may join the IHI plan, but only in the first month of a new semester.
Continuing Studies students have a plan through MACES. Graduate students have the PGSS plan, with a set window to opt in or out.

title: Accessibility and Academic Accommodations
points: For medical needs, book with the Student Wellness Hub. For barriers from disability, injury or illness, Student Accessibility and Achievement sets up accommodations, possibly with documents, on both campuses and in Continuing Studies.
UGME and PGME: Medical Learner Affairs. Nursing, Physical and Occupational Therapy, and Communication Sciences: the WELL Office.

title: Academic Accommodation for Pregnant Students and Students Caring for Dependants
points: McGill has guidelines on how and when pregnant students and those caring for dependants can ask for academic accommodation in exceptional cases, so that they can continue their program.

title: Health Professions – Immunization Requirement
points: New students in health care programs, Dietetics and Social Work included, must complete a compulsory immunization program well before classes begin. The Wellness Hub has details.

title: Explore McGill
points: A list of the official ways to see McGill in person and online. Undergraduate Admissions has programs, requirements, dates and scholarships.

title: Virtual Tours
points: 360° online tours of both campuses, with menus and optional audio.

title: Book a Campus Tour
points: A 90-minute guided outdoor walk of the downtown campus with student ambassadors. Doesn't include athletics or residences. Register on the Campus Tours portal.

title: Visit the Macdonald Campus
points: Guided tours in Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue, home of agriculture, environment and food science programs. Register through the Macdonald portal.

title: Music Facilities
points: Tours of the Schulich School of Music's downtown buildings and spaces, booked from its Campus Tours page.

title: Meet McGill (On-Campus and Online Events)
points: Program events and the Meet McGill series are by invitation for admitted students, and may include tours and talks on student living.

title: Open House
points: Held each fall with tours. Details change yearly, so see the Open House site.

title: Start Your Visit at the Welcome Centre
points: In person downtown: the McGill Welcome Centre, 3415 McTavish St., Monday to Friday 10:00–16:00, helps you find tours, admissions information and resources.

title: Stay in the Loop
points: Use the Admissions hub to explore, apply and join events. Student-for-a-Day has ended.

title: Personal Information
points: Keep your address, phone and emergency contact current in Minerva's Personal Menu: McGill uses them all year and asks you to check every six months.
Name, gender or birth date corrections need official documents, as set out on Student Records. Macdonald students can do it at Laird Hall, Room 106.
Nursing students need a Québec address and phone number in Minerva for OIIQ registration.

title: Submitting Legal Documents
points: McGill needs documents proving your legal status. What you send depends on your situation.

title: What Documents Does McGill Need from You
points: Requirements can change, so go by the Legal Documents website.

title: Québec and Canadian Out-of-Province Students
points: From CEGEP or already in McGill's records: usually nothing. Check your status in Minerva under Student Accounts, View Tuition and Legal Status.
From another Québec university: proof of Canadian status. Québec residency usually needs nothing further.
Born in Québec: Québec birth certificate.
Born in another province or a Landed Immigrant: proof of Canadian status and a Permanent Code Data Form.
Québec resident through another situation: proof of status, Permanent Code form, Attestation of Residency in Québec, and whatever else it asks for.

The Permanent Code form can often be skipped if you've given your parents' names or already have a code. Permanent Residents can use the confirmation (IMM 5292 or 5688), PR card or Record of Landing (IMM 1000). A Québec birth is proven by the certificate or, with a code, a Canadian passport showing it.

title: International Students
points: Under six months (Exchange, Special, Visiting): a visitor permit or eTA if required, passport photo page and Permanent Code form.
Longer (a degree, certificate or diploma): CAQ, study permit, passport photo page and Permanent Code form.
Forms are on the Forms and Reference Materials page.

title: Fee Exemptions
points: Québec authorizes exemptions from out-of-province or international supplements in three categories.
French courses: full-time international students pay the Québec rate on eligible French courses, with some exclusions.
Out-of-province: non-Québec Canadians in a Ph.D., in postgraduate medical education, or registered full-time in a Master's in French, from when they register and not retroactively.

International, by legal status: citizens of France or of agreement countries, diplomats and staff of international bodies, convention refugees, those awaiting permanent residency with a CSQ, spouses or dependants of temporary workers, and FRSQ-funded students. Some are charged at the Canadian rate.

title: Where and How Do I Send My Documents
points: Send clear copies by email after accepting and before classes, not originals, with your student ID in each file's name. The Legal Documents site has instructions by category.
Problems: Service Point.

title: Why Does McGill Collect Legal Documents from You
points: Your documents set your tuition rate (Québec, out-of-province, international) and confirm your status.

They also get you a Permanent Code, a 12-character code from Québec's Ministry of Education required of all students in the province. You already have one if you studied in Québec. It appears on your unofficial transcript.
Medicine and Health Sciences asks for more documents during admission and registration.

title: Québec/Canadian/International Fees and Immigration Status
points: Processing takes 5–10 business days. In Minerva, select the right term under View Tuition Fee and Legal Status and read the line saying which rate you're charged.
If you disagree, tell McGill right away. Papers must arrive within the semester; changes are never retroactive, and late ones apply from the next semester.

title: Permanent Code
points: Created or checked by the Ministry, usually within six to eight weeks of your first semester. See it in Minerva. If it's not there, your documents are missing or not yet confirmed.

title: What Are the Consequences of Not Providing Your Documents
points: The deadline to change your tuition status is the last day of classes, such as December 1 for Fall and April 1 for Winter.
Missing documents after the term starts bring a hold on registering, dropping and sometimes your transcript. International students without valid immigration papers may be de-registered.

title: Identification (ID) Cards
points: Needed for exams, libraries and services, residences, meal plans and the shuttle. It belongs to McGill, isn't transferable, and goes back to Enrolment Services (or Macdonald Student Affairs) if you withdraw from everything.
Register for at least one course and wait 24 hours. Keep it between terms if you're returning.
Replacing an expired card or changing program is free if you hand the old one in; lost, stolen or damaged cards cost a fee (see Student Accounts).
For access to labs and buildings, ask the building's Area Access Manager. Continuing Studies students wait a day and return the card when withdrawing.

title: ID Card Schedule for the Downtown Campus
points: New students can get a card 24 hours after registering for their first course, and returning students any time the centres are open if registered. Student Records lists locations and hours.

title: ID Card Schedule for the Macdonald Campus
points: The centre is in Laird Hall, Room 106, in Student Affairs. Same rule: 24 hours after first registering. Dates for new students are on the Important Dates site.

title: Legal Name
points: Your legal name is on your degree, official transcript, e-bills and tax receipts, and is used for your Permanent Code. On admission it's checked against one of the documents below, in this order of preference.

Canadians and PRs: birth certificate or citizenship card (a passport won't do), Record of Landing, a marriage certificate from outside Québec (or a Québec one from before 1984), or a Certificate of Change of Name with driver's licence or health card.
International: study or work permit, CAQ, passport, birth certificate with translation, consulate letter, marriage certificate, or a change of name certificate with passport or licence.
To update: fill in a Personal Data Change Form, attach the document, and email both as PDF or TIFF to permcode@mcgill.ca.

title: Legal Sex Designation
points: Same steps as a legal name: a Personal Data Change Form and an accepted document, emailed to permcode@mcgill.ca.

title: Preferred First Name
points: Your legal name stays on official documents such as transcripts, reports to government, attestations, diplomas and e-bills.
A preferred first name shows up on unofficial ones such as ID cards, class lists and advising transcripts, and doesn't change your legal name.
Set it in Minerva under Personal Menu, Name and Pronoun Change, as early as you can. You can also ask IT for a matching McGill email alias.

title: Verification of Name
points: Check your name in Minerva. You can fix case, accents and spacing yourself, but a legal name change needs official documents. Continuing Studies students bring theirs to the Client Services Office.

title: Online (Distance) Programs
points: Students in fully online programs must declare where they're located each term in Minerva, because location affects fees. Forms open July 16 for Fall, November 16 for Winter and March 16 for Summer.
Undergraduate program: Integrated Nursing (B.N.I., p. 1081).

Studying in Québec means provincial rates by residency; outside Québec, deregulated rates. Self-funded programs pay differently. Some fees, like Athletics, are lower or removed for those away from Québec.

To change a declaration, Continuing Studies students call or email, and others go to Service Point, with proof of location by the last day of classes (August 15 for Summer). After that it waits for the next term.
Falsely declaring you're in Québec can lead to deregulated tuition and action under the Code of Student Conduct.

title: Undergraduate Programs
points: Integrated Nursing (B.N.I.) (65 credits) (p. 1081)

title: Graduate Programs
points: Online: Chronic Pain Management, Cybersecurity and Healthcare Management (Gr. Cert., 15 credits each), Analytics and IMHL (M.M., 45), Multilingual Digital Communication and Occupational Health (M.Sc.A., 45).

title: Continuing Studies Programs (Undergraduate and Graduate Levels)
points: Online certificates (30 credits): Applied Cybersecurity, Indigenous Business Management, Public Administration and Governance. Legal Translation (Gr. Dip., 30).

Graduate certificates (15): Data Analysis for Complex Systems, Data-Driven Decision Making, Public Administration and Governance, Public Relations and Communication Management Practice, Strategic Public Relations and Communications Management.

title: Registration
points: After confirming you're coming, register in Minerva in your window and adjust until your schedule is final. The Class Schedule and this catalogue have course descriptions.
Arts and Science have their own pages. New Engineering students must see an adviser during the advising period, and returning ones at the start of Fall and Winter.
Law: returning students choose courses in June, using materials from Student Affairs.
M.D.,C.M. and D.M.D. students register online for prescribed Fall courses. Follow Medical Admissions (Med-1) or the UGME office (Med-2 to 4).

title: Registration Periods
points: Your start time is in Minerva under Registration, Step 1. See When to Register for details.

title: Returning Students
points: Undergraduates register between May 27 and August 14, 2026. Some faculties set their own schedule, so check with Student Affairs.
Law uses rolling priority by year, fourth-years first, set with the Law Students' Association.
Medicine and Dentistry must register for at least one course by August 14 or pay late fees.

title: Newly Admitted Students
points: Some faculties require meeting an adviser first. You may register for Summer before a Fall start. Law students get instructions in their orientation package.
Health Sciences students must register by August 14 and attend the mandatory orientation and registration session.

title: New Students Starting in Fall 2026
points: Registration runs June 10 to August 15, 2026. See the start dates for new undergraduates.

title: New Students Starting in Winter 2027
points: Registration runs December 1, 2026 to January 5, 2027 without penalty. The DMD Advanced Standing pathway begins in the first week of December 2026. Law and Nursing don't admit for Winter.

title: Late Registration
points: Late registration carries a fee. Returning and new Fall students: August 15 to September 15, 2026. New Winter students: January 6 to 19, 2027.
If you were admitted late and can't register online, your acceptance letter explains how to get special permission.

title: Course Change Period
points: You can add and drop from the day registration opens until the add/drop deadline, which is also the late registration deadline. Winter courses can be changed during Fall too.
After that, adding takes written approval from the instructor and your Associate Dean or Director, plus a fee per course.
Arts and Science requests go through Service Point, but talk to an adviser too.

title: Dropping all Courses
points: Before the end of August (Fall) or December (Winter): you simply aren't registered that term. New students may defer; returning students follow readmission.
After those dates: you're University Withdrawn, noted on your transcript, and readmission applies. Health Sciences students see their own section.

title: Course Withdrawal
points: After add/drop there's a short period to withdraw with a W and a full refund, then a longer one with a W and no refund. Later still, withdrawal is exceptional and never just because of poor work; it shows W or WF without affecting GPA.

It's up to you to do it. Telling the instructor or not attending isn't enough, and the date in Minerva is the official one, even if you stopped going earlier. If you don't withdraw and miss the exam, you get a J.
Required or complementary courses may need an adviser's approval and a form. Music has extra limits, and withdrawals can affect aid, Work Study, immigration status and work permission.

Dietetics Stage and similar internships have different dates. M.D.,C.M. allows changes only on an approved leave. Physical and Occupational Therapy need the Program Director's approval, and Nursing the Director's after the deadline, by written request. Law students are encouraged to see an adviser, and graduate students use a course change form.

title: Courses that begin in the Fall 2026 Term
points: With refund: Tuesday, September 22, 2026.
Without refund: Tuesday, October 27, 2026 for single-term courses; Tuesday, January 19, 2027 for multi-term courses starting in Fall, with only the Winter part refunded.

title: Courses that begin in the Winter 2027 Term
points: With refund: Tuesday, January 26, 2027.
Without refund: Tuesday, February 23, 2027 for single-term courses; May 15, 2027 for multi-term courses starting in Winter, with only the later part refunded.
