Fee refunds, if any, will be in accordance with Fees and Withdrawal from the University

title: Class Schedule
points: Fall and Winter usually appear in Minerva in May, two weeks before registration, and Summer in early February. It shows times, rooms, instructors and any prerequisites or permissions needed.
It changes, so check it when registering and again before classes. The last day of classes depends on a course's pattern (see Important Dates).
Health Sciences students see their faculty's section; M.D.,C.M. students see the UGME site.

title: Visual Schedule Builder
points: VSB shows your possible schedules as a week. It can't register you, but you can copy the CRNs into Minerva.

title: Course Information and Regulations
points: Courses and programs can change or be cancelled without notice, and not all are offered yearly, so check the Class Schedule.
Graduate, Health Sciences and Summer students have further rules in their own sections.

title: Course Numbering
points: Seven characters: four letters for the subject, then three digits whose first is the level.
100–400: undergraduate, with 300–400 usually for your last two years. 500: senior undergraduates and graduate students. 600–700: graduate only.
Two more characters (D1, D2, N1, N2, J1, J2, J3) mark multi-term courses. Student Records' Transcript Key explains numbers from before 2002.

title: Multi-Term Courses
points: Most courses finish within one term. Multi-term versions spread the same content and credits over two or three terms, and you can get credit for only one version.
D1/D2: two consecutive terms, same section, credit once both are passed; registering for D1 in Fall signs you up for D2.
N1/N2: two non-consecutive terms, same section, within 12 months. J1/J2/J3: three consecutive terms, same section.
Arts and Science: registering in different sections can lose you credit, and changing a section in Winter can cause a W on D1, with a fee to reinstate it.

title: Important Conditions for Multi-Term Courses
points: Register for every component in the same section, and pass them in order. Credit comes only at the end, with none for part of it.

title: Course Terminology
points: Prerequisite: pass A before enrolling in B. Corequisite: take A with or before B. Credits are in parentheses after the title (see Credit System, p. 52).

title: Course Nomenclature in Program Descriptions
points: Required: must be done unless exempt, with no choice.
Complementary: chosen from a set list or area to meet program requirements. They aren't electives.
Elective: usually outside your program requirements, with the most choice. Some faculties allow the S/U option. Graduate students need approval.

title: Auditing of Courses
points: McGill doesn't allow auditing. Continuing Studies courses can be taken as non-evaluated.

title: Course Load
points: Minerva stops you going past your faculty's maximum. The usual load is 15 credits per term, and fewer than 12 makes you part-time. See Entrance Awards (p. 50) for load rules tied to awards.

title: Faculty of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences
points: The normal course load is 15 to 18 credits per term.
Students in Probationary Standing may take up to 14 credits.

title: Faculties of Arts and Science (including B.A. & Sc.)
points: New and Satisfactory Standing students: up to 17 credits. CGPA above 3.50: more than 17 by request to Enrolment Services, ideally after seeing an adviser. Probationary Standing: up to 14.

title: Faculty of Education
points: Newly admitted students may take up to 17 credits per term.
Continuing students in Satisfactory Standing may take up to 17 credits per term.
Students in Probationary Standing may take up to 12 credits.

title: Faculty of Engineering
points: Normally 15–18 credits. More than 18 needs your adviser's permission. Deferred exams (grade L) limit you to 18 credits or six exams a term, whichever is more.

Take enough for visa, aid and scholarships. The (3-1-5) pattern after a description means weekly hours of lectures, tutorial or lab, and personal study. Probationary Standing: 13 maximum, repeats included.

title: Faculty of Law
points: The normal course load is 15 to 18 credits per term.
Students in Probationary Standing may take up to 12 credits.

title: Desautels Faculty of Management
points: Newly admitted students may take up to 17 credits per term.
Continuing students in Satisfactory Standing may take up to 17 credits per term.
Students in Probationary Standing may take 12 credits maximum of new material

title: Health Sciences
points: Nursing students in Probationary Standing may take up to 14 credits. See your own faculty's section, and the UGME site for medicine.

title: Schulich School of Music
points: Normally 15–18 credits. Over 18 in Satisfactory Standing needs permission from your adviser or area coordinator. Probationary Standing: up to 14.

title: Courses Taken under the Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory (S/U) Option
points: S/U lets you explore outside your field: one elective a term, to at most 10% of your McGill credits, if your faculty allows.
Apply it in Minerva before the add/drop deadline; you can remove it until the withdrawal without refund deadline. Checking the grade mode and whether the course qualifies is on you.
Instructors grade as usual. A to C becomes S; D, F and J become U. It's out of your GPA, though it counts as attempted, and S earns credits.

For multi-term courses, choose by the first part's deadline. Awards need 27 graded credits, not counting S/U. Visiting, Exchange and IUT students have to arrange it with their home university and McGill's Faculty. Special and U0 Foundation students in Agriculture, Arts & Science and Science can't use it.
Engineering: for Complementary Studies, some Natural Science and Elective courses, not others; D counts as a pass if you skip S/U. Architecture: outside electives only, never toward a minor.
Law: Law and non-Law electives and complementaries, one course up to 4 credits, not for required courses or a minor. Management: not in Minerva, so ask the BCom Office during add/drop.
M.D.,C.M. is pass/fail throughout. Music: non-music electives, not for a major or minor. Not for B.N.I. and B.Sc.(N.) required courses, nor for Physical and Occupational Therapy.

title: First-Year Seminars
points: Small credit courses (25 students at most) for U0 or U1 students of any faculty, with close contact with the professor and advanced methods. You may take one, first-come, first-served.
Lists: Arts (p. 167) and Science (p. 1109).

title: Changing Programs within Selected Faculties
points: In Minerva's Student Records menu, in Arts, B.A. & Sc., Education (B.A. Education and Kinesiology minor only), Management and Science. See an adviser first; restrictions apply.
Minerva can't change your degree or move you to another faculty.

title: Faculties of Arts, Science, and B.A. & Sc.
points: Foundation students (97+ credits to go): can't change the program, only its options, until promoted.
96 or fewer: change majors, minors and honours in Minerva, with limits.
Science students choose majors or honours only within the group they were admitted to, though any minor. Moving group takes an Intra-Faculty Transfer.

title: Desautels Faculty of Management
points: Add or change certain programs in Minerva. Confirm limits with the B.Com. Office.

title: Faculty of Education
points: B.Ed. Secondary students can add, drop or change majors in Minerva.

title: Faculty of Law
points: Adding a major or minor goes through the Student Affairs Office. Program changes are blocked in Minerva.

title: Schulich School of Music
points: Changing or adding a music major takes an Intra-Faculty Transfer in Minerva by the deadline. Double majors, double degrees and minors have their own School pages, and a few music minors are open to other faculties.

title: Interfaculty Transfer
points: Apply through Minerva's Faculty Transfer/Readmission menu unless told otherwise, and check your faculty's rules, documents and deadlines.
International and non-Québec Canadian students pay the tuition for newly admitted students in the new degree.

title: Quebec Inter-University Transfer Agreement
points: The IUT lets you register at McGill and another Québec institution at once.

title: McGill Students
points: With permission from your faculty, you may take 3–6 credits a term elsewhere in Québec (sometimes a full 12–15), within your maximum load and degree residency limits. You normally need 60 credits at McGill.
Talk to Student Affairs first. The other university can refuse you, and exam or schedule clashes are your problem. Grades there aren't in your GPA or transcript, and late ones can delay graduation.
Exchange students from outside Québec can't use the IUT.

title: Visiting IUT Students
points: Students from other Québec universities apply online for approval and check their home university's credit and transfer rules. This applies to Nursing among the Health Sciences.
Once both universities approve, you still have to register yourself in Minerva by McGill's deadlines, and any drop must be done in Minerva and in the IUT application.
Engineering's Summer courses are for McGill students only. Continuing Studies visitors register in person by appointment. McGill sends your grades to your home university.

title: University Withdrawal
points: Talk to a Faculty adviser in your Student Affairs Office before deciding.

title: Student's Responsibility
points: You start the withdrawal, by form or in writing to Student Affairs. Telling an instructor or not attending doesn't count, and the date in Minerva is the official one.

Arts, Science and B.A. & Sc.: through Service Point, with a Faculty adviser's help. Law: also speak to Student Affairs. Agriculture: see an adviser after the deadlines. Education, Management and Music: late withdrawal only in exceptional cases.
Physical and Occupational Therapy: if Minerva blocks you, contact Student Affairs.
Graduate students: use the request form by the deadline, and not registering means being withdrawn as of September 1, January 1 or May 1. Returning needs a Request for Readmission.

title: Consequences of University Withdrawal
points: Refunds follow the fee rules (p. 46), and your ID card goes back. Withdrawing in Fall takes you out of the whole year, Fall and Winter. Coming back later means readmission (p. 41).

title: Deadlines for University Withdrawal
points: Not attending? Withdraw officially by dropping every course in Minerva before the deadlines. Dropping everything between September 1 and the Fall add/drop deadline, or January 1 and the Winter one, also counts.
If Minerva blocks the last course, your Student Affairs Office will guide you, as long as the deadline hasn't passed. Readmission is how you return.

title: Fall Term
points: September 1–22, 2026: dropping all courses is a withdrawal with refund, less the cancellation fee (returning) or deposit (new). Deadline: Tuesday, September 22, 2026.
Without refund: Tuesday, October 27, 2026.

title: Winter Term
points: January 1–19, 2027: same as Fall, with refund. Deadline: Tuesday, January 19, 2027.
Without refund: Tuesday, February 23, 2027.
For D1/D2 courses, partial refund ends at the Winter add/drop deadline.

title: Deferred Admission
points: Ask in the Applicant Portal by August 31 for Fall or December 31 for Winter, after paying your deposit. Drop any courses first if you've registered. The deposit stays on your account if it's granted.
Miss the date and you reapply. Registered students who withdraw after add/drop use readmission instead.

Music doesn't allow deferral. Law normally doesn't, but you may accept, pay and write to the Assistant Dean (Admissions and Recruitment) with reasons. M.D.,C.M. requests go to the Medical Admissions Office by July 1.

title: Readmission
points: After a withdrawal, apply in Minerva's Faculty Transfer/Readmission menu, explaining your absence and what you did. It isn't guaranteed. New students qualify only if they left after the refund deadline.
If you left because of illness, give Student Affairs a medical note saying you're ready. Medicine needs one from your physician or counsellor too.
You normally come back under the requirements then in force, and your faculty decides what remains. A different faculty means a transfer request.

Fees can change after a break for non-Québec and international students. Graduate students submit a Request for Readmission. Agriculture: Student Affairs. Music: studentaffairs.music@mcgill.ca, including re-audition rules. Law: admissions.law@mcgill.ca.

title: Faculty/School Specific Information
points: Your faculty's section of the catalogue applies to you too.

title: Agricultural and Environmental Sciences
points: Its courses have no supplemental exams.

title: Arts
points: Arts OASIS has the Faculty's course information. Terms after the credit weight show when a course normally runs.
Courses have limited enrolment. Minerva can't check every rule, so a course breaking them can pass registration, then be marked "not for credit" after add/drop, which can delay graduation.
Check early whether you need permission from the instructor, department or Faculty. To take something that may not count, ask your Associate Dean or Director.

title: Education
points: Some courses run only in the evening or in Summer. Watch prerequisites, corequisites and Field Experience registration.

title: Engineering
points: Most courses, including Architecture's, are for Engineering students only. Others need permission from the Student Affairs Office in the Engineering Student Centre, and a few ARCH courses are open.
(3-1-5) under a description means 3 lecture hours, 1 tutorial or lab hour and 5 hours of study a week.

title: Extra Courses
points: A course outside your program can be marked "extra" when you register (RX, later E), which keeps it out of your GPA. Not possible after add/drop, nor for program or minor requirements.

title: Prerequisites and Corequisites
points: Finish them before registering, or Minerva may drop the course automatically.
If Advanced Standing or a placement exam covers it but you're blocked, your department or school can give an override.

title: Management
points: Important sections: Grading and Credit (p. 909), credit structures (p. 912, p. 913) and the Management Core (p. 914).

refs.label: BCom Program Credit Structure: General Management Program (Concentrations)
BCom Program Credit Structure: Major or Honours Programs

title: Science
points: The Faculty's Undergraduate Studies page has its course information. Otherwise, the same as Arts: limited enrolment, and courses that break the rules may be flagged "not for credit" after add/drop, delaying graduation.
Check permissions early, and ask your Associate Dean or Director about courses that may not count.

title: Summer Term Studies
points: Over 600 credit courses starting in May, June or July, mostly one-month intensive, and often transferable elsewhere. Finishing your degree in Summer means Fall convocation, usually in November.
Maximum 12 credits (Music 18) across Summer, here or elsewhere, unless your Associate Dean or Director agrees.

At most two Arts, Education, Engineering, Management or Science courses in a session, which is already heavy. More takes written permission from your Faculty; visitors need their home university's too.
IUT students: one course per Summer term, or more with approval through bci-qc.ca.

title: Fees
points: The published fees can change without notice, and this text was last updated in March 2025. Student Accounts has current rates. Scholarships and Student Aid covers financial support, and graduate students see Graduate Funding.

refs.label: Fees and Withdrawal from the University

title: Billings and Due Dates
points: How and when you're billed.

title: Access to Fee Information
points: See your Account Summary by Term in Minerva. Fall fees appear in mid-July.

title: Confirmation of Acceptance Deposit
points: Accept your offer in Minerva's Applicant Menu and pay the deposit, which varies by program, by AMEX, Visa or MasterCard.

title: Invoicing of Fees
points: Billed by term, through e-bills only. They cover tuition, fees, insurance and other charges, normally appear at the start of the month, and are announced to your McGill email. Later charges appear right away in Minerva's account summary.
Not reading your email doesn't cancel interest or late fees.
Payment dates as printed: Fall, August 29, 2025; Winter, January 5, 2026 (returning and new). Check Student Accounts for current ones.
A balance over $100 at the end of October (February for Winter) brings a late fee. When a deferral ends, the next e-bill shows it, and interest and penalties follow if unpaid.

title: Guest Access in Minerva
points: You can let a guest see e-bills and tax receipts and pay online, and you can revoke it any time. They're emailed a link, and Service Point can answer their questions.
Or set an Alternate Student Billing email to send a copy of the notice and balance. Never share your PIN.

title: Payment Procedures
points: Student Accounts lists the ways you and guests can pay.

title: Yearly Fees and Charges— Undergraduate
points: Undergraduate tuition depends on the credits you take. Rates are on Student Accounts.

title: Tuition Fees
points: Rates change yearly and are posted when known.
Missing documents by December 1 (Fall), April 1 (Winter) or August 1 (Summer) means being billed at the non-Québec Canadian or international rate.
If your residency status should change during a term, ask Service Point before the first payment about a deferral. Past interest and fines aren't reversed.
Online students declare their location each term in Minerva. In Québec they pay provincial rates, and outside it deregulated rates.

title: Québec Students and Non-Québec (Canadian or Permanent Resident) Students
points: Québec rules require proof of your rate; some non-Québec Canadians pay the Québec rate. Exceptions are listed on Student Accounts.

title: International Students
points: Students in certain categories can claim an exemption and pay the Québec rate, or sometimes the Canadian one. Categories and papers are on the Legal Documents site, with more on Student Accounts or at Service Point.

title: Tuition Assistance for McGill Staff
points: Staff may get a waiver of up to 100% of eligible tuition. Not completing courses cancels it, and you then pay normally.

title: Staff Dependent Waivers
points: Dependants of staff or pensioners may get a reduction, credited to the account once confirmed and shown on a T4A in February. See HR policies or the MUNACA agreement.

title: Compulsory Fees
points: Current rates are on Student Accounts.

title: Student Services Fees
points: Overseen by a Senate committee with equal student and staff numbers, and topped up by Québec, McGill and donors.

Pays for the Student Wellness Hub, Counselling and Tutorial Services, Religious and Spiritual Life, CaPS, Scholarships and Student Aid, International Student Services, Student Accessibility and Achievement, Campus Life and Engagement, and First Peoples' House.

title: Athletics and Recreation Fee
points: Covers access to most facilities on both campuses. Courses, intramurals, pay-as-you-go and the Fitness Centre cost extra.

title: Student Society Fees
points: Compulsory, collected for student groups and set by referendum, with votes in Spring or Fall.
Canadians get health and dental cover through these fees, and international students get dental, with health through the compulsory IHI plan.

title: Administrative Charges and Other Fees
points: Registration: charged to everyone in courses and programs. Information technology: for services, training and support.
Transcripts and diploma: free transcripts while enrolled, plus diplomas and part of convocation. Those away for over 12 months pay per official transcript.
Copyright: for using protected material, as Québec and Canadian law requires.
General administrative: indexed the same way as tuition, with part going to Athletics (not in Continuing Studies).

title: Other Fees
points: For further information about administrative charges, see mcgill.ca/ student-accounts/tuition-fees/non-tuition-charges/society-services-and-administrative-fees.
For the current year's non-tuition charges, please refer to mcgill.ca/ student-accounts/tuition-fees/non-tuition-charges.

title: Other Fees: Health Sciences
points: In each section: Dentistry and Medicine (p. 947), Nursing (p. 1064), Physical and Occupational Therapy (p. 1088).

title: Fees and Withdrawal from the University
points: Withdraw officially (p. 40) or you owe all tuition and fees, even if you stopped attending.
Dropping your last course from September 1 (or January 1) to the end of the full-refund period counts as withdrawal, with a $200 cancellation fee.
New students who drop everything for a full refund pay $200, or lose the deposit if they paid one. Student Accounts explains the financial effects.

title: Fee Refund Deadlines
points: Refund dates are separate from course withdrawal dates.
Graduate students generally get no refund for Summer courses; new ones withdrawing from a Summer Term of Residence should see Summer Registration.

title: Fall Term – Up To And Including September 16
points: 100% refund for returning and new students, less the $200 cancellation fee on complete withdrawal.

title: Fall Term – After September 16
points: No refund.

title: Winter Term – Up To And Including January 20
points: 100% refund for returning and new students, less the $200 cancellation fee on complete withdrawal.

title: Winter Term – After January 20
points: No refund. Refunds include tuition and compulsory student fees.
For a special case, undergraduates ask their Student Affairs Office, and graduate students their Graduate Program Director or Coordinator.

title: Refund Procedures
points: Credit balances stay on your account unless you ask for them in Minerva, if over $2.00. With awards, you may wait until add/drop ends, as most need full-time status.
Give Canadian direct deposit details, or a refund charge applies.

title: Other Policies Related to Fees
points: Other fee rules that may apply to you.

title: Overdue Accounts
points: You must pay in full or arrange to settle. Unpaid 60 days after billing, your account is delinquent: a hold stops official transcripts and Minerva registration, and may stop diplomas and meal plan top-ups. McGill may ask for a certified cheque or money order.
Interest is 1.24% a month (14.88% a year), charged within 2–3 days of the due date and reset each Spring.
McGill needn't issue transcripts or diplomas, or re-register you, while tuition, library, residence fees or loans are unpaid. Check your balance regularly.

title: Information for Registered Students
points: Owing from an earlier term? Pay or arrange with Student Accounts before add/drop ends, or your current and later registration is cancelled. If money's tight, start with the Student Aid Office: Brown Building, 3600 McTavish, Room 3200.

title: Information for Students Who Are No Longer Registered
points: Unsettled debts or out-of-date contact details can lead to a collection agency and possibly a credit bureau report. McGill may use legal means, at your cost.

title: Cancelling Registration for Non- Payment of Previous Term(s)
points: Owing more than $100 or being delinquent brings notices from Student Accounts, then cancellation on the last day of add/drop.
Settling later? Submit the Request for Reinstatement form. Enrolment Services decides, and a Reinstatement Penalty applies.

title: Acceptance of Fees vs. Academic Standing
points: Paying fees doesn't guarantee you can continue. If your standing doesn't allow it, fees paid in advance are refunded.

title: Deferred Admission, Degree Transfers, Break in Enrolment
points: Deferring means paying the rates for the term you start. Guaranteed rates for international and non-Québec students depend on no break or transfer.
Transferring degrees means the new-student rate for international undergraduates and non-research graduate students, and for non-Québec Canadians.

Québec residents absent over two terms (Summer aside) may need to prove status again. Non-Québec Canadians and international students in such programs away over three terms (Summer included) pay the new-student rate.
Approved leaves, exchanges and study away don't count as a break, but an uncharged withdrawal term does. Visiting and Special students always pay the new year's fees.

title: Fees for Students in Two Programs
points: Expect extra fees for a second program, and possibly both society and faculty fees or more tuition across levels. Bills may be adjusted during term. See Student Accounts.

title: Students Taking Courses Extra to Their Program
points: With permission from your department and Enrolment Services, ask your department in writing to flag the courses as extra. Extra tuition is charged after add/drop. See the Extra Courses policy.

title: Québec Inter-University Transfer Agreements
points: You pay your home university. The agreement only moves credits, and visitors at McGill still pay compulsory course charges such as activities or materials. McGill can refuse registration in non-government-funded activities.

title: Senior Citizens
points: Aid is available for students aged 65 or over in need, in full-time degrees. Contact Scholarships and Student Aid.

title: Students with Sponsors
points: With an outside payer, such as Veterans Affairs, CIDA or a foreign government, you need written proof, and the sponsor confirms on letterhead. Notify McGill at least one month before the term.
If they don't pay within 90 days of invoice, you owe it all with late fees and interest. McGill can insist on payment.

title: Students Receiving McGill Funding
points: Funding goes to your fee account or bank. Check the schedule in Minerva's Financial Aid/Award menu.
If awards come in early January, you can reduce your payment by that amount. Resulting credit balances are refundable only after the full-refund withdrawal deadline.

title: External Scholarships
points: Awards from outside bodies usually come to McGill. Give Student Accounts a letter with the terms. Otherwise it's split across two terms, with the second part on the first working day of January, and returned if you don't qualify.

To count an expected award against your balance, email student.accounts@mcgill.ca at least a week before the deadline with "External Scholarships" in the subject, the amount, currency and source. The deferral ends in September (Fall) or January (Winter), and interest follows.
Refunds are possible only after the full-refund withdrawal deadline.

title: Tuition and Fees – Payment Deferral
points: With no older debts, you may defer payment based on funding you report. It's granted by term, with no interest or late fees meanwhile, and then all is due at the next deadline.
Apply in Minerva from mid-July (Fall), mid-December (Winter) or early April (Summer). Applying by the fee deadline protects you from interest; late applicants can't cancel it.
It covers tuition, administrative and academic fees, and insurance, but not housing, meal plans or printing. Tuition and student housing come first when aid arrives.

title: Tax Slips/Receipts
points: T4A, Relevé 1, T2202 and Relevé 8 appear in Minerva by the end of February.
For Québec returns, give McGill your Permanent Code, SIN and mailing address when registering, as they go to Revenu Québec.

title: Scholarships and Student Aid
points: This office runs merit and need-based awards for new and continuing undergraduates, and all federal, provincial and U.S. government aid. The Undergraduate Scholarships and Awards Calendar has the full list.

title: Entrance Awards for McGill Students
points: For first-time, full-time undergraduates. Merit only, worth $3,000 to $12,000.
Two types: One-Year, on grades alone, and renewable Major, on grades plus leadership.

title: Application Procedures
points: One-Year: automatic when you apply, if you meet the minimum.
Major: apply online by the deadline, after your admission application is acknowledged, with supporting documents. Renewal depends on meeting McGill's standards.
Dentistry, Law, Medicine and Music run their own entrance awards, so ask their admissions offices.

title: Need-Based Entrance Financial Aid
points: First-year students from families of modest means can apply in Minerva once accepted. The amount depends on need and your tuition rate, and you're expected to apply for government aid if eligible.

title: In-Course Awards for McGill Students
points: Decided by faculty committees, mostly using your Fall and Winter sessional GPA or rank in the top 1–5%, with no application unless stated.
You need at least 27 graded credits in the regular year, unless your faculty says otherwise. S/U and Summer courses don't count, and up to 6 IUT credits can.
The Dean's Honour List names at most the top 10% of each faculty, with each setting its minimum GPA. It's on your transcript, with no money.
Awards go to your account for the next year, apart from convocation prizes, and you must be full-time. Renewable scholarships depend on the standards, and the office can help if you're struggling.

title: In-Course Financial Aid
points: For full-time undergraduates with demonstrated need: bursaries, short and long-term loans, and Work Study. Apply for the maximum government aid first. Counsellors also advise on budgeting and debt.

title: Work Study Program
points: Part-time jobs on campus, from office work to research, based mainly on need and also standing, and useful work experience. Office: Brown Building, 3600 McTavish, Suite 3200.

title: Student Records
points: Standing, grading, GPA and transcripts. Check back for changes.

title: Credit System
points: A credit reflects weekly contact hours, and generally a 3-credit course means three lecture hours a week for a term, with labs worth less. Assume two hours of study per contact hour.
One credit is about 45 hours of total work. Live activity must fit the scheduled time, and accredited programs may set minimum contact hours.
Multi-term courses earn credit only when all parts are done in order.
Engineering: a credit is about three hours a week. Summer: a 3-credit course is about 10 lecture hours a week, for five weeks at most, starting in May, June or July.

title: Transcript of Academic Record
points: Shows all attempted work and final grades in all programs. McGill never issues partial transcripts.
Order official ones in Minerva. eTranscripts come through MyCreds™, a secure wallet owned by ARUCC, the same day in as little as 15 minutes if there's no hold, and you pay for share credits.
Paper takes 3 to 5 working days (5 to 7 at peak) by regular mail, is free while registered, and costs alumni a fee. Pre-1972 records take longer.
Both are secured against copying. Holds block orders, so check the top of your unofficial transcript.

title: Unofficial Transcripts
points: View and print in Minerva for records from 1976 on; older ones need an official order.
You must check that your courses, program and graduation term are right. If you're graduating, check before your last term ends or you could be missed. Ask Student Affairs about problems.
Once "Degree Granted" shows, your record is final, with no more changes.
Arts and Science requests go through Service Point, 3415 McTavish, with an OASIS or SOUSA adviser. Graduate students ask their Program Director.

title: Official Transcripts
points: Current students use Minerva's ES Services menu. Paper is for rare needs.
Alumni from 1972 on use the same menu, and the IT Service Desk can supply their ID and PIN. Earlier records need a Request for Archived Official Transcript with photo ID and McGill ID.
Someone else can ask only with your written authorization.

title: Course Numbering on the Transcript
points: Before September 2002, numbers began with a three-digit unit code, then a three-digit course number whose first digit was the level, then a term letter: 107-200A was Philosophy 200 in Fall, B meant Winter and D both.
Continuing Studies used X, Y and Z the same way. The Transcript Key maps old codes to subjects.

title: Grading and Grade Point Averages (GPA)
points: Your transcript shows letter grades, even if instructors report percentages. Courses with 25 or more grade-point grades across sections show a class average.
A–C pass, D is a conditional non-continuation pass, F fails. Program courses and prerequisites need C or better, unless the department chair approves in writing.
GPA is credits times grade points, divided by GPA credits, and cut off at two decimals rather than rounded: 3.596 shows as 3.59. P grades add no GPA credits.
TGPA covers a term at one level, and CGPA your whole record at that level, restarting if you change level. Repeats all count in GPA, with credit given once, and you need a 2.00 CGPA to graduate.

Outlines arrive in the first week and should say whether there's a final, how term work counts and when it's due, and how supplementals work (required if there's a formal final). In Science and B.A. & Sc., they say whether extra work is possible after D, F, J or U.

title: Policy on Pass/Fail Grading
points: P/F must be approved by the Program Director, Faculty Curriculum Committee and SCTP, stated in the syllabus, and applied to the whole section.
P isn't in GPA, so it's rarely used for required courses, while F is. Both count as completed credits for awards.

Engineering: letter grades follow the professor's scheme, not the numerical scale. D is accepted only for certain complementary and elective courses, never core or technical ones. Departments decide about D in a prerequisite.
Global Engineering's first two years at CentraleSupélec follow its grading. Law doesn't use this scale. Physical and Occupational Therapy: C+ minimum in OCC1, PHTH and POTH, and C elsewhere.
Designations: A, A- Very Good. B+, B, B- Good. C+, C Satisfactory. D Conditional Pass. F Fail.

title: Other Grades
points: Not every grade applies everywhere, and faculty rules decide.

J: missed the exam or required work, unexcused; counts as failure. K: instructor extended the deadline. KE or K*: further extension, may need the SAO. KF: missed the extension; counts as failure. KK: requirement waived by the Associate Dean; not in GPA.
L: deferred exam approved. LE or L*: longer deferral. WL: allowed to withdraw from a deferred exam. NR: no grade reported.
P: pass. S: equal to C or better in an elective. U: equal to D or F in an elective. None count in GPA.
W: dropped with permission after course change. WF: dropped in an exceptional case while at F level (not used by Music). Neither counts in GPA.
Q: continued next term, before Fall 2002. NA or &&: not yet available. W-- or --: withdrew from the University, before Fall 2002.
S/U doesn't apply to Physical and Occupational Therapy. Medicine has its own UGME policies.

title: Unexcused Absences
points: Missing a final or required work gives you a J. Options: (1) a grade from your work so far, with 0 for the missing part, unless the outline says it's mandatory; (2) a deferred exam with reasons and documents; (3) a supplemental, if your faculty allows.
Ask for option 1 within four months of the exam period's end, and options 2 and 3 by the deadlines on McGill Exams. Appeal to your Associate Dean or Director.
No option 1 in Engineering, Law or Music. Law's option 3 needs approval. Graduate students have options 2 and 3, and appeal to associatedeans.gps@mcgill.ca.
Arts and Science requests go through Service Point, with an OASIS or SOUSA adviser.

title: Class Averages
points: Calculated on February 15 for Fall, June 15 for Winter and October 15 for Summer, per course, when there are 25 or more letter grades (not W, S, U, P).
Once on your transcripts they're fixed and later grade changes don't count. Medicine, Dentistry, Graduate Studies and Farm Management don't show them.

title: Transfer Credits
points: Credits from approved study or exchange count if your grade meets what the host requires to graduate, and the course has the same purpose as it would at McGill. Student Affairs decides the category.
Get approval first, and from your adviser too in some faculties. Courses not pre-approved may not transfer. Normally 60 credits must be at McGill, and you need Satisfactory Standing.
Host grades aren't on your transcript or in your GPA, but failed or withdrawn courses show with zero credit.
Outside Québec, you arrange for an official transcript and submit your papers within four months. Under the IUT, grades come automatically.

Transcript deadlines: April 1 to graduate in Winter (Spring convocation), August 15 for Summer (Fall convocation), December 15 for Fall (degree in February, Spring convocation). Late ones wait for the next period.

Arts and Science discourage study away in your last U3 term, because it delays graduation. B.Eng.: at most 50% transferred. B.Sc.(Arch.): 60 McGill credits needed. Law: at most six non-law and six non-McGill law credits, with approval.

title: Advanced Standing Transfer Credits
points: Declare IB, AP, A-Levels, French Baccalaureate and similar when applying, and credits or exemptions follow.
With Advanced Standing you can still do 120 McGill credits over four years, within limits on repeating exempted courses. Ask your Faculty or School advisers.

title: Incomplete Courses
points: An instructor may extend term work past the course's end with a K and a date. A grade in time replaces K on your official transcript, while unofficial ones show both. Missing it brings KF, counted as F. The Associate Dean or Director may give a further KE in exceptional cases.

Arts and Science limits: graduating in June, April 30; otherwise April 30 (Fall), July 30 (Winter and multi-term), November 30 (Summer). Agriculture: January 15 (Fall), and April 30 or May 15 (Winter and spanning). Instructors may set earlier dates, and work must be early enough to grade.
A KF can change your standing. Ask the instructor, and see an adviser.
Law: only the Director (Student Life and Learning) can grant the delay, and missing exams or work without excuse gives J.

title: Academic Standing
points: You start in Satisfactory Standing. After each term, your GPAs and faculty rules decide it, with codes generated in January, May and September and shown on transcripts.
Unsatisfactory Standing means you can't continue or register and must apply for readmission, which isn't guaranteed.

title: Academic Standing: Desautels Faculty of Management
points: See p. 905.

title: Academic Standing: Faculty of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences
points: See p. 88. Farm Management and Technology has its own Academic Rules.

title: Academic Standing: Faculties of Arts and Science (including B.A. & Sc.)
points: Based mainly on CGPA and sometimes TGPA, and it sets whether and how you continue.
Fall decisions are Interim, using grades available in January. They ignore deferred and spanned courses, and don't appear on official transcripts.

title: Satisfactory/Interim Satisfactory Standing: Arts, Science, and B.A. & Sc.
points: CGPA of 2.00 or more. You continue normally.

title: Interim Probationary/Probationary Standing: Arts, Science, and B.A. & Sc.
points: You continue with at most 14 credits a term, seeing your departmental and Faculty advisers. Interim students should do so before Winter withdrawal deadlines. On Probation, raise your CGPA to get back.

Probationary if your CGPA is 1.50–1.99 after being Satisfactory; or 1.50–1.99 with Fall or Winter TGPA of 2.50+ after Probationary or Interim Unsatisfactory; or still below 2.00 after meeting your readmission conditions.

title: Unsatisfactory Readmitted Standing: Arts, Science, and B.A. & Sc.
points: After being readmitted, you must meet your letter's conditions and carry at most 14 credits, or fewer if it says so. See your departmental and Faculty advisers.

title: Unsatisfactory/Interim Unsatisfactory Standing: Arts, Science, and B.A. & Sc.
points: Interim (Fall): you continue at 14 credits maximum and should see advisers before the deadlines.

Unsatisfactory: registration is cancelled. It applies if your CGPA falls or stays below 1.50; if your TGPA is under 2.50 and CGPA under 2.00 after Probationary, Readmitted or Interim Unsatisfactory; or if you missed your readmission conditions.
Appeal to your faculty by the deadline, with proof of extenuating circumstances. A second time means permanent withdrawal.
Supplementals are normally not allowed, but you can appeal for one. Appeals go to the Associate Dean (Student Affairs) of Arts or of Science.

title: Incomplete Standings: Arts, Science, and B.A. & Sc.
points: Your standing waits on deferred exams, Ks, Ls or supplementals. You can register for Fall, but it must be settled by the end of course change.

You continue if it becomes Satisfactory, Probationary or Interim Unsatisfactory. If Unsatisfactory, registration is cancelled unless readmitted: ask right away, with proof, through your Associate Dean (Arts or Science).

Winter standing is set in June if a K or L won't change it. Otherwise it waits. Requests go through Service Point, 3415 McTavish; B.A. students book with Arts OASIS, and B.Sc. and B.A. & Sc. students with SOUSA.

title: Academic Standing: Faculty of Education
points: See p. 688.

title: Academic Standing: Faculty of Engineering
points: Based on CGPA after each term, ignoring any deferred exam grades.

title: Satisfactory Standing: Faculty of Engineering
points: CGPA of 2.00 or more. D or F in a core course must be repeated with C or better, or replaced by an approved course. F elsewhere must be repeated or replaced before graduating.

title: Probationary Standing: Faculty of Engineering
points: CGPA from 1.20 to below 2.00, or TGPA of 2.50+ with CGPA under 2.00.

Take at most 13 credits, and end the term with CGPA 2.00+ or TGPA 2.50+, staying on Probation until your CGPA reaches 2.00. Otherwise you become Unsatisfactory. See an adviser before the withdrawal deadlines.

title: Unsatisfactory Standing: Faculty of Engineering
points: CGPA below 1.20, or TGPA under 2.50 with CGPA under 2.00.
Fall (Interim): continue at 13 credits at most, and end the term with CGPA 2.00+ or TGPA 2.50+. See an adviser before withdrawal deadlines.

Winter: you must leave the Faculty for at least one term. If you're readmitted and fall Unsatisfactory again, you can't continue, and must leave for a term or permanently according to your last readmission letter.

title: Academic Standing: Faculty of Law
points: A sessional GPA (Fall and Winter together) under 1.50 means withdrawing, unless the Admissions Committee allows otherwise for exceptional reasons.
From 1.50 to 1.99 you continue, but need a later sessional GPA of 2.50 or CGPA of 2.00. Graduating takes a 2.00 CGPA.

title: Academic Standing: School of Continuing Studies
points: In Unsatisfactory Standing, apply to your academic area's Appeals Committee.

title: Academic Standing: Schulich School of Music
points: See p. 1012.

title: myProgress
points: A degree audit tool that compares your record to your curriculum, shows what's left, and records approved exceptions such as a substituted course.
It's only an advising aid, and doesn't approve you to graduate. Open to selected faculties.

title: Student Record Changes
points: Covers adding, dropping or withdrawing from courses, withdrawing from McGill, changing programs, status changes such as leave, exchange or term away, and tuition status changes through legal documents.

title: Registrar Deadlines
points: Fall term – January 31
Winter term – June 1
Summer term – October 1

title: Before Registrar Deadlines
points: After normal deadlines but before Registrar Deadlines, write to your Associate Dean or Director explaining why you couldn't ask sooner.
Arts and Science requests go through Service Point, 3415 McTavish, with an OASIS or SOUSA adviser.

title: After Registrar Deadlines
points: Normally refused. Only unforeseeable, extraordinary personal or academic circumstances are considered, on request to your Associate Dean or Director. A fee may apply, and the faculty must document it for Enrolment Services (except grade changes).
Arts and Science requests go through Service Point, with an adviser.

title: Fee Assessment Consequences
points: The new charge shows on your next statement. To contest it, write to Enrolment Services, who review your faculty's documents with Student Accounts if needed and reply to you.

title: Student's Citizenship, Immigration, or Fee Exemption Status
points: Faculties don't handle these; see the legal documents section (p. 28). A fee may apply after the deadline.

title: Examinations: General Information
points: Exams follow the Exam Regulations and the Policy on Assessment of Student Learning, both on the Secretariat site. Check the Exams website and your faculty's own rules too.

title: Credit by Examination
points: Exceptionally, some faculties let you ask your Associate Dean or Director to take a final for credit without registering, only in courses assessed by the final alone.

title: Undergraduate Advising
points: There are faculty and degree advisers, departmental advisers, professors and peers. The types below show who to see.

title: Advising and the University Mission
points: Advising is part of McGill's educational mission and happens in many places. Your Faculty's site and the Academic Advising site explain where.

title: The Role of Student Advising
points: Seek advice actively. Advisers guide you, but meeting requirements and knowing the rules is ultimately on you.

title: University-Wide Regulations
points: Read the Regulations section (p. 20).

title: Faculty-Specific Regulations
points: McGill has 12 Faculties, and you belong to one. Your offer letter gives your Faculty, degree, program and credits to complete.

title: Your Academic Program
points: You're in a degree, usually with programs such as majors and minors. B.Eng. students normally follow one, and B.A. students more than one.

A typical degree is 120–140 credits over four years. CEGEP students usually get 30 credits of Advanced Standing, leaving 90–110 from U1. Others usually start in U0, the Foundation year. IB, French Baccalaureate, AP and transfers vary.
Requirements are in your faculty or department's section, even for a program in another faculty, such as a B.Com. with a minor in Arts.
Three credits is typically a one-term course. Departments may offer recommended streams or handbooks.
Conversations with advisers are confidential, and some matters need more than one to sign off.
Faculty advisers, in Student Affairs all year, know the degree rules, help with program choice, load and deadlines, exchanges and awards, and support you through difficulties.

Departmental advisers, available at set times, guide course selection for a major or minor, assess equivalencies and transfer credit, and usually confirm you've met requirements. Check in before your final year.
Professors can mentor you on trends, readings and research, and send you to advisers for signatures. Peer advisers are trained students with drop-in hours, in some units.

title: Related Resources
points: Campus Life and Engagement helps new students find their way. The Student Wellness Hub has counsellors, social workers and psychologists, with drop-ins and crisis help, and Local Wellness Advisors work across faculties.
CaPS helps with careers and jobs. Service Point, 3415 McTavish, handles official documents, records, fees and exchanges. At Macdonald, it's Laird Hall, Room 106.
The WELL Office serves Nursing, Physical and Occupational Therapy, and Communication Sciences students. Medical Learner Affairs serves UGME and PGME students.

title: Internships and Co-op Programs
points: Agriculture: Experiential Learning and Community Outreach. Arts: Arts Internships. Education: B.Ed. field experience through Internships and Student Affairs; Kinesiology through your KPE adviser.
Engineering: Internship Program (p. 745), plus co-ops in Mining and Materials. Law: International Human Rights Internships. Management: BCom Internships.
Science, plus Arts and B.A. & Sc. students majoring in Computer Science, Geography, Mathematics, Psychology, Environment or Software Engineering: Science Internship Program.

title: Exchange Programs
points: McGill Abroad covers exchanges, funding and pre-departure help.
Details: Arts OASIS; Engineering Student Affairs; Law's Exchange and Study-Away page; Management (p. 911); SOUSA for Science and B.A. & Sc.; Music's Learning Abroad page and Student Affairs.

refs.label: Desautels Faculty of Management: see the International Student Exchange Program page

title: Field Study Semesters
points: See the Field Study Semesters page.

title: Mobility Bursary for Exchanges
points: Helps pay for studying abroad within your degree. See McGill Abroad's Funding page.

title: Study Abroad Opportunities
points: See p. 1286 or McGill Abroad.

title: Overview
points: You must finish faculty and program requirements, be in Satisfactory Standing and have a CGPA of at least 2.00; some faculties ask more. See your adviser early in your last year.
After Senate approval, transcripts show "Degree Granted" and your record is final, with no more changes.

Fall: courses by end of December, apply by end of November, degree in February, Spring convocation. Winter: end of April, apply by end of February, degree in May, Spring convocation. Summer: end of August, apply by mid-May, degree in October, Fall convocation.

title: Minimum Residency Requirement
points: At least 60 McGill credits for an undergraduate degree, or for a second one. Some programs add limits, such as two-thirds of program requirements done at McGill. Check your faculty's section. Graduate programs have their own.

title: Apply to Graduate
points: Most undergraduates and non-thesis graduate students apply in Minerva (Student Records, Apply for Graduation) once registered for their final year. You must tell McGill you intend to graduate. Medicine and Dentistry students are flagged automatically.
Applying confirms that your curriculum is right and that you'll have finished by that term.

Unless you submit an Opposition Form by April 15 (Spring) or September 15 (Fall), your details are shared for the program and broadcast, regalia, photographer, your professional order, and a digital diploma through ARUCC's MyCreds™ / MesCertif™, whose terms apply if you use it. Opting out doesn't affect your degree.

title: Deadlines
points: Same dates as above. If you miss one, contact Student Affairs at once. Arts and Science students file a Graduation Term Change Request and see an adviser.
Continuing Studies certificates and diplomas don't need 60 credits. Graduate students follow the GPS Graduating page. Physical and Occupational Therapy students need a 2.30 CGPA.

title: Graduation Approval
points: Follow it in Minerva's Graduation Approval Query from early January (Fall), early April (Winter) or early September (Summer).
"Faculty Approved" comes first; "Degree Granted" follows Senate approval in late February, late May or late October.

title: Graduation Honours Dean's Honour List
points: 60+ McGill credits and in the top 10% of your faculty's graduating class by CGPA. Transfer students may lose it if their earlier CGPA isn't comparable.

title: Distinction
points: 60+ McGill credits and in the top 25% but not the top 10%, by CGPA. Same transfer condition. Not given by Education, Dentistry, Law, Medicine or Continuing Studies.

title: Faculty of Science Dean's Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research List
points: Recognizes B.Sc. and B.A. & Sc. students with broad research: 9+ credits of approved research courses for a letter grade, one of 3+ credits from another unit, all C or above, averaging 3.0 or above. It's noted on your transcript.
S grades in Winter 2020 to Winter 2021 count exceptionally toward the 9 credits, though not the average.

title: Application
points: Automatic if your courses are on the approved list. To count another research course, one with a project and substantive report, ask SOUSA at least four months before graduating (February 1 for June, July 1 for November, August 1 for February). Reading courses, BASC 396 and 449, and Arts courses don't qualify.

title: Honours and First-Class Honours for Faculties of Arts and Science (including B.A. & Sc.)
points: Your department recommends you if you meet its requirements: CGPA 3.00 for Honours, 3.50 for First-Class. Joint Honours students must qualify in both parts, and some departments ask more.
Below 3.00, see your adviser about graduating in another program.

title: Honours and First Class Honours for Faculty of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences
points: Same thresholds: 3.00 and 3.50 at graduation, all program requirements done, possibly more by program. Below that, ask your adviser about another program.

title: Outstanding Achievement for Schulich School of Music
points: Departments may recommend this for superior performance on an instrument or voice, or in an academic discipline.

title: Required Documents
points: Diplomas are given at convocation in May/June or October/November, and not before, as the parchment bears that date.

title: Replacing a lost diploma
points: Order and pay, including courier, in the ES Services eStore.

title: Requesting a diploma following your Convocation ceremony
points: Didn't attend? Order courier delivery on the eStore or book a pick-up with Service Point. Unclaimed diplomas are kept two years and then destroyed, after which you'd pay for a replacement.

title: Modifying the name on your diploma
points: First change your name with a Personal Data Change Form and documents (p. 30). Once it's confirmed, order and pay for a replacement on the eStore.

title: Certified Copies
points: Enrolment Services certifies copies and issues translations: into English from Latin, or into French from English or Latin.
From Spring 2026, parchments are in English for all degrees but the Executive MBA. Before that, English or Latin depending on the degree.

title: Submitting Your Request
points: All diploma requests go through the ES Services eStore.

title: Aegrotat Standing and Degree
points: A rare degree for students in Satisfactory Standing who've done 75%+ of requirements but can't finish because of a serious medical or similar situation.
Your Dean asks the Associate Provost (Student Life and Learning). It shows in the convocation program, not on the transcript.

title: Admission to Professional and Graduate Studies
points: Heading for Dentistry, Law or Medicine? Ask those faculties about prerequisites.

title: Language Requirements for Professions
points: Québec law requires French to enter a professional order. Show it by three years full-time in French post-primary school, by passing French mother tongue exams in Secondary 4 or 5, by finishing secondary school in Québec in 1986 or later, or by passing the OQLF exam.

Registered students within two years of such a degree can write the OQLF exam, held every three months with no limit on attempts, and priority to those closest to graduating. Enrolment Services has the form. OQLF: 125 Sherbrooke St. W.

Learn French at the French Language Centre or Continuing Studies (688 Sherbrooke St. W.), or keep it up in French Language and Literature. Some Continuing Studies language courses don't count toward your degree.

McGill degrees give access to orders for agrologists, architects, accountants (chartered, industrial administration, licensed general), chartered appraisers, chemists, dentists, dietitians, engineers, geologists, industrial relations counsellors, lawyers, nurse clinicians, occupational therapists, physicians, physiotherapists, psychologists, social workers, speech therapists and audiologists, urbanists, and vocational guidance counsellors.

title: Graduate Programs
points: Over 250 doctoral and master's programs in more than 85 fields. See mcgill.ca/gradapplicants and the catalogue's graduate section.

title: University and Facilities
points: University governance and student facilities.

title: University Government
points: McGill is a corporation under a Royal Charter, with the Crown's supervisory power exercised by the Governor General as Visitor.

The Board of Governors, the Royal Institution for the Advancement of Learning under Québec law, manages finances and appoints professors. Members: 12 elected by the Board, 3 by alumni, 2 by Senate, 2 by administrative and support staff, 2 by academic staff, 2 by students, plus the Chancellor and President ex officio.
The Chancellor presides over Convocation and joint meetings. The President and Vice-Chancellor is chief executive and chairs Senate.
Senate is the top academic authority, over admission, courses, discipline and degrees, and faculties carry out its rules.

title: The Visitor
points: Mary Simon, Governor General and Commander-in-Chief of Canada, as Administrator of the Government of Canada. The Board has 25 voting members as of July 1, 2024.

title: Student Governance
points: SSMU represents all 22,000+ downtown undergraduates, with six elected executives and a Legislative Council of 37 that meets every two weeks. It runs over 250 clubs and 19 services, plus events like Orientation Week, Activities Night and Faculty Olympics.
It has a five-floor building with lounge, cafeteria, bar and spaces for groups. Offices: 3600 McTavish, Suite 1200, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

MACES represents those whose records are run by Continuing Studies. Founded 1985, incorporated 1989, accredited 1990. It has a free computer lab, Microsoft courses and study and social spaces at 3437 Peel, with an elected board. Students in several programs may belong to several associations.

title: Facilities and Residences
points: Treat facilities with respect. Facilities Management and Ancillary Services has details.

title: Residential Facilities
points: Various housing types on both campuses.

title: Mission Statement
points: Residences aim to be a safe home and community, built on respect, sustainability, responsiveness, open communication, integrity, and honouring tradition.

title: University Residences: Downtown Campus
points: Move-in weekend: August 22–23, 2026.
Leases: August 20, 2026 to May 2, 2027 for first-years and exchange students; to June 30, 2027 for upper years and graduate students; Solin Hall, August 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.

title: First-Year Undergraduate Students
points: About 3,000 students, with 24-hour support, a Residence Council and wireless.
Traditional (meal plan, mostly single rooms with shared bathrooms): Gardner, McConnell, Molson, Douglas (quiet), Royal Victoria College (West Wing, women only), University Hall.
Hotel-style (meal plan, mostly doubles with en-suite): New Residence Hall, Carrefour Sherbrooke, La Citadelle. All You Care to Eat plan, plus oneCard Flex dollars.
Shared-facilities houses (quiet, singles, shared kitchens and laundry): 506/510/522 Pins Ave, 3653 and 3601 University.
Solin Hall (apartments with 2–4 bedrooms, no meal plan, oneCard dollars) is near Atwater Market and the Lachine Canal, four metro stops away.

title: Upper-Year Undergraduate Students
points: RVC Tower (meal plan) or Solin Hall. Also Greenbriar and Hutchison: studio and one-bedroom apartments, no meal plan, oneCard dollars.

title: Graduate Students
points: Solin Hall; studios and one-bedrooms at Greenbriar, Hutchison, 3643 University and Rexford Hall; and shared-facilities houses with singles and shared kitchens. No mandatory meal plan, but oneCard dollars.

title: Meal Plans
points: All You Care to Eat, with unlimited dine-in, is mandatory at Carrefour Sherbrooke, La Citadelle, Douglas, Gardner, Molson, McConnell, New Residence, Royal Victoria College and University Hall.

title: oneCard
points: Linked to your ID for campus purchases, and due at the end of September. Flex dollars: $500 in meal plan residences, $600 in other downtown residences, $400 at Macdonald.

title: Living in Residences
points: Residence Life Facilitators, who are students, run activities to build community and support personal development.

title: Contact Us
points: McGill Student Housing and Dining Service Centre, 3465 Durocher St. Requests go through the Service Desk portal.

title: Student Government
points: Each hall elects a Residence Council at the start of the year to gather opinions, manage money, run activities and help set community standards. Everyone pays a $30 activity fee.

title: Residence Fees
points: Options and prices are on the Student Housing site.

title: University Residences: Macdonald Campus
points: Laird Hall and Eco Residence, for undergraduate, graduate and FMT students. Downtown students are welcome if there's room.

title: Residence Options
points: Laird Hall: about 250 students, furnished rooms, shared kitchens and lounges.
Eco Residence: about 100, mainly upper-year and graduate students, furnished two- or six-bedroom split-level apartments.
Internet and laundry are included in both.

title: Residence Occupancy Period
points: August 20, 2026 to May 2, 2027. Staying outside that needs approval and maybe a fee, in exceptional cases like extended sessions, Summer courses, campus jobs or travel constraints.

title: Residence Fees
points: Billed separately but paid through your fee account. See the latest fee sheet.

title: Food Services
points: No mandatory plan, but new students are charged $400 in oneCard dollars at the start of the lease. Eat at Twigs Café, between Macdonald-Stewart and Barton Library, or use the shared kitchens.

title: Parking – Macdonald Campus
points: Permits for students and staff only, from Laird Hall, Room 101, paid in person. You can send the form ahead by email.

title: Macdonald Campus Residence Information
points: Residence Admissions Office: 21 111 Lakeshore, Room 107, Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue, P.O. Box 188. Requests go through the Service Desk portal.

title: Summer Accommodation
points: La Citadelle, 410 Sherbrooke W.: hotel-style, queen or two doubles, private bath, AC, Wi-Fi, 24-hour laundry and gym, shared kitchen (bring your own dishes).
Carrefour Sherbrooke, 475 Sherbrooke W.: hotel-style, one or two queens, private bath, AC, small fridge, daily housekeeping, gym, paid laundry.
Royal Victoria College, across from campus: private dorm rooms with twin bed, desk and small fridge, shared bath, kitchenettes and laundry.

title: Reservations for Summer Residences
points: Arriving before May 8 means at least a month's stay, paid in advance and non-refundable.
Cancel with the reservations office by noon ET on May 8 to avoid a one-night fee; telling another office doesn't count. Check availability before applying.

title: Proper Use of Computing Facilities
points: Follow the Policy on the Responsible Use of McGill IT Resources.

title: Smoking Policy
points: Québec law bans smoking in public buildings, and on campus it's allowed only in outdoor designated areas. This includes e-cigarettes and similar devices.

title: Policy Concerning Cannabis
points: Under the Policy Concerning Alcohol, Cannabis and Other Drugs, recreational cannabis is banned on all McGill property, including the Gault Nature Reserve and leased spaces. Medical use needs a valid certificate, under conditions.

title: Incorporated College
points: Royal Victoria College is a non-teaching, co-ed residential college.

title: Royal Victoria College
points: 3425 University St.

title: Affiliated Theological Colleges
points: Three colleges train for ministry and grant ordination certificates; they've handed degree-granting to McGill except for the M.Div. and honorary doctorates.

title: Montreal Diocesan Theological College
points: 3473 University St. Principal: Rev. Dr. Jesse Zink.

title: Presbyterian College of Montreal
points: 3495 University St. Principal: Rev. Dr. Roland de Vries.

title: United Theological College of Montreal
points: 3475 University St. Principal: Rev. Maylanne Maybee.

title: Libraries and Historical Collections
points: Over 10 million print and electronic items across several locations, including the Visual Arts Collection. Bring your ID to borrow; e-resources work anywhere with your McGill login.
The site gives you thousands of databases, subject guides, digitized collections and eScholarship@McGill for theses and faculty work. Liaison librarians teach and answer questions.
Quiet and bookable group spaces, wireless, computers, printing and scanning, and longer hours at exams.
Course Readings Service links to readings in myCourses. Return books anywhere. Network and Interlibrary Loan are free for the McGill community.

title: Workshops
points: Sessions and tours on using the library run through the year.

title: Historical Collections
points: Listed on the Historical Collections page.

title: McGill Writing Centre
points: McGill's central writing resource since 2010. Credit courses cover academic, creative, digital and business writing and communicating science, usable as electives or for language requirements in some degrees (some faculties need approval).
Also workshops, retreats and one-on-one consults.

title: McGill Writing Centre Course Information
points: Undergraduate course offerings can be found at mcgill.ca/mwc/ courses/undergraduate.
Graphos graduate course offerings can be found at mcgill.ca/graphos/ courses.
Continuing Education (non-credit) course offerings can be found at mcgill.ca/mwc/special-interest-courses.
Course Coordinator Information:
If you have inquiries about courses, please contact the specific course coordinator listed at mcgill.ca/mwc/contact-us.

title: McGill Writing Centre Tutorial Service
points: Help with writing and presentations at any stage, for all students.

title: McGill Writing Centre Contact Information
points: McLennan-Redpath Library, Main Floor, Room #02, 3459 McTavish St. Graphos has its own site and email.

title: Service Point
points: Ground floor of the McLennan Library Building. Handles certified or translated diplomas, degree verification, admissions and Minerva help, insurance cards and exemptions, ID cards, transcript pick-up, replacement diplomas, exchanges, legal documents and fees.
Arts and Science students can also ask about registration and deferred or supplemental exams.

points: Most services are in the Brown Student Services Building, Suite 4100, 3600 McTavish St.

points: Connects new and returning students to resources and opportunities. Suite 4100, Brown Building. First-years have their own email and getting-ready site.
