points: Confidential support for anyone affected by sexual or gender-based violence, in both languages.

title: Office of Sustainability
points: Based downtown, with monthly visits to Macdonald. Get involved or ask questions.

title: Continuing Studies
points: Continuing Studies students don't pay Student Services fees but can opt in if registered for at least 9 credits in a term.
That gives access to CaPS, the Wellness Hub, International Student Services, Off-Campus Housing, MORSL and Student Accessibility. You need a McGill ID. Apply at Brown Building, Room 4100.

title: McGill Athletics Package for Continuing Studies Students
points: Membership covers the B2 Gym and drop-in basketball, badminton, jogging and lap swim, with classes extra. Currie Gym, 475 Pine Ave. W.

title: Parking for Continuing Studies Students
points: Permits exist but space is limited. If you need to park close because of a disability, condition or injury, ask Student Accessibility.

title: University Centre for Continuing Studies Students
points: Food and drink in the evening at the University Centre, 3480 McTavish St.

title: McGill Writing Centre Tutorial Service
points: In-person or virtual writing tutoring at every stage. See the MACES Tutorial Service page.

title: IT Tools
points: See Resources for Students for what's available.

title: IT Support
points: One place for help with email, Microsoft 365, Wi-Fi and VPN: knowledge base, service requests, chat, system status and tickets.

title: Communication and Collaboration
points: Tools that work together for your studies.

title: Email
points: Every student gets a McGill address, usually firstname.lastname@mail.mcgill.ca. See p. 84.

title: MS Teams
points: Recommended for meetings, calls, messages and file sharing.

title: OneDrive
points: 1 TB of free cloud storage for documents.

title: Microsoft Office and 365 Apps
points: Install Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote and more on your own devices and sync with OneDrive, plus Forms, Sway, Stream and SharePoint. Not for those in short courses off the official transcript.

title: Online Course Materials and Lecture Recordings
points: myCourses has assignments, readings and syllabi. Many lectures are recorded for streaming, and Zoom is used when classes can't be on campus.

title: Minerva
points: McGill's information system, with your username or ID and PIN.

Use it to apply and check status, see schedules and spaces, register and change courses, change programs (some faculties), see your unofficial transcript and degree evaluations, your username, Permanent Code, status and fees, update your details and preferred name, evaluate courses, apply for exchange (some faculties), apply to graduate, order transcripts, get tax receipts, and get proof for a reduced-fare STM Opus card.

title: Secure Your Journey
points: Tips on strong passwords, 2FA, safe learning and phishing.

title: IT Policies
points: McGill's IT resources are subject to its policies, listed on the IT policies site.

title: Responsible Use of McGill Information Technology Resources
points: The policy is a code of conduct for McGill technology. M.D.,C.M. and D.M.D. students also have social media guidelines.

title: Report Security Incidents
points: Tell IT right away through the Service Desk or by phone. For bullying, harassment or safety risks, call Security Services: downtown 514-398-3000, Macdonald 514-398-7777.

title: Use of Cloud Services
points: The Cloud Directive governs online apps. Use approved ones; not all protect sensitive data.

title: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
points: All accounts use 2FA for many systems, as required of Canadian higher education institutions, so a stolen password isn't enough.

title: Email Communication
points: McGill email is the official channel, and you must check and act on it. Sign in on the Microsoft Office site, and confirm your address or set your password in Minerva's Personal Menu.
If you use another provider, see the IT Knowledge Base article. There's also a Policy on E-mail Communication with Students.

title: Downtown Campus Athletics and Recreation
points: Gym, fitness centre, varsity weight room, pool, fieldhouse, stadium, running tracks, tennis, squash, racquetball, spinning, fitness and martial arts studios, fields, training spaces, and gender-neutral changing rooms.

Join instructional, recreational, intramural and intercollegiate activities or sports clubs. Courses, intramurals, rentals and Fitness Centre have small fees. Skis, snowshoes, racquets and balls can be borrowed or rented. McGill Sports Complex, 475 Pine Ave. W.

title: Macdonald Campus Athletics and Recreation
points: Free gym, fitness centre, smart studios, multi-courts, fields, outdoor Trekfit gym and volleyball court, and green space. Intramurals and fitness courses cost a little, and equipment can be borrowed or rented. Offices: Stewart Athletic Complex.

title: Ombudsperson for Students
points: Confidential, independent, impartial help resolving disputes informally, with information, advice, intervention and referrals, before any formal process. 3610 McTavish St., Room 14.

title: Extra-Curricular and Co- Curricular Activities
points: Over 300 clubs and services: sports, charity and environment, outreach, arts and performance, health, languages and publications, hobbies, networking and leadership, activism, religion and culture.

title: Co-Curricular Activities
points: Learning outside class. Use myInvolvement, from CaPS, to find opportunities, and record them on your Co-Curricular Record.

title: University Centre, Thomson House, and Centennial Centre
points: University Centre, 3480 McTavish: clubrooms, dining, ballroom, lounges and black box theatre. Thomson House, 3650 McTavish: graduate students. Macdonald: Centennial Centre. Space varies by season and health guidelines.

title: Day Care
points: CPE McGill, 3491 Peel St.: independent, for 110 children aged four months to five years. Apply early at laplace0-5.com as places are limited.
Campus Day Care, 1 Maple Ave., Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue: independent, about 60 children of the same ages, with preference for the Macdonald community.

title: Downtown Campus
points: McGill Campus Store, 680 Sherbrooke St. W.: books, stationery, clothing and gifts, plus a 24/7 online store and newsletter.

title: Macdonald Campus
points: Centennial Centre, main floor: McGill and Macdonald clothing and insignia. Order online and pick up here.

title: About the Faculty of Agricultural and Environmental Sciences, including School of Human Nutrition
points: The Faculty and the School of Human Nutrition are on the Macdonald Campus: 650 hectares on the waterfront at the western tip of Montréal island, by public transport from downtown and the airport.

Degrees in agricultural sciences and applied biosciences, food and nutrition, environment, and bioresource engineering. Study abroad in places like Panama, Barbados or Africa, and internships are possible.

Labs, an experimental farm and the Morgan Arboretum. Known for plant and animal biotechnology, bioproducts, bioinformatics, food safety, environmental engineering, water, soils, parasitology, microbiology and ecosystem science. Small classes and hands-on learning.

title: Mission
points: Excellence in teaching, research and service, so that food, health and natural resource needs are met while protecting the environment.

refs.label: Department of Food Science and Agricultural Chemistry

title: Location
points: 21,111 Lakeshore Rd., Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue.

title: Faculty Admission Requirements and Application Procedure
points: See the Undergraduate Admissions Guide for requirements and Key Academic Dates for deadlines. Apply online through Undergraduate Admissions.
Student Affairs Office, Macdonald Campus. Find your adviser with the site's search tool. For transfers, see Faculty Transfers and Programs.

title: Faculty Information and Regulations
points: Advisers help, but correct course choice, requirements and deadlines are your responsibility. Misunderstanding a rule won't earn an exemption.

title: Minimum Credit Requirement
points: Your admission letter sets it. Usually 120 credits over four years, with up to 30 Advanced Standing for DCS, IB, French Baccalaureate, A-Levels or AP.
With a Québec DEC or equivalent: 90 credits, 113 for Bioresource Engineering, 115 for Dietetics, 122 for concurrent Food Science and Nutrition, plus any missing science.
From outside Québec with a high school diploma: start with the 30-credit Foundation Program. No credit for courses overlapping earlier work.
Transfers need 60 McGill credits, 72 for B.Eng.(Bioresource). B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) and Diploma in Environment students take at least two-thirds of their credits in the Faculty.

title: Minimum Grade Requirement
points: C or better in required, complementary and Foundation courses used for your program, and in prerequisites, unless the Chair agrees in writing.

title: Academic Advisors
points: Before registering, see your program's academic adviser, who normally stays with you throughout. A faculty adviser in Student Affairs helps with record matters.

title: Full-Time Students
points: Full-time is at least 12 credits a term, normally 15, at most 18. Scholarships need 27 graded credits in Fall and Winter. Probationary: at most 14, unless the Committee allows more.

title: Part-Time Students
points: Part-time students take fewer than 12 credits per term.

title: Academic Standing
points: CGPA (or first-term TGPA) under 2.00 means Probationary, at most 14 credits. Then you need a TGPA of 2.50 to stay there or a CGPA of 2.00 to return; otherwise Unsatisfactory (Interim in Fall, under Probationary rules).
CGPA under 1.50 means Unsatisfactory, and you must withdraw (Interim in Fall). You can apply for readmission after at least one term away, not counting Summer.
When readmitted, reach CGPA 2.00 for Satisfactory or TGPA 2.50 for Probationary, or you must leave permanently. Dietetics has further standards (p. 118).

refs.label: Students in the School of Human Nutrition have additional standards in place for the professional program (Dietetics). See Dietetics Major (B.Sc.(Nutr.Sc.)) (115 credits) (p. 118).

title: Committee on Academic Standing
points: Reviews special requests. Get the form at Student Affairs, Laird Hall 106.

title: Credit System
points: About three hours of work per credit each week, so nine hours for a 3-credit course.

title: School of Continuing Studies Courses
points: Not all count toward your degree. Ask a faculty adviser before registering.

title: Credit Transfer
points: Earlier courses are assessed after you accept your offer. Courses elsewhere while at McGill need permission first, and need a grade meeting the host's graduation standard. They don't count in GPA.
Exemptions need approval from the McGill instructor and your adviser. Full-time students may take courses at Québec universities through BCI with Student Affairs' approval, with at least a C.
Outside Québec, arrange an official transcript and submit everything within one month of finishing. IUT grades arrive automatically.

title: Adding a Second Major
points: Apply to the Associate Dean (Student Affairs), Laird Hall, Room 106, with CGPA 3.00+ and Satisfactory Standing, normally before finishing U1.
Propose all courses with each major's advisers. At least 36 credits must be unique to the second, approved by your adviser, Student Affairs and the other faculty. Each major's standards apply.

title: Procedures for a Minor Program
points: Submit a Minor Approval Form, usually early in U2, to Student Affairs. It continues yearly until cancelled: tell the minor adviser and file a Program Change Form.

title: Course Change and Withdrawal Guidelines
points: See p. 34 and Important Dates. Student Affairs handles other changes.

title: Graduate Courses Available to Undergraduates
points: You need a CGPA of 3.2 and approval from Enrolment Services. They can't also count toward a graduate program. See Laird Hall 106.

title: Attendance and Conduct in Class
points: The Dean handles teaching-related discipline. Professors may warn you about dishonest or improper conduct, and disciplinary cases go to the Associate Dean (Student Affairs). Be on time for everything.

title: Incomplete Grades
points: See p. 56.

title: Examinations
points: See p. 62. The tentative schedule is posted about four weeks into term and the final one at six. Write in English or French, except language courses; oral presentations are in English.

title: Reassessments and Rereads
points: See the page on the McGill Exams site.

title: Degree Requirements
points: C or better (or exemption) in all required and complementary courses, CGPA 2.00+, and all other requirements. Dietetics also needs the Stages with CGPA 3.00.
60 McGill credits, two-thirds in the Faculty for B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.). B.Eng.(Bioresource): 72 McGill credits, of 143 in the program including Year 0.

title: Graduation Honours
points: See Graduation Honours.

title: Scholarships, Bursaries, Prizes, and Medals
points: Open to entering, in-course and graduating students with no application. See the Faculty's in-course scholarships page.

title: Student Information
points: Staff can help with academics, residence, athletics, student life and health.

title: Student Rights and Responsibilities
points: Rules are published by the Dean of Students and the Secretariat.

points: Laird Hall, Room 106. Admissions, transfer credit, standing, exams, exchanges, transfers, program changes, registration, scholarships, second degrees and majors, minors, study away and graduation.

title: Student Services
points: See p. 81. Eligible students can use services on both campuses.

title: Macdonald Campus Residences
points: See p. 75, or the Student Housing site.

title: Student Life
points: Undergraduate and FMT students belong to the Macdonald Campus Students' Society, which runs events, academic affairs and clubs. Graduate students have MCGSS, part of PGSS.

title: Fees
points: Student Accounts has step-by-step help.

title: Tuition Fees
points: See your e-bill and account summary in Minerva, and p. 44.

title: Other Expenses
points: Budget at least $1,000, depending on your program, for textbooks and supplies. The Macdonald bookstore is open 10–5, Monday to Friday, with online orders for pickup. Food labs need uniforms; Nutrition students are told on acceptance or promotion.

title: Immunization for Dietetics Majors
points: Start and finish the Compulsory Immunization Program in Fall of U1, in Professional Practice Stage 1A. Bring your records to the health nurse. Later Stages require it complete, and updates may be needed.

title: Language Requirement for Professions
points: Québec orders, including those for agrologists, chemists, dietitians and engineers, require working French.

title: Overview of Programs Offered
points: Degrees: B.Eng.(Bioresource), B.Sc. in Agricultural and Environmental Sciences, Food Science, Nutritional Sciences, and concurrent Food Science and Nutrition.

Also: Certificates in Ecological Agriculture and Food Science, Diploma in Environment, DCS in Farm Management and Technology, and M.Sc. and Ph.D. programs. Partner in the Bieler School of Environment.

Accreditation: Agricultural Economics and Sustainable Agricultural Systems (Ordre des agronomes and provincial institutes); Bioresource Engineering (professional engineer in any province and the Ordre des agronomes); Dietetics (Dietitians of Canada and ODNQ); Food Science (IFT and Ordre des chimistes). Dietetics practice takes place in teaching hospitals and other agencies.

title: Bachelor of Science (Agricultural and Environmental Sciences) - B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.)
points: Pick one major and at least one specialization, or two for interdisciplinary interests, and optionally a minor. Environment majors pick a concentration, and Agricultural Economics specializations are for its own students.
Each specialization needs 18 credits that aren't shared with the major or the other, and 12 at the 400 level or higher. Honours versions are open after U2 if you qualify.

points: Interdepartmental programs in the B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) and B.Eng.(Bioresource), for training in an interdisciplinary subject and managing natural resources.

points: Hands-on work placements tailored by your employer and instructor.

title: FAES 200 / FAES 300 Internship Program
points: Full-time undergraduates with CGPA 2.7+: at least 10 weeks at 35 hours a week, related to your field. FAES 200 is pass/fail with no credit; FAES 300 is 3 credits, graded.

title: AGRI 310 Internship in Agriculture/ Environment
points: 3 credits, at least 12 weeks, in a business in your field, to understand its technical, economic and social challenges.

points: At least 420 hours, part of the Professional Agrology Specialization and required training for the Ordre des agronomes. Placements need the instructor's approval.

points: Supervised practical work on agriculture and international development: abroad, with an agency, or on research. Placements need the instructor's approval.

title: Graduate Programs in Agricultural and Environmental Sciences
points: M.Sc., M.Sc. Applied and Ph.D. through Animal Science, Bioresource Engineering, Food Science, Human Nutrition, Natural Resource Sciences, Parasitology and Plant Science. Graduate office: Macdonald-Stewart Building.

title: Browse Academic Units and Programs
points: Degrees: B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.), B.Sc.(F.Sc.), B.Sc.(Nutr.Sc.), B.Eng.(Bioresource) and the concurrent B.Sc. Also post-baccalaureate certificates in Food Science and Ecological Agriculture, and a Diploma in Environment. Bieler offers further programs (p. 821).

DCS, AP, A-Levels, IB, French Baccalaureate, placement exams and other studies can bring exemptions or credits; ask Student Affairs.

title: About the Department of Animal Science
points: For interests from livestock nutrition, breeding, reproduction and welfare to animal health and biotechnology models of human disease.
Offers Animal Biology and Health, Livestock, and Global Food Security specializations, taken within a major.
To become a professional agrologist, take the Sustainable Agricultural Systems Major with Livestock and 9 credits in Professional Agrology.

title: Location
points: Macdonald-Stewart Building, Room MS1-084.

title: Program Description
points: Basic biology of large mammals and birds, giving a background in biomedical studies and animal models. Prepares you for most North American veterinary colleges, graduate biology and lab work.
Not open to B.Sc.(Ag.Env.Sc.) students, who can take the specialization instead.

title: Program Description
points: Livestock production essentials: reproduction, breeding and genomics, nutrition, welfare, farm experience and precision agriculture, in a global context.
Pairs with the Sustainable Agricultural Systems Major, and Professional Agrology content can lead to Ordre des agronomes eligibility.

title: About the Department of Bioresource Engineering
points: Engineering applied to plants, animals and ecosystems: sustainable food and biomaterial production, and protecting soil, water and other resources. An accredited B.Eng. run with the Faculty of Engineering, focused on the circular bioeconomy.

title: About Programs in Bioresource Engineering
points: Accredited by the Canadian Engineering Accreditation Board, leading to professional engineer status in any province. The Professional Agrology version also qualifies you for the Ordre des agronomes.

Three non-restrictive streams: Bio-Environmental (soil and water, waste, ecology, climate), Bio-Production (machines, instrumentation, geospatial data, precision agriculture), Bio-Process (food, fibre, fuel and biochemical products). An Honours program and minors are also available.

Mostly on the Macdonald Campus, with one term downtown. Minors include Agribusiness Entrepreneurship, Agricultural Production, Biomedical Engineering, Biotechnology, Computer Science, Construction Management, Environmental Engineering, Field Studies and Technological Entrepreneurship.

C minimum in required and complementary courses. 143 credits include 30 from U0, with at least 50% at McGill. Required courses must be at McGill, with rare exceptions, and the capstone BREE 490/495 must be done in the Department.

title: Location
points: Macdonald-Stewart Building, Room MS1-028.

title: Program Description
points: Engineering for biological, agricultural, food and environmental systems, including bio-based products, with a research focus. Graduates can register as engineers in any province and some other countries.

title: Set C - Social Sciences
points: Plus 6 credits of social sciences, management, humanities or law at U1 or higher with adviser approval, which may include one 3-credit course in a language you don't normally speak. ENVR courses have limited enrolment.

title: Set D - Engineering
points: Up to 6 of these may come from other Engineering courses with adviser approval.

title: Program Description
points: Engineering for biological, agricultural, food and environmental systems, including bio-based products, with a research focus. Graduates can register as engineers in any province and some other countries.

title: Program Description
points: The engineering degree above, with registration as an engineer plus eligibility for the Ordre des agronomes and similar bodies in other provinces.

title: Set D - Engineering
points: At least 6 from each group. With approval, 6 may come from other Engineering courses.

title: About the Farm Management and Technology Program
points: A three-year college program in commercial agriculture at Macdonald: soil, plants, animals, engineering and management, with internships.

title: Academic Rules and Information
points: McGill's rules and Québec's Ministry rules for the college level both apply.

title: Entrance Requirements
points: Practical farming knowledge for eastern Canada: a year's experience recommended, or a four-month summer in special cases.
Québec: SSD plus Secondary IV History, Science and Technology, Mathematics, and Secondary V Language of Instruction and Second Language.

Ontario: OSSD plus grade 10 French, science SNC2P or SNC2D (with a tech course), and math MFM2P or MPM2D. Other Canadians need grade 10 second-language French. International students may need French and English tests.
Everyone comes for an interview. Fall admission only. Get car and farm equipment licences first, for safety and because employers require them.

title: Sessional Dates
points: Set by the Ministry, currently 75 teaching days and seven exam days per semester.

title: Last Day for Withdrawal or Course Additions
points: The last day to make course registration changes for Fall term courses is September 20.
The last day to make course registration changes for Winter term courses is February 15.

title: Registration
points: Register in Minerva each semester. Courses normally won't run with fewer than five students.

title: Academic Standing
points: First semester: failing half or more courses, or averaging below 60%, means withdrawing for at least a semester, then applying in writing to the Director.
Later: a cumulative or semester average under 60%, or failing half or more, means probation, possibly limited to 10 credits with course approval by the Associate Director.
Two probationary semesters in a row means withdrawing, with readmission possible after 6 to 12 months, on probation.

title: Student Rights and Responsibilities
points: See the Secretariat's Policies and Regulations site.

title: Institutional Policy on the Evaluation of Student Achievement
points: Explains how learning is evaluated, who's responsible for what, and how standards are accounted for. Copies are in the Library.

title: Fees
points: No tuition for eligible Québec residents, thanks to the provincial agriculture ministry. Full-time out-of-province and international students pay tuition, and part-time (under 8 credits) pays half. Everyone pays student fees. Rates are on Student Accounts.

title: Textbooks and Supplies
points: The cost of textbooks and supplies is estimated at $250 per semester.

title: Financial Assistance
points: Need-based loans and bursaries for full-time students, after applying for maximum government aid. Apply in Minerva and meet a counsellor at Student Services, Macdonald.

title: Residence Accommodation
points: Laird Hall: co-ed, 250 students, double and single rooms, with shared washrooms, kitchen, lounge and laundry on each floor.

title: Location
points: Harrison House, 21,111 Lakeshore Rd.

title: Program Description
points: Three years, funded by the provincial agriculture ministry, aiming for professional competence, mobility and lifelong learning.

title: Program Overview
points: Six terms on campus. Year 1's first summer is a 13-week internship on another farm or agricultural business, prepared through two Stage courses. Year 2's summer is Enterprise Management 1, collecting data for later courses.
English, Français, Humanities, Physical Education and two complementaries lead to the DEC.

title: Fall 2
points: Two from the elective production list.

title: Winter 2
points: Two from the elective production list.

title: Elective Production Courses
points: Four animal and four plant science courses. Take at least two from each, four in all, and at least two a semester. More is possible with your adviser.

title: Complementary Courses
points: Take two. With your adviser, you can substitute courses from another college at your own cost, including science courses for further study.

title: Comprehensive Assessment
points: Mandatory for the DEC; pass at 60%. It's noted on your transcript.

title: English Exit Examination
points: Required for the DEC, set by the Ministry on its dates.

title: About the Department of Food Science
points: Chemistry, physics, biology, engineering and microbiology applied to food quality and safety, covering analytical chemistry, risk assessment, product development, packaging, processing, flavour and sensory science.

Accredited by the Institute of Food Technologists and recognized by CIFST. Offers the B.Sc. (Food Chemistry or Food Science option), a concurrent B.Sc. with Nutritional Sciences, and a post-baccalaureate Certificate.

title: Concurrent Bachelor of Science in Food Science - B.Sc.(F.Sc.) and Bachelor of Science in Nutritional Sciences - B.Sc.(Nutr.Sc.)
points: Two degrees together, unique in North America. Food Science covers chemistry, safety, processing and packaging, and Nutritional Science covers metabolism and nutrition, with an industry placement.

refs.label: Food Science - Food Science Option Honours (B.Sc.(F.Sc.))

points: Macdonald-Stewart Building, Room MS1-033.

points: Food processing, chemistry, quality assurance, analysis, products and regulations, for scientist roles in industry or government.
Qualifies you for CIFST, and possibly IFT and the Ordre des chimistes. Reaches 90 credits with free electives. See Minimum Credit Requirements for prerequisites.

title: Degree Requirements — B.Sc.
points: To graduate, you need both the program's courses and the degree's requirements, including Foundation and structure (p. 1106). Fitting them together is your responsibility, and SOUSA's Degree Planning Guide helps.

points: Without a CEGEP organic chemistry course, FDSC 230 must be taken in its place.

points: Qualifies you for IFT and Ordre des chimistes recognition.

title: Electives (6 credits)
points: Choose with an adviser to reach 90 credits, partly in humanities or social sciences.

title: Program Description
points: Combines both fields to develop healthy foods, integrating both degrees' requirements and professional or industry training.

Honours: 12 extra credits beyond major and specialization. Apply in March or April of U3 with a CGPA of 3.3, once a professor agrees to supervise. Earn B or higher in Honours courses and a 3.3 CGPA at graduation. Your Program Director, supervisor and you sign a description of the research.

points: Choose with an adviser.

title: Definitions
points: Units: departments or equivalents. Programs: lists of required and complementary courses. Major Concentration: typically 36 credits. Minor Concentration: typically 18.

title: Foundation Program (Overview)
points: With 0–23 credits of Advanced Standing (97+ to go), you start in the Foundation Year before choosing a program, selecting an option in Minerva.

title: Regulations
points: Core courses need C or better, and U0 can't use S/U. Advanced Standing may count. With 96 or fewer credits to go, choose your programs when you register.

title: Multi-Track Requirement
points: Usually two components in different subjects: Major + Minor, Major + Major, Honours + Minor, or Joint Honours + Joint Honours. A Faculty Program is exempt.

title: Regulations
points: At least one component must come from an Arts unit. A Major or Honours from outside Arts must pair with an Arts Major or Minor. A Joint Honours component from outside pairs with an Arts one, or with another outside one plus an Arts Minor.

title: Honours Program Requirements
points: More focused than a Major, typically 48–60 credits with special courses, preparing you for graduate study.

title: Regulations
points: Needs GPA and CGPA of 3.00 in the previous year to stay in, unless the department and Associate Dean allow otherwise. Finish with CGPA 3.00 and program GPA 3.00, or higher if the unit says.
You also need a Minor in another subject, except in Honours Faculty Programs and the Spécialisation enrichie Langue et littérature françaises.

title: Joint Honours Program Requirements
points: Two subjects at a high level, each usually 36 credits (30–48), with high marks in program and elective courses.

title: Regulations
points: Same 3.00 rules for staying in and finishing, with the program GPA met in both components. It satisfies Multi-Track if one is from Arts, with no Minor needed.

title: Faculty Program Requirements
points: Interdisciplinary concentrations of usually 54+ credits, exempt from Multi-Track: Environment, and Population and Global Health (from 2026–2027).

title: Other Options: Science Minor Programs and Out-of-Faculty Programs
points: You can add an approved Science Minor with its prerequisites. For programs in other faculties, see OASIS and p. 155.

title: French as a Second Language (FRSL)

title: Substantive Content Courses Taught in French
points: Subject courses taught in French count when they are; POLI 226 alternates between languages.

title: Degree Requirements — B.A. students
points: Faculty and program requirements on p. 151; see an OASIS adviser for planning.

title: Core Requirement (18 credits)
points: 6 credits in each of three of the four categories, from lists of courses approved for U0.

title: Approved Courses - Social Sciences
points: See OASIS. Some, like CANS 200 and ISLA 210, also count as humanities.

title: Approved Courses - Humanities
points: See OASIS. Some need university prerequisites and don't suit a first term, and some count in other categories.

title: Approved Courses - Languages
points: See OASIS. D1 needs its D2 too. Take at most one language at introductory level; with prior knowledge, take higher levels with permission.

title: Approved Courses - Mathematics and Sciences
points: See OASIS. Check prerequisites. GEOG 205 is also a social science.

title: Course Requirements
points: C or better in program courses. If you fall short in a required course, pass the supplemental or repeat it, normally once. See OASIS before a third attempt.
A failed complementary can be replaced. A D then still counts as an elective. Repeating a required D course gives credit only once.

title: Course Prerequisites
points: Arts won't block you, but ask the instructor if you lack one. Other faculties may block you.

title: Course Overlap
points: No extra credit for courses overlapping earlier credit from McGill, CEGEP, another university, AP, A-Levels, IB or French Baccalaureate. Check with OASIS, SOUSA or the department.
Double-prefix courses: take your own department's version if offered together, otherwise whichever fits. Computer course credit follows each course's own rules.

Science and B.A. & Sc. students need the Associate Dean's permission for statistics from other faculties (except B.Sc. Environment's required ones), and for outside computer courses, only exceptionally.

Only one introductory statistics course counts, and only one intermediate. Credit for PSYC 204, MATH 324 or MATH 357 rules out the lower ones listed. PSYC 305 can go with ECON 227 or 257. For other 500-level statistics, check with an adviser.

title: Credit Limit for Courses Outside the Faculties of Arts or Science — For Arts Students
points: Maximum 12 credits outside Arts and Science over your degree, or 30 in designated programs, 39 if you combine them.

Designated: minors in Education for Arts Students, Educational Psychology, Entrepreneurship and Management for Non-Management Students, Field Studies, Geography Urban Studies, and music subjects; Geography Urban Studies major and honours; Environment honours and Faculty Program; Population and Global Health; Joint Honours in Economics with Accounting or Finance, who can't take Desautels minors.

Continuing Studies courses starting with C don't count. Courses listed in Arts or Science sections, and approved Field Study courses, count as Arts or Science. Limits are strictly enforced, with excess courses flagged as no credit after add/drop.
A minor from another faculty that isn't on the approved list needs Faculty permission, which isn't guaranteed.

title: Inter-University Transfer Credit Policy for Courses Taken Outside the Faculties of Arts and of Science
points: From a faculty outside Arts and Science elsewhere: up to 30 credits, C or better only (no C-, P or S). The original faculty decides how it's classed. Continuing Education courses count only if they led to a degree.
At McGill you can take more outside courses only if you transferred under 12 credits, up to 12. Programs requiring more are capped at 39 in all.

title: Interfaculty Transfer Credit Policy for Courses Taken Outside the Faculties of Arts and of Science
points: Moving to the B.A.: all Arts and Science credit, plus up to 30 outside credits with D or better, with grades remaining in GPA. Same 12 and 39 limits.

title: Definition of Online Courses for Transfer Credit
points: A course is online if more than 20% is delivered online.

title: Credit Limit for Online Courses
points: At most 6 credits through Independent Study Away, as electives, from an accredited degree-granting institution, counting toward its degrees, with Arts OASIS's prior approval. They count toward your term maximum.

title: Exceptions

Science decides for CHEM, COMP, ENVR, GEOG, MATH, PHYS and PSYC; Desautels for BUSA, INSY, FINE, MGCR, MGPO, MGSC, MRKT and ORGB.

points: Offered for credit; see the Arts Internship Program.

title: About the School of Religious Studies
points: World religions and their roles across history and today, embedded in culture, politics, aesthetics and social change, using many methods.

Affiliated with Montreal Diocesan Theological College, Presbyterian College and United Church Studies. In the Birks Building (1931, formerly Divinity Hall), 3520 University St., with a chapel and reading room.

title: History of the School
points: Theological colleges affiliated with McGill in the 19th century and formed a Joint Board in 1912. The Faculty of Divinity came in 1948, renamed Religious Studies in 1970, and it became a School within Arts in 2016.

title: Religious Studies Programs
points: B.A. in Religious Studies, Bachelor of Theology, Master of Divinity. Contact an adviser.

title: Birks Lectures
points: An annual series since 1950, funded by William M. Birks, given by distinguished visitors in late September or early October. Past lecturers include Huston Smith, Northrop Frye, Gregory Baum and Talal Asad.

title: Numata Visiting Professor in Buddhist Studies
points: A 20-year Numata Foundation grant brings a visiting Buddhist Studies scholar each year to teach a 500-level course, give a public lecture and consult. First in 1999–2000: Dr. Mahinda Deegalle.

title: Bachelor of Arts (B.A.)
points: Flexible study of Eastern and Western religions and comparison, across politics, philosophy, gender, colonialism and conflict. Major, minor, honours and joint honours.
Leads to law, development, human rights, policy, education, medicine, social work, and the religious sector, including faith-based NGOs, health care, chaplaincy and schools.
Possible minors: International Development, Indigenous, African, Jewish, Anthropology. Joint options: Philosophy, East Asian, Islamic, Political Science.

title: Bachelor of Theology
points: Theology, Biblical Studies and Church History, more intensive on Christianity than the B.A. Take it as a first degree (90 or 120 credits) or second (60), mainly for those preparing for ordination.
Independent or with one of three affiliated colleges in the Montreal School of Theology. Ministry candidates normally take it within the M.Div.

points: See Student Accounts, and affiliated colleges for their fees.

points: 120 credits: high school from outside Québec, or mature student; up to 60 transfer. 90 credits: DCS with Cote R 24 or equivalent; up to 30 transfer. 60 credits: a bachelor's with CGPA 2.7; no transfer.

McGill students in Good Standing with 30 credits may transfer in. Minors are possible in the 90 and 120 routes. Three years full-time with a DCS, two with a degree, otherwise four. Normal load: 15 credits a term.

title: Mature Students Admissions Policy
points: For those with no conventional basis or credentials too low, and no qualifying studies in the last five years. Canadian citizen or PR, 23+ at registration (21 for Management and Music).
Two reference letters, a letter of intent, employment and personal history, and recent courses within three years, including two relevant ones with B or better. Assessed individually.

points: Online, about 20 minutes, with a credit card for the fee.

title: Required Documents

Upload in Minerva after applying. Applying to a college means sending it a full set too. Files aren't reviewed until complete.

title: Application Deadlines
points: Fall: January 15. Winter: November 1. All documents must arrive before then.

title: Admissions Review Procedure
points: Write to the Chair of the B.Th. Admissions and Awards Committee within two weeks of refusal, with a $40 certified cheque or money order and new or corrected information. The decision stands unless standards were misapplied or your record misread. Special, Visiting and Exchange decisions are final.

points: Through Minerva.

points: Withdraw from all courses in Minerva, contact the Chair, and complete the form.

Registered candidates may get bursaries. Some colleges require a biblical language, usually Greek. With a Religious Studies B.A. and CGPA 3.3, you may apply for the S.T.M. after the In-Ministry Year.
Montreal School of Theology and Diocesan College: 3475 University St. Presbyterian College: 3495 University St.

title: About Biology
points: Life from molecules to ecosystems: evolution, environment, development, cells, inheritance, disease and the nervous system, applied in agriculture, medicine, biotechnology and conservation.

Liberal, Major, joint majors with Computer Science and Mathematics, Honours, Joint Honours with Computer Science, Minor, Science for Arts, Quantitative Biology options, and B.A. & Sc. concentrations (p. 453).
Leads to jobs and professional schools in medicine, veterinary, dentistry, agriculture, nursing, education and library science, or to research.

Stewart Biology, Bellini and Duff buildings, with links to Redpath Museum, MUHC, the Neuro, the Sheldon Biotechnology Institute and the Smithsonian in Panama. Field courses at Gault Nature Reserve, Barbados, Panama and East Africa. U2 and U3 students can do research for credit. MBSU represents students.

Builds skills in at least one language, for business, government, media and cultural careers. Graduate programs in German, Hispanic, Italian and Russian. For grad school, take honours or joint honours; B.A. & Sc. students can't take honours.

title: Bachelor of Arts (B.A.)

Leads to law, development, human rights, policy, education, medicine, social work, and the religious sector, including faith-based NGOs, health care, chaplaincy and schools.
Possible minors: International Development, Indigenous, African, Jewish, Anthropology. Joint options: Philosophy, East Asian, Islamic, Political Science.

title: Language Policy
points: Instruction is in English, but most Québec clinical placements need English and French, so build skills early.
Dentistry: working knowledge of both. Dietetics: both, with French proof for admission.
Medicine: English in Montréal, French at Campus Outaouais; working French from the start, with no alternative placements. You may be assigned a year-long clerkship in Gatineau or rural sites.

Nursing: written work in either language, French proficiency required for B.Sc.(N.) and Qualifying Year. Physical and Occupational Therapy: both needed; without French, fewer placements and possibly delayed graduation.

title: Proof of Proficiency in English
points: Not needed if English is your first language, you did Secondary V and a DCS in Québec, or studied five+ years in English.
Otherwise: TOEFL 90 iBT or 577 paper (varies), McGill Certificate of Proficiency, IELTS 6.5, MELAB 85%, or APIEL 4.

title: Proof of Proficiency in French
points: Clinical work requires French to learn safely and support patients. Essential for several Nursing degrees.
Physical and Occupational Therapy: all sites need both languages under the Charter of the French Language, so reach an appropriate level before placements.

title: Vaccination/Immunization Requirements for Health Sciences Programs
points: Compulsory: begin once accepted, finish well before patient contact, with proof signed by a nurse or physician. No exceptions; otherwise you're asked to withdraw. Influenza and others may be required.
D.M.D., General Practice Residency and Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery applicants are tested for Hepatitis B. A positive "e" antigen or viral DNA result withdraws the offer.

Students seropositive for Hepatitis B, C, HIV or other blood-borne pathogens must tell the Dean or Director, and follow the provincial service's recommendations, which may restrict procedures and could mean withdrawing. Those who know they carry such pathogens should weigh this carefully.
With a contagious disease that risks patients, tell your supervisor; you may have to pause clinical work.

Medicine and Dentistry have further UGME policies, and Nursing its own list. Physical and Occupational Therapy need complete records and a mask fitting before the first clinical course, with a card submitted by the third clinical seminar.

points: For graduates of non-CDAC-accredited programs: enter second year and get a D.M.D. in three years, starting in August, with places varying yearly.
To be licensed without it, use the NDEB Equivalency Process, three assessments before written and OSCE exams. For Québec, consult the Ordre des dentistes.

title: Admission Requirements
points: A graduate of a non-accredited program, and a Québec resident, Canadian citizen or PR. ADAT between March 1, 2025 and March 10, 2026 (2023–24 also accepted). CASPer. TOEFL 90 or IELTS 6.5 if needed.

French at B2 before the deadline, or B1 plus enrolment in B2 courses completed before Year 3; otherwise studies halt. Black and Indigenous pathway exemptions don't apply. Immunization required. Apply by March 1.

points: You can't be in another program at once. Apply when nearly finished: thesis submitted by July 31, confirmed by November 15; doctoral students show a successful defence by July 31, or the offer is withdrawn.

title: Transfer Students
points: Transfers aren't accepted.

title: Licensure by the Order of Dentists
points: A degree alone doesn't let you practise. Follow local dental laws, and register with the licensing body when you begin.

title: National Dental Examining Board of Canada
points: Canadian graduates need an NDEB certificate, normally by exam in final year. 80 Elgin St., 2nd Floor, Ottawa.

title: Province of Quebec
points: An NDEB certificate plus the French requirement (p. 70). Ordre des Dentistes: 800 René-Lévesque Blvd. W., Suite 1640.

title: Dental Regulatory Authorities in Other Provinces
points: Contact these bodies about each province's rules.

points: Alberta Dental Association, 8230 105th St., Suite 101, Edmonton.

title: British Columbia
points: College of Dental Surgeons of BC, 1765 West 8th Ave., Suite 500, Vancouver.

title: Manitoba
points: Manitoba Dental Association, 1735 Corydon Ave., Suite 202, Winnipeg.

title: New Brunswick
points: New Brunswick Dental Society, 570 Queen St., Suite 504, Fredericton.

title: Newfoundland and Labrador
points: Newfoundland and Labrador Dental Board, 49–55 Elizabeth Ave., Suite 204, St. John's.

title: Nova Scotia
points: Provincial Dental Board of Nova Scotia, 210 Waterfront Dr., Suite 103, Bedford.

points: Dental Association of PEI, 184 Belvedere Ave., Charlottetown.

points: College of Dental Surgeons of Saskatchewan, 201 First Ave. S., Unit 1202, Saskatoon.

title: National Board of Dental Examiners (U.S.)
points: American Dental Association, 211 East Chicago Ave., Chicago, and the state's licensing board.

title: Basic Cardiac Life Support
points: By July 31 of your entry year, show CPR level C or C+ and AED training, kept valid throughout, from Heart and Stroke, Red Cross, St. John Ambulance or the American Heart Association. Upload to your checklist.

title: Compulsory Immunization Program
points: Submit the form by July 31 of your entry year through the Wellness Hub portal; you consent to the Admissions Office sharing your health details for verification. You may need a meeting.

title: Instruments
points: Everyone buys a complete McGill Instrument Kit (p. 947).

title: New Students
points: Register in Minerva by August 14 and check your transcript. Orientation week is mandatory, or your application may be cancelled. Details come in June.

title: Returning Students
points: You get a list of Fall, Winter and Summer courses to register for in Minerva.

title: Scholarships, Awards, and Financial Aid
points: Available to the Faculty's students.

refs.label: Financial Aid for the Faculty of Dentistry

title: Dental Officer Training Plan
points: The Canadian Forces pays tuition, instruments, supplies and books with a second lieutenant's rank and salary, in return for short service after graduating, with summer officer training. Meet Forces standards and be accepted into a professional year. 1420 Sainte-Catherine St. W.

title: Entrance Scholarships for the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Medicine
points: A few each year, on merit, usually with no application. See the Financial Aid site.

title: McCall MacBain Scholarships
points: A full scholarship and enrichment program for professional or master's study at McGill.

title: Dr. Yu-Ming Lam Scholarship
points: Since 1999, for high achievers entering the four-year program. Renewable with standing.

title: ###### Ping Kwan Lau Scholarship
points: Since 1998, for high achievers entering the program, preferring international students. Renewable.

title: Phyllis Butterworth Major Entrance Scholarship
points: For high achievers, preferring students from the UK. Renewable.

title: Dr. Harry Rosen Entrance Scholarship in Dentistry
points: Since 2004, for an outstanding student entering the program. Renewable.

title: Dr. Leo Paul Ramsay Major Entrance Scholarship
points: Since 2023, for academic excellence at entry, preferring Québec students with community leadership.

title: Award for Indigenous Undergraduate Students
points: OKÒN:RA Award for full-time Indigenous students in any undergraduate degree, including D.M.D. Application needed.

title: Financial Aid for the Faculty of Dentistry
points: Start with government aid, and accept the maximum, plus a professional line of credit. Then apply in Minerva and meet a counsellor for low-interest loans and limited bursaries. Suite 3200, Brown Building.

title: In-Course Scholarships for the Faculty of Dental Medicine and Oral Health Sciences
points: For high-standing full-time students. Advanced Standing students must meet each prize's exact criteria.

points: Since 2001, for common sense, compassion and excellence in restorative dentistry, preferring those entering fourth year.

points: Since 2002, for academic achievement after at least one year, preferring students from BC.

points: Since 2001, for commitment to ethical practice, preferring those entering third or fourth year.

title: Dr. Howard S. Katz Scholarship in Dentistry
points: Since 2001, for academic achievement after at least one year.

title: Dr. William Boroff Scholarship in Dentistry
points: Since 2004, for character, perseverance and sportsmanship, preferring those entering fourth year.

title: Dr. Harry Rosen Scholarship in Dentistry
points: Since 2004, for high standing after at least one year, preferring those entering fourth year.

title: Carol David Scholarship
points: Since 2019, for high standing and pre-clinical skills after two years. Renewable.

title: Rena and Mervyn Gornitsky Scholarship in Dentistry
points: Since 2005, for performance and initiative in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, preferring those entering fourth year.

title: Dr. Robert Axelrad Award
points: Since 2022, for one or two students showing warmth and empathy with patients.

title: Dr. Stanley S. Blum Award
points: Since 2023, at the White Coat Ceremony, for interest and excellence in restorative dentistry.

points: By a policy begun by the Dental Students' Society, only prizes listed here appear on records.

points: Highest standing in Physicianship and Dentistry Apprenticeship units.

points: Highest in second-year Support Tissue.

points: Highest in second-year Foundations of Dentistry.

points: Highest overall in second year.

points: Highest in third-year Prosthetic Dentistry.

points: The junior CDA Student Governor, for leadership.

points: Highest in third-year Pharmacology, Oral Pathology, Medicine and Radiology.

title: Dr. Gerald Franklin Prize
points: Highest in third-year exams.

title: Dr. Philip J. and Mrs. Stella Gitnick Prize
points: Since 2009, highest in Periodontology on entering fourth year.

title: International College of Dentists Prize (Canadian Section)
points: Third-year achievement and character.

title: Dr. Morton and Dr. Jonathan Lang Prize in Dentistry
points: Academic merit.

title: Dr. Ernest R. Ambrose Scholarship in Dentistry
points: Since 2001, for common sense, compassion and excellence in restorative dentistry, preferring those entering fourth year.

title: Dr. Leanore K. Feine Prize
points: Commitment to the local community's oral health.

title: Canadian Dental Association Student Leadership Award
points: A graduating CDA member with outstanding leadership, scholarship, character and humanity.

title: Dr. J.K. Carver Award
points: Second-highest overall across four years, from the Ordre des Dentistes.

title: Dr. Soo Kim Lan Prize in Dentistry
points: Since 2000, an outstanding graduate entering a residency or postgraduate program.

title: Dr. W.G. Leahy Prize
points: Final-year achievement in Clinical Dentistry.

title: Dr. Paul A. Marchand and Maurine McNeil Marchand Prize
points: Final-year professionalism and patient management.

title: Dr. James McCutcheon Medal
points: A graduate with outstanding leadership, scholarship and professional achievement.

title: McGill Alumnae Society Prize
points: Excellence and high standing at graduation, preferring women.

title: Prix Micheline-Blain – ACDQ
points: A graduate who best served colleagues, from the Québec Dental Surgeons Association.

title: Dr. A. Gerald Racey Prize
points: Excellence in the OSCE of the final oral and maxillofacial exam.

title: Dr. A.W. Thornton Medal
points: Highest overall across four years, from the Montreal Dental Club.

title: Prix d’excellence Jean-Robert Vincent
points: Highest in Geriatric Dentistry, from the Québec Association for Special Care Dentistry.

title: Dr. A.L. Walsh Prize
points: Final-year achievement in Oral Medicine.

title: Dr. Marvin And Mandy Werbitt Award in Dentistry
points: Since 2008, a graduate with initiative and strong standing in Periodontology.

title: Evaluation and Promotion in Dentistry
points: The Student Promotion Committee decides on promotion and graduation. Rules may change, generally not mid-year. See the Professionalism Standard, Absences and Leaves Policy, Ethical Behaviour guidelines and Promotion Guidelines.

title: About Dentistry
points: A dynamic D.M.D. curriculum aimed at sound judgment and evidence-based care with social justice, linking oral and general health, and preparing leaders to tackle disparities.

title: Admissions – Undergraduate Program
points: Applications open September 1 the year before, with a non-refundable fee. Any field of study is welcome. The Faculty seeks socially aware, community-minded people with listening, empathy and compassion.

title: Application Deadlines – Undergraduate Dentistry Program
points: Four-year D.M.D.: apply November 1, documents November 3. Dent-P: apply March 1, documents March 3. Advanced Standing: apply March 1, documents March 3.
Accepting requires a CAD $500 deposit against tuition.

title: Deferred Admission
points: Exceptionally one year, at the Committee's discretion, after an offer. Write to the Chair of Admissions by July 15, in two pages at most with documents, plus a non-refundable $500. Not for Dent-P or Advanced Standing.

title: Extenuating Circumstances
points: Serious medical or personal difficulties affecting your grades can be claimed on your application.

title: Students Enrolled in a Graduate Program
points: No concurrent programs, so apply in your final year. Thesis submitted and confirmed by July 31 of your entry year, or the offer is withdrawn.

title: Four-Year Undergraduate Dental Program (D.M.D.)
points: 16 months of Fundamentals of Medicine and Dentistry with Medicine, seven months of preclinical training, then two clinical years, with rotations at Montreal General, Montreal Children's, the Jim Lund Clinic at Welcome Hall Mission, and the Alan Edwards Pain Unit.

title: Requirements
points: A full-time 120-credit bachelor's in any field by July 31 of entry, or 90 credits with a pre-university DEC. A second degree counts with 45 new graded credits by November 1 and 15 more by July 31. A marked decline can cost the offer. No narrative transcripts.

title: Basic Science Requirements
points: With labs: 6 credits Biology, 6 General or Physical Chemistry, 3 Organic Chemistry, 6 Physics (3 of Calculus can count for half). All by May 31 of applying, with four of seven done by November 1. Graded, not P/F (except Winter 2020). A-Levels, French Baccalaureate, IB HL and AP may be accepted.
Cell biology, physiology, statistics and genetics are strongly recommended.

title: Casper Test – Computer-Based Assessment for Sampling Personal Characteristics
points: Mandatory before the deadline: 12 sections of video and written scenarios, assessing personal skills, each scored by a different rater. No studying needed; do the practice test. You need a webcam computer. Valid one cycle.

title: Dental Aptitude Test (DAT)
points: Removed for Fall 2025 entry, with future use under review.

title: French Language Requirements
points: B2 by the start of Clinical Practice in third year.

title: Dentistry Preparatory Qualifying Year (DENT-P Year + D.M.D.)
points: A year in the Faculty of Science to adapt to university, then the D.M.D. Keep CGPA 3.5 to continue.

title: Requirements
points: Québec residents in the final year of CEGEP Sciences, not university students or from outside Québec. At least six courses each semester. Three-year Science and Science-IB, and Arts and Science (700.A0) with the competencies, can qualify. Collège Marie de France and Stanislas qualify under conditions.

title: Basic Science Requirements
points: Biology NYA and NYB, Chemistry NYA, NYB and Organic I, Math NYA–NYC, Physics NYA–NYC. 700.A0 and IB-DEC have their own equivalents, with preference for closer matches.

title: Casper Test — Computer-Based Assessment for Sampling Personal Characteristics
points: CASPer required; see the Dent-P Requirements page.

title: Dental Aptitude Test (DAT)
points: Removed for Fall 2025 entry, with future use under review.

title: Applicants not Admissible to the Dent-P Year:
points: DEC taking over two years, those who already have a DEC or have registered in a degree, and LCC IB or Stanstead Grade 12.
Exceptions: remedial entry, transfer into Science within three years, Sport-études with a form, and Dental Hygiene DEC followed by Science within five. You may still apply to the four-year D.M.D.

title: Dentistry (Four-Year Program) (D.M.D.) (221 credits)
points: Fundamentals with Medicine, preclinical training, then two clinical years with hospital rotations and the McGill Pain Centre.

title: Dental Preparatory (Dent-P) (B.Sc.) (30 credits)
points: A preparatory Science year, then the D.M.D., with CGPA 3.5.

title: Location
points: 2001 McGill College Ave., Suite 500.

title: Program Description
points: Simulation and clinical training, with Fundamentals taught with Medicine and hospital rotations.

title: Program Description
points: 30 credits in Science (18 required, 12 humanities electives), then four years. Promotion needs CGPA 3.5, B or higher in each required course, and passes in complementaries. Otherwise transfer to a B.Sc. and reapply later.

title: Degree Requirements — B.Sc.
points: To graduate, you need both the program's courses and the degree's requirements, including Foundation and structure (p. 1106). Fitting them together is your responsibility, and SOUSA's Degree Planning Guide helps.

title: About General Practice Residency (GPR) Program
points: One year of advanced general dentistry across specialties, with oral sedation, BLS and ACLS. Canada's largest, with 23 residents, at Montreal General, Montreal Children's and Jewish General.

title: Admissions Requirements
points: CDA or ADA-approved graduates or final-year students, with the degree by registration. Based on standing and interviews. Apply to the ODQ for a temporary permit. Québec graduates must pass ODQ's exam. No narrative transcripts.

title: French Language Requirement
points: Québec graduates must show French before a permit, with no temporary permit, usually by OQLF exam unless schooled in French.
Others may get a permit for up to a year, renewable three times, passing the OQLF exam in time.

title: Application Procedures
points: Online, not through the undergraduate portal, opening each fall. Official transcripts, three references (your Dean and two dental professors), and a personal statement, plus another if applying to Montreal Children's. Put your McGill ID on everything.

title: Location
points: 2001 McGill College Ave., Suite 500.

title: Program Description
points: Advanced general practice training, with sedation, BLS and ACLS, from accredited Canadian or U.S. schools and eligible for Québec licensure. Those not schooled in Québec must meet OQLF's French requirement first.

title: About Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
points: Oral Surgery Internship, sponsored 2-year internship and 4-year program, Integrated O.M.F.S. & M.D.,C.M. residency, and an ad hoc Fellowship in Maxillofacial Oncology and Microvascular Reconstruction.

title: Oral Surgery Internship (Cert.) (52 credits)
points: One year for Canadians or PRs from accredited North American schools, working with residents. Two years, unfunded, only for graduates of programs with a sponsorship agreement.

title: Sponsored 2-year Internship and 4-year Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (Cert.) (144 credits)
points: Sponsor-funded, only for graduates of programs with a sponsorship agreement.

title: Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (Integrated O.M.F.S. & M.D.,C.M.)(Cert.)
points: Six years, giving an M.D.,C.M. and a Certificate, accredited by CDAC, LCME and CACMS.

title: Admissions Requirements
points: See Find your program, or contact the Division.

title: Application Procedures
points: Online only: unofficial transcripts (McGill can demand official ones and rescind offers), three references, CV, personal statement, and possibly the National Board Comprehensive Basic Science Exam.

title: Application Dates and Deadlines
points: For 2026–2027: opened September 1, 2025; deadline August 31, 2026.

refs.label: Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (4-year program) (Cert.) (144 credits)
Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (Integrated O.M.F.S. & M.D.,C.M.) (Cert.)

title: Location
points: Montreal General Hospital, 1650 Cedar Ave., Room B3.119.

title: Program Description
points: One year preparing you for an OMFS residency: assisting residents with patient care, plus lectures, seminars and journal clubs. One or two places, for Canadians or PRs from accredited North American schools, or sponsored programs.

title: Program Description
points: Four years from July 1, accredited, with an optional M.Sc. year, for practising and academic surgeons. Only for graduates of sponsored programs. Needs a D.D.S. or D.M.D., a limited ODQ licence (no French test first), a year of internship or GPR, and ACLS.

title: Program Description
points: Six years from July 1, accredited, with an M.D.,C.M. Only for dentists who are Canadian or PR, from accredited North American schools, with a limited ODQ licence.

title: Graduate and Postgraduate Dentistry Programs
points: Some are in the Professional section; others in the graduate section.

title: Continuing Dental Education
points: Recognized by licensing bodies, in clinical and basic sciences, to keep practitioners and researchers current. See the page for the list.

title: Faculty of Education
points: Over a century preparing education professionals, advancing knowledge and practice in Québec, Canada and internationally.

title: Department of Integrated Studies in Education
points: Prepares elementary and secondary teachers: four-year B.Ed. for CEGEP graduates, five years for out-of-province, and options with prior degrees.

B.Ed. in Secondary English, Math, Science and Technology, Social Sciences; Kindergarten and Elementary, with First Nations and Inuit, Jewish Studies or French Immersion; TESL. B.Mus./B.Ed. isn't currently offered. B.A.(Education) in Global Contexts, and First Nations and Inuit programs (p. 699).

title: Department of Educational and Counselling Psychology
points: Research on cognition and development across the lifespan, assessment and intervention, neuroscience, and learning environments. Minor concentrations (p. 697).

title: Department of Kinesiology and Physical Education
points: Knowledge about health and physical activity, and professional preparation. B.Ed. in Physical and Health Education, B.Sc. Kinesiology Major and Honours, and a B.Sc. minor (p. 738).

refs.label: Programs for First Nations and Inuit

title: Location
points: Education Building, 3700 McTavish St.

title: Overview of Programs Offered
points: Undergraduate: B.Ed., which can lead to certification, B.A. in Education, B.Sc. in Kinesiology. Professional development for teachers: certificates and diplomas, mostly evenings and summer. Graduate: master's and doctorates, and a Master of Arts in Teaching and Learning with certification.

title: Programs for First Nations and Inuit
points: For First Nations and Inuit teachers, through OFNIE, Education Building, Room 431A. One route to certification, plus Student Personnel Services (p. 734) and Inclusive Education (p. 737) for certified teachers, with enrolment limits.

refs.label: Kindergarten and Elementary Education (B.Ed.) - First Nations and Inuit Studies (120 credits)
Elementary Education: Indigenous Education (B.Ed. for Certified Teachers) (90 credits)
Education for First Nations and Inuit (Cert.) (60 credits)
Middle School Education in Indigenous Communities (Cert.) (30 credits)
First Nations and Inuit Educational Leadership (Cert.) (30 credits)
Indigenous Language and Literacy Education (Cert.) (30 credits)

title: Programs of Professional Development
points: Usually 30 credits, part-time possible, normally for certified teachers.

title: Programs Offered
points: Certificate in Inclusive Education; Diploma in Human Relationships, Diversity and Sexuality. Room 614.

title: Programs Offered
points: Graduate Certificates in Educational Leadership and TESL. Room 244.

title: The Office of First Nations and Inuit Education (OFNIE)
points: With Kativik Ilisarniliriniq, the Cree School Board, Kahnawà:ke Education Centre and other Indigenous communities, delivers field-based programs leading to certification and B.Ed. degrees, at McGill or off campus.

title: Undergraduate Education Programs
points: All B.Ed. programs are CAPFE-accredited. CEGEP gives 30 credits of Advanced Standing, sometimes fewer. Without CEGEP, French or IB, or a university year, add a 30-credit Foundation: 120 for B.A.(Ed.) and B.Sc.(Kin.), 150 or 167 for B.Ed.

title: Bachelor of Education Programs Leading to Teacher Certification
points: Completing a program, plus Ministry requirements, means recommendation for Québec certification. The concurrent Music program isn't currently offered.

refs.label: Secondary Social Sciences - History and Citizenship, Culture and Citizenship in Quebec (120 credits)
Secondary Social Sciences (B.Ed.) - History and Citizenship, Geography (120 credits)
Kindergarten and Elementary Education (B.Ed.) - First Nations and Inuit Studies (120 credits)
Kindergarten and Elementary Jewish Studies (B.Ed.) (120 credits)
Kindergarten and Elementary Pédagogie de l'Immersion Française (B.Ed.) (120 credits)
Teaching English as a Second Language (TESL) (B.Ed.) - Elementary and Secondary (120 credits)
Teaching English as a Second Language (TESL) (B.Ed.) - Elementary and Secondary: Teaching Greek Language and Culture (120 credits)

title: Bachelor of Arts and Bachelor of Science Education Programs
points: B.A.(Education), Global Contexts (90 credits): education for global challenges across sociology, psychology, leadership, history and policy, with a semester internship, for non-classroom educators.
B.Sc. Kinesiology (90 credits): human movement from social, historical, psychological and biological angles, with minors and an Honours for graduate-bound students.

title: General Admission Requirements
points: See the Undergraduate Admissions Guide. Secondary Science, Secondary Math and Kinesiology have math or science prerequisites. For transfers and readmission, see p. 39, p. 41 and the ISA site.

title: Language Requirement for Applicants to B.Ed. TESL Program
points: Apply to McGill; those considered may need to pass written and oral English tests.

title: Credit Requirements
points: B.Ed. 120 credits, or 150 with Foundation; B.A.(Ed.) and B.Sc.(Kin.) 90, or 120. At least 60 at McGill.

Transfer credit is decided after you apply. Courses over five years old aren't allowed where content changed, nor pedagogy for Québec's K-11; others go to the Program Director. Check your record, and see your adviser in your admitted term.

title: Language Proficiency
points: Oral and written fluency in the language of instruction is required for certification.

title: Confidential Declaration Concerning Judicial Record
points: Under a 2005 Québec law, anyone seeking certification must submit a confidential judicial record declaration to the Minister.

title: Quebec Teacher Certification
points: The Ministry certifies, on McGill's recommendation, and you must apply. All B.Ed. graduates can apply for a permanent Brevet at graduation, by the deadline.
To teach elsewhere, get Québec certification first and check that place's rules. Those from elsewhere apply to the Ministry.

title: International Students
points: You need a co-op or internship work permit, besides CAQ and study permit, with a medical exam by a designated physician, or you can't work in schools or start your placement. For a Brevet, hold a Post-Graduation Work Permit or study permit.

title: Faculty Regulations for Undergraduate Programs
points: University rules apply, plus these. Correct courses, requirements, deadlines and records are your responsibility.

title: Advising
points: Internships and Student Affairs (ISA), Education Building, Room 243.

title: Academic Advising
points: New students must see an adviser before Fall. Returning students are advised in spring. Those entering their final year should meet their program adviser.

title: Academic Standing
points: Based mainly on CGPA and TGPA, and for B.Ed. on Field Experience. Fall decisions are Interim and advisory.
An F in a Fall EDFE means Unsatisfactory, though the ISA Director may allow Winter courses. A D means Probationary.

title: Satisfactory/Interim Satisfactory Standing
points: CGPA 2.00 or more. You continue.

title: Interim Probationary Standing at the End of the Fall Term
points: Continue, reduce your load, and see your adviser before withdrawal deadlines. First- or Second-Year Field Experiences may proceed.

title: Probationary Standing at the End of the Winter Term
points: Continue with at most 12 credits, no Field Experience next year, raise TGPA and CGPA, and see your adviser.

title: Placement in Probationary Standing
points: CGPA 1.50–1.99 after Satisfactory; a D in Field Experience after Satisfactory; CGPA 1.50–1.99 and TGPA 2.50+ after Probationary or Interim Unsatisfactory; or the same after Readmitted, meeting your letter's conditions.

title: Interim Unsatisfactory Standing at the End of the Fall Term
points: Continue, reduce your load and see an adviser, but no next Field Experience (B.Ed.) or internship (B.A.).

title: Unsatisfactory Standing
points: You've missed the minimum standards and can't continue, or do planned internships or field experience.

title: Placement in Unsatisfactory Standing
points: CGPA below 1.50; TGPA under 2.50 with CGPA under 2.00 after Probationary, Readmitted or Interim Unsatisfactory; failure (F, J, KF, WF) in any Field Experience, in any term; or missing your readmission conditions.
Concurrent B.Mus./B.Ed.: F or J in Field Experience means leaving that program, though you can ask Schulich about a B.Mus.

title: Readmission
points: Apply in Minerva by July 1 (Fall) or November 15 (Winter). Appeal to the ISA Director with proof of extenuating circumstances. A second Unsatisfactory means leaving permanently.
After a Field Experience failure, wait at least a full year, apply by April 15 for Fall, and the Student Affairs Committee hears the appeal.

title: Readmission After Unsatisfactory Standing
points: You become Readmitted Unsatisfactory, with a set load and conditions. See your adviser.

title: Incomplete Standing
points: Clear Ks, Ls or supplementals. You can register for Fall, but it must be settled by the end of course change.
You continue if it becomes Satisfactory, Probationary or Interim Unsatisfactory. If Unsatisfactory, ask the Director right away, with proof. If still Incomplete, contact ISA.

title: Attendance
points: Varies by course, and is critical in B.Ed. for professional competence. Unexcused absences can mean exclusion, failure or removal from a Field Experience.
Field Experience needs punctuality throughout. Some start in August, some are in spring or overlap exams, so check the schedule; you're excused for a final exam. See the Student Teaching e-Handbook.

title: Course Load
points: Usually 15 credits a term; under 12 is part-time. Satisfactory: up to 17. CGPA above 3.00: may ask for more, not in major Field Experience terms. Probationary: at most 12.
B.Ed. and B.Sc.(Kin.) are full-time only, unless the ISA Director agrees before add/drop ends. B.A.(Ed.) can be part-time within the time limit.

title: Part-Time Student Status
points: Not allowed in order to study elsewhere. It can affect your time limit, scholarships, loans, aid, awards, immigration, insurance, and student discounts such as OPUS. Keep documents justifying it, and check with the relevant office first.

title: Time Limit and Credits for Completion of Degrees
points: B.Ed.: five years and 150 credits. B.A.(Ed.) and B.Sc.(Kin.): four years and 120. Foundation students start counting after a year. Going beyond takes permission, for valid academic reasons, and only needed courses count.

title: Course Requirements
points: C or better in program courses. If short, pass a supplemental or repeat, or replace a complementary. See your adviser yearly, and at the end of year 3 (B.Ed.) or 2 (others). Failure in Field Experience means leaving the program.

title: Electives
points: Any McGill course, except Continuing Studies courses with C codes (CHEM excepted). See below for online.

title: Courses Taken as Transfer Credit
points: Outside Québec: approval from your adviser and ISA first, only for courses your program needs, and not in your graduating term.

title: Inter-University Transfer Credit
points: 3, exceptionally 6, credits a term in Québec, with your adviser's permission. Only needed courses, and not in your graduating term.

title: Online Courses
points: At most 18 credits, with approval for other universities' courses. May affect some government loans.

title: Courses Taken under Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory Option
points: Not for required or complementary courses, including B.Ed. subject courses.

title: Course Equivalencies and Overlap
points: No extra credit for overlaps. Know the exclusions, and confirm Advanced Standing and exemptions.

title: Dress Code Regulations
points: Follow school rules on attire. Kinesiology and Physical Education need suitable activity clothing and possibly some equipment.

title: English Language Requirement
points: B.Ed. students write the English Exam for Teacher Certification in their first semester (Foundation in Year 1), and must pass before the Fourth Field Experience. Register for EDEC 215 and with CEETC, and pay each time.
Failing means support and a retake. After five tries, ask the ISA Director. A sixth failure means withdrawal. Not for First Nations and Inuit certificates.

title: Examinations
points: See p. 62. Tentative schedule about a month in, final about two. Don't book travel early.

title: Supplemental Examinations
points: Apply in Minerva by the deadline, in Satisfactory or Probationary Standing with D, J, F or U.

title: Reassessment and Rereads
points: You can see and discuss your graded work. Two types: reassessing coursework and rereading a final.

title: Reassessment of Course Work
points: Ask within 10 working days of its return, normally done within 20. The reviewer judges fairness. The grade can go up or down, and the new one stands.

title: Rereads of Final Exams or Final Term Papers or Projects
points: Write to ISA by March 31 (Fall), June 30 (Winter) or September 30 (Summer), strictly. Talk to the instructor first if you can. The grade can change either way. Other faculties' rules apply to their courses.

title: Grading
points: Outlines in the first week describe evaluation. See p. 53 and the assessment policy.

title: Graduation Requirements
