title: Programs of Study, Admission, and Curriculum
points: Toutes ces informations sont disponibles en français et en anglais au : mcgill.ca/medadmissions.
All information is available in both English and French at: mcgill.ca/ medadmissions.

title: Medical Societies
points: All medical students belong to the Medical Students' Society; see p. 941.

title: Undergraduate Medical Programs
points: See p. 940 for the Faculty. Fees are on the Student Accounts site.

title: Doctor of Medicine and Master of Surgery (M.D.,C.M.) Medicine (200–204 credits)
points: Four years, requiring a bachelor's degree. Graduates can work as supervised, undifferentiated physicians. Science and scientific method are central, through lectures, small groups, labs and computers. CACMS status: fully accredited, with probation.
Two campuses: Montreal Downtown, and Campus Outaouais in Gatineau, opened in 2020 and taught in French to a select cohort. Both share electives and residency options.

Four components: Fundamentals of Medicine and Dentistry (FMD), Transition to Clinical Practice (TCP), Clerkship, and Physicianship. Placements are bilingual or francophone, with new third-year Integrated Clerkships being developed in the RUISSS McGill network. Expect to be audio- and video-recorded, as at the Steinberg Centre.

Observation starts in first year; clerkship in third adds responsibility. Classes are in English (Montreal) or French (Outaouais), but you must work comfortably in both. French is required before admission; English proof only for those schooled in non-English countries outside Canada (p. 1001). No part-time study.

title: Doctor of Medicine and Master of Surgery with Ph.D. (Joint M.D.,C.M. & Ph.D.)
points: Seven years for research careers: medical sciences from September of Year 1 to December 31 of Year 2, then 3–4 years of graduate study ending in a thesis, then M.D.,C.M. from January of Year 5 to May of Year 7. Meetings every two weeks for research talk and networking.

title: Doctor of Medicine and Master of Surgery with Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (Joint M.D.,C.M. & O.M.F.S.)
points: Six years, with Dental Medicine: an M.D.,C.M. and a Certificate in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery.

title: Admission Requirements
points: A D.D.S. or D.M.D. from an accredited North American school, eligibility for a limited Quebec dental license (no French test first), a passed NBME Comprehensive Basic Science Exam before the deadline, and ACLS before starting.

title: Application Information
points: Through Dental Medicine, online (postgrad Med/Dent Education), August 1 to September 1.

title: Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.) - Medicine Preparatory Program (Med-P Program)
points: A one-year Science qualifying program for new CEGEP graduates, then the four-year M.D.,C.M. In English in Montreal, or French in Outaouais with UQO.

refs.label: Doctor of Medicine and Master of Surgery with Ph.D. (Joint M.D.,C.M. & Ph.D.)
Medicine and Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery (Joint M.D.,C.M. & O.M.F.S.)

title: Location
points: Administrative Offices: 3605 de la Montagne St., H3G 2M1. Educational Services: 680 Sherbrooke St. W., Office 1701. Admissions: 2001 McGill College Ave., Suite 1310.

title: Program Description
points: FMD covers year 1 and early year 2; TCP late year 2; Clerkship years 3–4; Physicianship all four. Objectives follow Canadian authorities. Graduates can only be licensed to practise in supervised residency, not independently.

title: Program Description
points: Seven years, as above, meeting Thursday evenings. Taught in English. In year one you start choosing a supervisor and lab, with Research Bursaries helping you explore. By September of Year 2 pick a supervisor and department with the Advisory Committee and be accepted to graduate studies. See p. 983.

title: Program Description
points: Six years, based at the Montreal General, a level-one trauma centre. MUHC handles over 802,000 ambulatory visits a year, including 134,000 emergency visits. Accredited by the Commission on Dental Accreditation of Canada; the M.D.,C.M. by LCME and CACMS. Taught in English. See p. 983.

title: Program Description
points: For new CEGEP graduates, registered in Science with all campus services. Molecular and cell biology, metabolism, and organic chemistry if needed, plus options like computer science, chemistry, physiology and math, and required humanities, social sciences and electives.

To enter M.D.,C.M.: at least B in each compulsory course and a CGPA of 3.5. Otherwise you may be admitted with conditions, repeat a preparatory year, or be invited back after a bachelor's. Far more apply than get in, so choose a second program. Gatineau students continue in French.

title: Degree Requirements — B.Sc.
points: To graduate, you need both the program's courses and the degree's requirements, including Foundation and structure (p. 1106). Fitting them together is your responsibility, and SOUSA's Degree Planning Guide helps.

title: Programs in Science Taught by the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences
points: The Faculty teaches and collaborates on B.Sc. programs in Science (p. 1104).

title: Graduate Studies and Research in the Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences
points: Ph.D. work in many departments, plus the M.D.,C.M. & Ph.D. (p. 985). Clinical research happens across MUHC sites, the Lady Davis Institute, the Douglas and Shriners. Several clinical departments are grouped under Experimental Medicine and Surgical and Interventional Sciences. Ask the Chair or Graduate Director.

title: Graduate Training Programs in the Clinical Departments
points: Residency programs leading to McGill certificates and certification by the CMQ, College of Family Physicians and Royal College. See mcgill.ca/pgme.

title: Admission Procedures and Requirements
points: mcgill.ca/medadmissions wins if details differ. A rigorous, multi-criteria review guided by excellence, inclusivity, alignment, fairness and transparency. Show commitment to academics, ethics and awareness of the world you'll serve.

title: Undergraduate Degree Performance
points: Based on degree CGPA, science prerequisites and context. Successful applicants have been above 3.5, average about 3.8; below 3.5 is rarely competitive. You may not be considered without 60 consecutive graded credits. See p. 994.

title: Performance in the Basic Science Prerequisites
points: Normally C or above. Pass or Satisfactory counts only for Winter 2020. For exemptions, contact Admissions between June and September; requests after September 30 may be ignored. See p. 994.

title: Academic Context
points: The Committee looks at your whole record: course levels, graduate and professional study. Take challenging, varied courses with progression, and a full load in regular terms.

title: CEGEP Performance for Med-P Applicants
points: R-score generally above 34.0, average about 37.0; below 33.0 is rarely competitive. Strongest academic evidence wins out.

title: Applicant Categories
points: Quebec's government sets places and their distribution by residence. Prove citizenship and confirm your category when applying.

Quebec Resident: University (CGPA 3.5+) or Med-P (R-score 33.0+). Canadian Out-of-Province: CGPA 3.7+. International, needing a study permit, US citizens included: CGPA 3.7+. All must meet education and science requirements, French proof and CASPer. Interviews follow ranking; final selection is by MMI within your cohort.

Your category lasts through your studies, even if status changes. Quebec requires Out-of-Province and study-permit students to sign a contract with a return-of-service obligation or a fine if they stay to practise. M.D.,C.M./Ph.D. seats come from Quebec university, Canadian and International quotas. Some seats go first to Special Pathways.
Extra positions: Quebec First Nations or Inuit through FNIFMPQ, and Quebec-resident International Medical Graduates with Advanced Standing. See p. 989.

title: File Review Process
points: You compete within your cohort for set positions. Files are ranked by academics, and separately CASPer, with no strict GPA line. Documents get reviewed for four to six times the number to be interviewed, such as the top 200–300 for 50 interviews. Final rank is 100% interview score. The waitlist can run until classes begin.

title: Interview Process
points: By emailed invitation only, in two Zoom sessions, and required for admission. Virtual multiple mini-interviews use task, simulation, scenario and discussion stations based on Physicianship and CanMEDS, sometimes on sensitive themes. No clinical skills. Say at application if you want French, English or either.
Half-day sessions. Keep your date free; no repeats, and missing it for any reason ends your file. Accommodations are considered case by case.

title: Process to request an accommodation for the virtual Multiple Mini Interviews (vMMIs)
points: Including colourblindness. Send the request and documents from a health professional or disability service within 3 days of your invitation or waitlist notice. Prepare ahead.

title: Non-Academic Qualities
points: Screened through CV and CASPer, then interviews, in line with CanMEDS: compassion, judgment, integrity, adaptability, creativity, respect, curiosity, reliability, teamwork, handling stress, leadership, confidence, community involvement, professionalism and personal growth.

title: Special Admissions Pathways
points: To make classes reflect the community and include historically under-represented ethnic, cultural and racial groups, sexual minorities and all economic backgrounds.

title: Quebec First Nations and Inuit Faculties of Medicine Program
points: Since 2008, twelve positions across Laval, Montréal, McGill and Sherbrooke, by preference and availability. Must be a Quebec resident with status under the Indian Act or in the Inuit registry, with R-score 28 for Med-P or CGPA about 3.2, plus education, science, French (ask about support) and Casper.

Declaring status puts you in both this and the regular contingent; otherwise regular only. Top candidates are interviewed by Indigenous and professional members. Those with a degree by July 31 apply to M.D.,C.M., perhaps with a preparatory year; others to Med-P; a bachelor's is needed for M.D.,C.M. & Ph.D.
Final selection: individual interview 50% and MMIs 50%. Confirm status with the First Nations of Quebec and Labrador Commission's coordinator. See jedeviensmedecin.com.

title: Canadian Indigenous Pathway
points: For non-Quebec First Nations, Inuit or Métis university applicants: two of the eleven out-of-province seats. Requires formal status documents (Indian Status card, Inuit land claim recognition, or Métis National Council or Manitoba Métis Federation card), GPA 3.4, plus education, science, French (ask about support) and CASPer.

Select this in the application and upload the Indigenous personal statement. You're also assessed in the general cohort, and self-identifying is optional. An advisory committee of Indigenous faculty, students, an Elder and others reviews CV, statement, CASPer and science. You do MMIs and an individual interview; offers rest on MMI within this cohort.
The Indigenous Health Professions Program offers outreach and support. All medical students get Indigenous health teaching, with rotations available. First Peoples' House is on campus.

title: Rural and Small Populations Pathway (RSPP)
points: For Quebec university-level applicants who did at least 3 of 5 secondary years in a public school in a rural or small area per Statistics Canada (generally under 1,000 or under 29,999 people). Two to seven seats. CGPA 3.5+. Ask about language support.

Indicate it in the application; proof of school may be requested, official only if you get an offer. Same process, but compared within the pathway and also the general pool, so a general offer frees a seat for the next person. Offers rest on MMI.

title: Black Candidate Pathway
points: For Quebec Med-P and M.D.,C.M. candidates who self-identify as Black. No seat limit, with simultaneous general consideration. GPA 3.5+ or R-score 33.0+, Casper and CV comparable to the Quebec pool, plus education, science and French (ask about support).

A holistic review, with a personal statement read by Black community members and health professionals. Indicate it online, then submit the statement in the Portal. Joining can't harm your decision. Endorsed candidates go to MMIs; offers rest on them. The Community of Support Program offers mentorship.

title: International Medical Graduates IMG-2 Pathway (with Advanced Standing)
points: For Quebec residents with a recognized foreign medical degree. Enter at TCP in April and earn the M.D.,C.M. Deadline November 1.

Needs CMQ Recognition of M.D. by November 1, MCCQE Part 1 and a NAC-OSCE (or LMCC), results shared via physiciansapply.ca, a Medical Student Performance Record and transcript, language proof, science and CASPer. Offers rest on MMI. Positions depend on attrition; some years none.

title: International Medical School Graduates IMG-4 Pathway
points: Foreign medical graduates from Quebec, Canada or abroad entering year one with that degree. Needs graded transcripts, a passed MCCQE Part 1, science, French and CASPer. Offers rest on MMI. Positions depend on attrition; some years none.
Quebec-resident citizens or landed immigrants with CMQ equivalence may instead ask PGME about direct residency. Admissions: 2001 McGill College Ave., Suite 1310.

title: Eligibility Requirements
points: The Undergraduate Medical Admissions site wins if details differ. See also Registration and Matriculation.

title: For Applicants in the University Categories
points: For degree holders in all categories. Your degree must be a bachelor's, finished by July 31 of entry.

title: Basis of Admission (Undergraduate) Degree
points: 120 credits, or 90 from a Quebec university after a pre-university DEC, in any discipline. Full-time and on schedule, with 12–15 credits a term; up to a year extra with some part-time terms stays eligible, at the office's call. Summer is fine if regular terms are full-time. At least 60 consecutive graded credits at application.

title: Second Bachelor's Degree
points: Usable if the first degree qualifies, 45 new graded credits are done by the deadline, the remaining 15+ are done by July 31 at a similar level, and the second is academically stronger.

title: All Bachelor's Degrees
points: Any background is welcome; study what interests you, for a broad education, not just to prepare for medicine. Degrees without grades, or narrative transcripts, aren't considered.

title: Special Consideration for Winter 2020 Term
points: Excluded from everyone's assessment because of COVID-19, for both GPA and full-time status.

title: Eligibility for Atypical Degrees
points: Multi-institution or pre-university credit: half must be done at the granting institution. Credit for informal learning, including Quebec's Reconnaissance des acquis extrascolaires, is capped at 10%.

title: Basic Science Prerequisites
points: College or university level, with labs: Biology 6 credits, general or physical Chemistry 6, Organic Chemistry 3, Physics 6. Grades required, not Pass/Fail, except Winter 2020. Distance courses may be accepted.

Must meet a minimum grade, but aren't weighted in the GPA. Up to three may be in progress, with transcripts by May 31. Physiology, molecular and cell biology and metabolism are strongly recommended; statistics and genetics are useful.

A Levels, IB Higher Level, French Baccalaureate terminale, and AP can substitute; see mcgill.ca/transfercredit/prospective. Ask about substitutions from June to September, not after September 30. Advanced courses generally don't replace missing introductory ones.

title: Eligibility for Special Admission Pathways
points: Pathways for those who identify as Indigenous, Black, from rural or small communities, or low-income. See Special Pathways – Underrepresented Groups.

title: Requirements for Med-P
points: Most finish a DEC in two years, full-time. Longer reasons include tremplin, Double-DEC, Sports-Études, medical withdrawal, course availability, or part-time terms.

Quebec residents in or graduated from: Science (200.B0, 200.B1); Double DEC (200.11, 200.12, 200.13, 200.15, 200.16); Science + IB (200.Z0, 200.Z1); Sciences, Lettres et Arts (700.A0, 700.A1); or a Quebec French Baccalaureate. DEC within three years, by July 31 of entry. You can't have applied before or been in a full-time university program.
Select this and send documents only if you took over 3 years or your results were temporarily affected.
Biology: NYA (00UK), Biology II (00XU), or new 0B01 and 0B0F; Arts & Science 01Y5, 01YJ; IB 7BL1, 7BL2; else two courses (5.32 credits).
Chemistry: NYA (00UL), NYB (00UM), Organic I (00XV), or new 0C01, 0C02, 0C0F; Arts & Science 01Y6, 01YH; IB 7CH1, 7CH2; else three courses (8.00 credits) with Organic I.
Physics: NYA (00UR), NYB (00US), NYC (00UT), or new 0P01, 0P02, 0P03; Arts & Science 01Y7 and 01YF or 01YG; IB 7PH1 and 7PH2 or 7PH3; else two courses (5.32 credits).
Math: NYA (00UN), NYB (00UP), NYC (00UQ), or new 0M02, 0M03, 0M04; Arts & Science 01Y1, 01Y2, 01Y4; IB 7MA1, 7MA2, 7MA4; else two courses (5.32 credits). Old and new codes are both accepted.
Not allowed: prerequisites outside regular terms, over a term in another post-secondary program, or graduating from another program. Grade 12 programs, including Stanstead or LCC, don't qualify.

Exceptions: a Fall DEC graduate may start a program that Winter, one term only and not counted. Past graduates never in full-time university and who never applied may apply with up to 12 credits and a letter with documents. French Baccalaureate applicants must do both years in Quebec with all compléments québécois and an R-score.

title: Procedures for Selection and Admission
points: The Undergraduate Medical Admissions site wins if details differ.

title: Submitting an Application
points: Everything is online.

title: Deadlines
points: M.D.,C.M., M.D.,C.M./Ph.D. and pathways: November 1. Med-P: March 1. Documents by the same dates. Submit and pay at least 48 hours before, to get your ID and password. Tests such as CASPer and MCCQE-1 must be done before the deadline.

title: Notification of Decision
points: Released through the online system, then by email. See the site for dates by cohort.

title: Request for Reconsideration
points: Very competitive: interviewed files are read by 10–20 people. Committee decisions are final. You may ask to reconsider the review procedure before interviews, or right after them before final decisions, only for an administrative error or a relevant factor you couldn't provide. Disagreeing isn't grounds.

Email Admissions within five working days of the published invitation date, or of your category's last interview day. If denied, you may go to the University Subcommittee on Admissions Review, which only checks procedure.

title: Offers of a Position
points: Conditional on your bachelor's or DEC and on similar results in current studies. First offers: reply within two weeks; waitlist offers may be shorter. Accepting needs a non-refundable deposit toward fees.

title: Waiting List
points: You get your number, not rankings. Stay reachable and keep your details current; missing a deadline can lose the offer.

title: Decision by Proxy
points: If unavailable, a delegate can respond, with a written statement signed by both.

title: Deferred Admission
points: After accepting, request in writing with documents by July 1. One year only, at the Assistant Dean's discretion. Not for Med-P.

title: Transfers
points: No transfer places. Quebec medical students can't apply to first year for seven years from original enrolment, even after withdrawing; McGill's counts from year one, not Med-P. Students elsewhere must prove withdrawal first. Those with medical degrees or residency from Canada or the US aren't eligible; others see IMG (p. 989).

No direct Medicine–Dentistry transfers: apply to first year of D.M.D. through regular selection; see UGME Advanced Standing Policy the other way. No transfers into Med-P, and Dent-P students can't apply to the M.D.,C.M. without a degree.

title: Credits and Advanced Standing
points: No credit for earlier courses, except: IMG Advanced Standing (degree in 2 years); interprofessional courses other than IPEA 500 and 501; M.D.,C.M.-OMFS (2.5 years); McGill D.M.D. courses.

title: Requirements for Registration and Matriculation
points: Some of these may be asked for during application.

title: Academic Standards and Essential Skills (Technical Standards)
points: You must have the intellectual, physical and emotional capacity to meet the curriculum in reasonable time, without changing its essentials. Applicants who qualify are considered, and eligible students get reasonable accommodation with Student Accessibility and Achievement, as Quebec's Charter requires.
Skills follow CanMEDS roles (Medical Expert, Communicator, Collaborator, Manager, Health Advocate, Scholar, Professional) and the Four Principles of Family Medicine.

Observe patients by sight, sound and touch; read documents; use a stethoscope, with aids if needed. Communicate well, sensitively and in writing, including non-verbal cues. Perform palpation, percussion and auscultation; ideally general and emergency care movements.

Measure, calculate, reason and solve problems promptly. Build mature relationships and work in clinics, hospitals and other settings. Show judgment, finish duties, adapt, handle uncertainty and stress. Compassion, integrity and motivation are expected.
Follow McGill's conduct rules and the CMQ code of ethics, and keep satisfactory standing. You confirm reading this when applying; it also applies through Med-P.

title: Basic Cardiac Life Support
points: By July 31 of your start year, show CPR level C or C+ and AED training, valid at start and kept current, from: Heart and Stroke Foundation, Canadian Red Cross, Canadian Ski Patrol, St. John Ambulance, Lifesaving Society of Quebec, American Heart Association or American Red Cross.

title: Immunization
points: Both campuses: a chosen professional reviews records. Submit by May 1, verified by Orientation. Meet the Protocole d'immunisation du Québec and COVID-19 directives, plus yearly flu shots; keep proof. Other vaccines may be needed.
AFMC requirements for visiting electives in third year are strongly recommended. If using your family doctor or CLSC, follow McGill's rules exactly. Missing them may mean being asked to withdraw.

title: Policy on Students Known to be Infected with Blood-Borne Viruses (e.g., Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV)
points: Carriers might not perform some procedures. If you have Hepatitis B or C, HIV or similar, you must tell the Associate Dean of UGME on entry. You're referred to SERTIH, helped with care and career advice; rotations and residency choices may be limited. Core rotation changes appear in your MSPR, and you must disclose to your residency program.

title: Health Insurance
points: Through the Student Society. Disability insurance: FMEQ's partner, with more from the CMA's financial division in first year.

title: Information Technology
points: You need a computer with office software, a browser and internet; myCourses hosts the e-curriculum. A Wi-Fi laptop is recommended, with some campus labs for backup. Applying means you agree to audio or video recording for teaching.

title: English and French Communication Skills
points: You'll treat francophone patients and may rotate at francophone sites, so be ready to work in both languages. Language courses are possible during the program under the UGME Registration Policy.

title: French Language Proficiency
points: Required before admission to the M.D.,C.M. or Med-P, as in other health programs. See the UGME Policy on Language Proficiency for accepted tests.

title: Student Campus Assignment (Montréal and Outaouais)
points: You finish all studies at your assigned campus, with no transfers or changes. Med-P in Outaouais is at UQO, the M.D.,C.M. at Campus Outaouais. Electives at both are open to all.

title: Medical Equipment
points: Buy your own for first year: stethoscope, pen light, reflex hammer, ophthalmoscope/otoscope, 128Hz tuning forks, BP cuff, and eye protection meeting Health Canada or CSA-Z94.3.

Lab: a long white coat, an anatomy dissecting kit per two people, a box of gloves and safety glasses. Also buy two white lab jackets through UGME. The White Coat Ceremony is in September or October of second year. A phone or pager is recommended in TCP and Clerkship.

title: Registration with the Collège des Médecins du Québec
points: Required by law, electronically, by September 30 of first year; the CMQ emails you to confirm. Without it you can't continue.

title: Security (Criminal Record) Check
points: CMQ registration includes a record check. Training sites may ask you to declare any record. The Faculty requests withdrawal if you don't meet CMQ conditions. Some hospitals for electives ask for background checks.

title: Standards of Behaviour and Code of Conduct
points: You're held to professional standards even before qualifying: courtesy, respect, honesty and integrity. No harassment, abuse or mistreatment. See the Code of Conduct, Harassment Policy, Professional Behaviours, Social Media Guidelines and Medical Learner Affairs. Misconduct or a criminal conviction can mean dismissal.

title: New Students
points: Register in Minerva from early June, before Orientation in mid-August. Attend Faculty Registration and Orientation in person with documents, August 18–20, 2026; missing it cancels your offer.

title: Registration for Courses outside the Program
points: Language courses, or joint program courses in some cases; see the UGME registration policy.

title: Returning Students
points: Register in Minerva by the deadline or pay late fees. Details are emailed in early April.

title: Leaves of Absence
points: Medium-term: 6 consecutive days to 7 weeks and 6 days. Long-term: 8 weeks or more. See UGME's Short-Term Absences and Medium and Long-Term Leaves policies. The program may limit their number and length.

title: Requirements for the Degree of M.D.,C.M.
points: Meet entrance requirements and pass all evaluations. Finish within 7 years, or 8 for the M.D.,C.M. Ph.D.

title: Requirements for License
points: A degree doesn't give the right to practise; each province, state or country has its own licensing body and rules, so contact yours early. Quebec also has a French requirement (p. 70).

Regulators: Colleges of Physicians and Surgeons of Alberta (Edmonton), BC (Vancouver), Manitoba (Winnipeg), New Brunswick (Rothesay; Dr. Ed Schollenberg, Registrar), Newfoundland and Labrador (St. John's), Nova Scotia (Bedford), Ontario (Toronto), PEI (Charlottetown), Saskatchewan (Saskatoon); Collège des médecins du Québec (1250 René-Lévesque W., Office 3500).
Medical Council of Canada: 1021 Thomas Spratt Pl., Ottawa. USMLE Secretariat: 3750 Market St., Philadelphia.

title: Medical Curriculum
points: The four-year M.D.,C.M. curriculum.

title: Assessment System
points: Rules can change, though usually not mid-period. Pass or fail: S or U on your transcript. Numeric grades are internal, for awards, tracking and feedback. Assessment runs by promotion period.

title: Promotion Periods
points: See the UGME Assessment and Promotion Policy, and older editions of the catalogue.

title: Student Promotions
points: This committee applies promotion rules, reviews M.D.,C.M. students and D.M.D. students during FMD, including professionalism, and has final say on suitability for medicine.

title: Failure of Supplemental Activities
points: You repeat the period or are dismissed, as the committee decides. Only one repeat in the program; failing a course during it means immediate dismissal.

title: Notice of Failures
points: Stay reachable; if you can't be found, you bear the consequences.

title: Curriculum Renewal— Governance
points: The M.D.,C.M. Program Committee, chaired by the Associate Dean (UGME), designs, oversees and improves the curriculum for mission and accreditation, with students on all committees.

title: Program Overview
points: Courses may change; check the learning system. The current curriculum began in Fall 2013, built on "The Patient at Heart and Science in Hand": family medicine alongside science, interdisciplinary learning, and themes learned together across the years.

title: About the Schulich School of Music
points: Canada's largest university music school, known for orchestral, choral, opera, jazz, chamber, contemporary and early music, and for composition, theory, musicology, education, performance science, sound recording and technology.

Halls: Pollack (600), Redpath (300, with the organ), Tanna Schulich (170), Clara Lichtenstein (50). Also the Wirth Opera Studio and Multimedia Complex, with an acoustics lab, isolation booths and studios.

Marvin Duchow Music Library: 300,000+ scores, recordings, books and journals on three floors, with a unique Open Lab for recording and editing. Gertrude Whitley Performance Library: materials for 6,000+ titles.

The Applied Performance Sciences Hub researches performance, health and careers. CIRMMT is an international group on music science and technology. Labs for composition, education, recording, cognition and modelling, plus classrooms, studios and 100+ practice rooms.
About 460 undergraduates and 400 graduates; 62+ full-time and 149 part-time teachers; about 600 concerts and events a year.

title: Location
points: Elizabeth Wirth and Strathcona Music Buildings, 527 and 555 Sherbrooke St. W., H3A 1E3.

title: Overview of Programs
points: B.Mus. and L.Mus. Music Research: Applied Performance Sciences, Composition, Education, Entrepreneurship, History, Theory, Musical Science and Technology. Performance: Conducting, Early Music, Orchestral, Piano, Voice, Organ and Guitar, Jazz. Double majors, double degrees and minors are possible across McGill. See p. 1022.

refs.label: Degrees and Diplomas Offered – Undergraduate Music
Music Courses and Music Minor Programs for Students in Other Faculties
Scholarships, Competitions, Prizes, and Financial Aid

title: Music Research
points: The B.Mus./B.Ed. Concurrent Major (p. 1027) isn't currently offered.

title: Performance
points: B.Mus. takes at least three years after a Quebec DCS, or four after secondary school elsewhere.

refs.label: Early Music Performance Major (Baroque Violin, Viola, Cello, Viola da Gamba, Flute, Recorder, Oboe, Organ, Harpsichord and Early Brass Instruments) (B.Mus.)

title: Licentiate in Music (L.Mus.)
points: Three years for advanced instrumentalists and singers, focused on performance, with only basic history, theory and musicianship.

refs.label: Performance Major (All Instruments except Piano, Voice and Jazz) (L.Mus.) (93 credits)

title: Minor Programs
points: Music minors can count as electives in a B.Mus.; minors elsewhere may also be possible. Most subjects continue to a graduate diploma, M.Mus. or M.A.

refs.label: Jazz Arranging and Composition Minor (B.Mus.) (18 credits)
Music Education Minor (B.Mus.) (18 credits) (p. 1029) **This program will not admit new students effective Fall 2026; currently under review.**
Musical Science and Technology Minor (B.Mus.) (18 credits)

title: Music Minors Open to Undergraduate Students
points: Open to all bachelor's students, with home faculty approval.

refs.label: Music Education Minor (B.Mus.) (18 credits) (p. 1029) **This program will not admit new students effective Fall 2026; currently under review.**
Musical Science and Technology Minor (B.Mus.) (18 credits)

title: Music Electives
points: Open if you meet the requirements; see the Electives site.

title: Ensembles
points: MUEN courses need an audition or the director's permission. Ask your home advisor if they count.

title: Scholarships, Competitions, Prizes, and Financial Aid
points: Entrance scholarships are automatic and renewable: Schulich, Lloyd Carr-Harris String, Student Excellence, Derek H. Davis, Suzanne Fortier (Jazz; Voice), Wirth Family (Strings; Voice), Alison Riseley Clark Organ, Mills-Tyrrell Best in the West.
Returning students' merit awards are automatic, from the year ending in April, for the next September. Competitions fund travel, projects and performance. SSAO runs other aid.

title: Summer Studies
points: One-month intensives, May to July; registration from early March. Up to 12 credits; over 6 in one month needs permission. Get approval before taking courses elsewhere.

title: Admission
points: Book a student-led tour through Discover Schulich.

title: Bachelor of Music
points: Audition and record both count, and places per instrument are limited, so minimums don't guarantee entry. Non-Canadians whose first language isn't English may need TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo before the deadline.

title: CEGEP Applicants
points: A DEC in Music or equivalent, 75% minimum; other DECs need performance experience and may add prerequisites. Three- or four-year program.

title: Canadian High School (excluding Quebec) Applicants
points: A university-track diploma with 75%. Ontario: six 4U/4M courses, at least four 4U. No non-Music prerequisites. Four years.

title: U.S. High School Applicants
points: A college-track diploma with B+. No SAT or set prerequisites. Some AP credit. Four years.

title: International Applicants
points: Eligible for university at home with above-average grades. IB, French Baccalaureate or three A Levels: three years. Five O Levels plus a further year: four years. Others either.

title: Transfer Students
points: Normally a full year of university in Good Standing, with CGPA 3.00. Non-Music credit at C or better after review; music complementary or elective credit may need more. At least 60 credits at McGill.

title: Mature Students
points: Age 21+, Canadian or Permanent Resident, lacking academic requirements but with exceptional talent. Send all documents; an interview may be needed.

title: Special Students
points: A music bachelor's or equivalent, course prerequisites and space. Usually no lessons. One year, then apply to a program.

title: Visiting Students
points: With prerequisites and your home university's permission.

title: Application Procedures
points: Music Admissions Office, 555 Sherbrooke St. W. Apply online by January 15 for September; no January entry usually. Late applications only if space remains. Recorded auditions by February 1.

Describe your background, training and intent, with diplomas or transcripts. Music Education needs a reference on teaching potential. Upload documents in the portal; official transcripts come after a decision.

title: Licentiate in Music (L.Mus.) (All Applicants)
points: Secondary school, music at McGill Conservatory Collegial II in Instrument or Voice and Secondary V Theory/Ear Training, plus an audition. Three years; good for those with non-music degrees or changing genres before graduate study.

title: Music Entrance Requirements
points: McGill Conservatory Collegial I Instrument or Voice (Performance: Collegial II) and Secondary V Theory and Ear Training.

title: Approximate Equivalents to Entrance Requirements in Practical Subjects (McGill Conservatory Collegial I – Instrument/Voice)
points: CEGEP II; Toronto Conservatory, Western Board or Mount Allison Grade 9; Associated Board Grade 7. Only a guide; Performance applicants should be about two years ahead.

All must audition, on campus or by video, with equal chances. Composition: 2–3 scores, with mp3s if any, other composition work, and a one-page or 3-minute statement. Music Education: reasons in your Statement of Intent, and a reference. Upload in the portal.

title: Music Placement Examinations
points: New B.Mus. and L.Mus. students, and minors with prerequisites, need these for 200-level theory (MUTH, MUJZ) and musicianship (MUSP), held once a year before early June. Equivalent courses or the RCM History exam may exempt you from MUHL 186 or MUJZ 187.

title: Readmission
points: No Fall or Winter courses without a leave means you're inactive. Request readmission by the deadline; you may need to re-audition.

title: Tuition Fees, Practical Instruction Fees, and Lesson Quotas
points: MUIN courses add a Music Private Lesson Fee to tuition: a term is 13 one-hour weekly lessons. Each program caps years of lessons.
One extra year of elective lessons (MUIN 110, 111) can count as electives. A second (MUIN 210, 211) needs Performance's permission and adds a post-quota Supplemental Fee.

title: Maximum Number of Years of Practical Instruction
points: Required years, all with an optional elective year. High school graduates (U0): B.Mus. Performance 4, Composition/Education/History/Theory 2, L.Mus. 3. CEGEP, transfer, IB or French Baccalaureate, and mature students (U1): Performance 3, others 1, L.Mus. 3.

Voice Coaching (MUIN 300, 301): per credit, up to two terms, for full-time Voice students, no lesson fee. Early Music and Jazz minors pay tuition plus lesson fee. Lessons aren't in Minerva: request them yearly.

title: Academic Policies in the Schulich School of Music
points: General requirements, requirements by program, and Academic Standing.

title: General Academic Requirements
points: Be on time; grades follow the syllabus; missing exams or work without a timely valid excuse risks failure. Follow the published sequence, especially core courses, or you may lose lessons and ensembles and delay graduation.
C generally passes prerequisites; some programs need more. Keep TGPA and CGPA at 2.0 or higher.

title: Academic Requirements by Program
points: These add to the general requirements.

title: B.Mus. Composition
points: B- in all MUCO courses, or you may be advised to transfer.

title: B.Mus. Performance
points: B- in all practical instruction, exams and ensembles. One miss gets a warning; another may mean transferring.

title: B.Mus. Jazz Performance
points: B- in all MUJZ, MUIN and MUEN courses. A warning brings probation conditions; failing those may mean transferring.

title: L.Mus. Programs
points: A- in all MUIN and MUEN courses. One miss gets a warning; another may mean withdrawing.

title: Academic Standing
points: Assessed each term, with TGPA 2.0+ expected. Fall gives Interim Satisfactory or Interim Probationary, the latter with terms for Winter. Fall decisions use only January grades, without deferred or two-term courses.

title: Satisfactory/Interim Satisfactory Standing
points: New students, CGPA 2.00+, and those meeting program requirements.

title: Probationary/Interim Probationary Standing
points: You continue under set conditions; Interim students should review loads with an advisor before add/drop.

Triggers: missing program minimum grades; TGPA or CGPA under 2.00 from Satisfactory. Staying: CGPA 1.50–1.99 and TGPA 2.50+. Readmitted from Unsatisfactory: CGPA under 2.00, meeting your letter's conditions.

title: Unsatisfactory Readmitted Standing
points: After readmission by the Associate Dean; your letter sets your load and conditions.

title: Unsatisfactory/Interim Unsatisfactory Standing
points: Interim: continue, adjusting with an advisor. Unsatisfactory after breaking probation: withdraw. Appeal to the Associate Dean by the published deadlines with proof. A second time means permanent withdrawal.

title: Incomplete Standing
points: No final grades yet from deferred exams (L), extensions (K) or supplementals. You may register for Fall, but it must resolve by the end of the course change period; Unsatisfactory then stops you, with appeal by proof. Still Incomplete? See Student Affairs right away.

title: Absence Policy
points: Attend regularly and tell your instructor about absences. No note for illness under five days; one may be asked for after five consecutive days when you miss a required task. Over 20% missed may not be accommodated. For auditions or professional work, contact Student Affairs promptly.
Make up missed learning yourself. Ask Student Affairs about missed assessments, under PASL article 7. Ensemble absences have their own policy.

title: Academic Category
points: Major (B.Mus., one or more); Music Studies (cross-disciplinary, with minors or outside majors); L.Mus. (shorter, performance-focused); Special (non-degree); Visiting (credit elsewhere); Exchange (official partners).

title: Accompanist Program
points: B.Mus. and L.Mus. students in lessons on eligible instruments can request funded hours.

title: Auditing of Courses
points: No auditing for-credit courses, ensembles included, without registering. See p. 36.

title: Course Changes and Withdrawal
points: Change in Minerva during add/drop. Late changes cost a fee unless the Faculty caused them, or your registration needs correcting.
Check your section for small ensembles (MUEN 560, 570, 580) before add/drop; a wrong section means a failing J.

title: Course Withdrawal
points: MUIN and MUEN need instructor or department approval. Others in Minerva before deadlines get a W, with no CGPA effect. Refunds depend on timing.

title: Late Course Withdrawal
points: Only for extenuating circumstances, requested before that term ends.

title: Distance Education (Online) Courses
points: Up to 6 elective credits. Outside courses must come from an accredited degree-granting school, count there, be approved in the Equivalency Database, and be cleared by Student Affairs first.

title: Electives
points: Non-music, music and free. See the Electives site.

title: Music Electives
points: Any non-required Music course may count as free or music elective. Extra ensembles can count as complementary performance or electives.

title: Non-Music Electives
points: Undergraduate courses from other faculties, like French or computer science. Extras become free electives. One a term may be S/U.

title: Free Electives
points: Any mix of music and non-music.

title: Schulich School of Music Ensemble Policy and Regulations
points: Ensembles train practical musicianship throughout. Small: usually 1 credit (MUEN 540, 541, 571 are 0.5), for Performance majors, L.Mus. and Jazz and Early Music minors. Large: 2 credits, for all B.Mus. and L.Mus. Check your program; extras need approval.

Orchestral instruments: flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon, saxophone, French horn, trumpet, trombone, tuba, percussion, harp, violin, viola, cello, double bass. Voice majors use vocal and choral ensembles. "Director" includes conductor, stage director and coach. Rules apply to everyone in any ensemble.

title: Small Ensembles
points: MUEN 540, 541, 567, 569 and 571 don't meet small ensemble requirements, but can be complementary or electives. See the Ensemble or Jazz Combo sites.

title: Large Ensembles
points: New violin, viola or cello students in orchestral programs take MUEN 565 in Fall and Winter of first year. See Ensemble Auditions.

title: Ensemble Assignments and Auditions
points: Large ensembles need an audition; for small ones, ask the director. If you can't attend, tell the supervisor two weeks ahead in writing and send a recording; otherwise the department assigns you. You're told by email before rehearsals start.
Assignments may change; ask how it affects grades. Orchestral, piano, guitar or percussion students without a place may take choir or ask the Ensemble Office.

title: Commitment
points: Ensembles are courses: attend all rehearsals, concerts, trips and recordings. You get notice of extra rehearsals, which are avoided if possible.

title: Request to be Excused from a Rehearsal
points: Applies to large ensembles and MUEN 567. Tell ensembles.music@mcgill.ca of professional engagements before placement. Fill out an Absence Request Form as soon as you know. Orchestral: find your own substitute.

Maximum four absences a term (two per orchestral cycle), excused or not, and none for dress rehearsals or concerts. More keeps you out of that cycle; for illness, ask about reassignment, extra work or late withdrawal. If hurt, attend and take notes. See Student Accessibility and Achievement if needed.
Penalties without approval: up to 10 minutes late, or arriving during tuning, drops one grade point (B to B-). Absent or later drops a full letter (A to B).

Valid reasons, not guaranteed: illness, medical or dental work (email before, form within 3 days of returning); audition, master class, major competition, important engagement, family emergency or occasion, other field trip, McGill function, religious observance (email a day before, form in advance and within 48 hours). Report pain to your teacher and director, and don't perform with injury.

title: Preparation
points: If unprepared, the director warns you in writing through the supervisor and coordinator. After that you can be removed from a performance. Withdrawing for this gives an F.

title: Withdrawal from an Ensemble
points: Needs the Ensemble Office, Director or Student Affairs, and you make up the credits later.

title: Failing an Ensemble
points: Academic probation and making up the credit. Failing the same one again may mean withdrawing.

title: Exemption from a Required Ensemble in a Semester
points: For a major competition or significant voice role after minimum terms, with teacher, coordinator and director approval; or when only your final exam remains; or only non-music or free electives remain; or a significant medical reason. This doesn't satisfy credits.

title: Rotation in Large Ensembles
points: Seating may rotate for fairness, as director and coordinators decide.

title: Performance Library
points: You pay for lost or damaged music, and Minerva holds can follow.

title: Examinations, Deferrals, and Rereads
points: Governed by PASL. Talk to your instructor first.

title: Practical Examinations
points: Held in official exam periods. Final-year students finishing in Summer may request early September (MUIN 283, 482, 452), recorded as Summer, through practicalexams.music@mcgill.ca. Otherwise plan for December or April.

title: Practical Examination Marking
points: The mark averages all examiners, and at least half must pass you to advance. Minimums: L.Mus. A- (80%), B.Mus. Performance B- (65%), Concentration and performance minors C (55%). If the average passes but most fail you, you get the grade just below the minimum.
Decide readiness with your teacher, choose material, and apply on the form, as exams aren't in Minerva. Late applications cost $50, with permission.
Application / cancellation: December, October 15 / November 15. April, February 15 / March 15. Early September, May 31 / August 1. Cancel free until then. Email to cancel or defer.

title: Deferrals
points: Talk to an advisor first. Final exams: apply in Minerva; write in the deferred period; missing it gets a failing J.

Practical exams and recitals: only for serious illness or unforeseen events, not travel or colds. Apply in Minerva and email within 24 hours. December moves to next April, April to December. You get an L until done. No second deferrals; withdrawal only in exceptional cases.

title: Assessment Task Extensions
points: Ask your instructor before the deadline (PASL article 7). Past term's end you get a K and finish by an agreed date next term.

title: Rereads for Graded Assessments and Exams
points: You can see and discuss marked work (PASL). Review with your instructor, then request a third-party reread, done by an impartial academic. The grade can go up or down and stands. Ask Student Affairs for deadlines.

title: Supplemental Exams
points: Not available in Schulich courses.

title: Graduation Requirements
points: Complete all requirements for each program; C or higher in required and prerequisite courses, D only in other electives; CGPA 2.00. Residency: 60 credits for B.Mus., 48 for L.Mus. Apply to graduate.

title: Graduation Honours
points: Dean's Honour List, Distinction, and Outstanding Achievement for superior performance or scholarship.

title: Incomplete Grades
points: K is at the instructor's discretion, due within four months; then KF (failed), or KE if extended. Ks don't count toward in-course scholarships. Abandoning a course without withdrawing gets a failing J. In exceptional cases, the Associate Dean may allow KK, permanently incomplete and outside your GPA.

title: Browse Academic Units and Programs
points: Music Research: B.Mus. in Composition, Education, History, Theory and Music Studies; Minors in Applied Performance Sciences, History, Composition, Education, Entrepreneurship, Theory and Technology.
Performance: B.Mus. in Performance, Early Music and Jazz; L.Mus.; Minors in Conducting, Early Music, Jazz Arranging and Composition, and Jazz Performance. Approved for 2026–2027.

refs.label: Music Education / Music Elementary and Secondary Concurrent Major (B.Mus./B.Ed.)
Early Music Performance Major (Baroque Violin, Viola, Cello, Viola da Gamba, Flute, Recorder, Oboe, Organ, Harpsichord and Early Brass Instruments) (B.Mus.)
Performance Major (All Instruments except Piano, Voice and Jazz) (L.Mus.)

title: Department of Music Research
points: Links applied performance sciences, composition, education, history, theory, technology and recording, treating musicianship, musical grammar and ideas as connected. Majors allow other interests; Music Studies suits individual plans. Analysis and writing skills also prepare you for law, journalism, management or librarianship.

The B.Mus./B.Ed. (170 credits) and Minor in Music Education (18) won't admit students in 2026–2027 during a review; admissions can suggest alternatives like Music Studies. Several minors are open to other faculties. Listed courses are required unless noted.

refs.label: Music Education / Music Elementary and Secondary Concurrent Major (B.Mus./B.Ed.)

title: Prerequisite Courses for M.Mus. in Sound Recording
points: Finish prerequisites before applying, and tell the Sound Recording Area first. Bachelor's students are encouraged to take them through the Musical Science and Technology Minor (p. 1032). See the program's site.

title: B.Mus./B.Ed. Bachelor of Music and Bachelor of Education Concurrent Program
points: Neither education program is accepting applications. The B.Ed. Music is 152 credits of teacher training toward Quebec certification, for B.Mus. holders, typically 2.5 years with Advanced Standing, through Education.

Without a B.Mus.: the 170-credit concurrent program (p. 1027), usually five years, with both degrees at one convocation, through Schulich. An F or J in Field Experience means Unsatisfactory Standing and withdrawal after finishing the term.

title: Program Description
points: Performance science for music practice, creation and teaching: optimal performance, healthy playing and singing, physical, psychological and social factors, and applied research.

title: Interdisciplinary courses
points: 3 credits, when the topic is relevant.

title: Program Description
points: Classical composition for instruments and voices, with or without electronics, through lectures and private lessons in years 3 and 4, plus theory and history. Free electives allow a minor or breadth. B- minimum in Composition Area courses.

title: Prerequisite Courses
points: 22 credits. Auditions, placement tests or equivalents can exempt you.

title: McGill University Designated Teaching Hospitals
points: Teaching hospitals are closely tied to McGill and form its clinical departments.

McGill University Health Centre (MUHC): merged teaching hospitals giving advanced bilingual adult and pediatric care. Yearly: 519,000+ ambulatory visits, 32,600+ inpatients, 29,600+ surgeries, 2,800+ births. Sites: Glen (1001 Decarie Blvd.: Children's, Royal Victoria, Chest Institute, Cedars Cancer Centre); Montreal General (1650 Cedar Ave.); The Neuro (3801 University St.); Lachine Hospital (650 16th Ave.); CHSLD Camille-Lefebvre (637, 13e Ave.); Reproductive Centre (888 de Maisonneuve E., Suite 200); Adult Ophthalmology Clinic (5252 de Maisonneuve W.).

17,000+ people across seven missions: Medicine, Surgery, Neurosciences, Mental Health, Women's Health, Cancer Care, Children's. In 2024–2025: 3,793 nursing and related staff, 2,098 other health professionals, 3,493 research members, 1,414 physicians, 150 pharmacists, 339 managers, 2,237 office staff, 2,531 paratechnical and trades, 863 volunteers. Every physician is a McGill professor. It trains 5,200+ a year: 1,000+ residents, 2,500 nursing, 980 medical and 700 others.

Research Institute of the MUHC: 744 researchers, 1,490+ trainees and 1,476 staff, at Glen and the General, partly FRQS funded; rimuhc.ca. The MUHC is also the server lab for Montreal's OPTILAB cluster.

Jewish General Hospital (CIUSSS West-Central, 3755 Côte Ste-Catherine Rd.): since 1934, 637 beds. Yearly 22,000+ admissions, about 592,000 outpatient and 92,000+ emergency visits, 3,600+ births, 12,000+ surgeries. Known for oncology (Segal Cancer Centre), cardiology, neonatology, orthopedics, family medicine, aging and emergency. A Quebec centre for high-risk obstetrics and breast referral, and an early COVID-19 hospital. About 850 doctors and 300+ residents. Hosts McGill's Wainberg Centre for Viral Diseases and translational cancer, head and neck, and menopause programs. Its Lady Davis Institute leads in cancer, aging, epidemiology, nursing, cardiovascular, genetics and more.

St. Mary's Hospital Center (CIUSSS West Island, 3830 Lacombe Ave.): 271 adult beds, university-affiliated. In 2024–2025, 3,551+ births; first Montreal hospital with WHO Baby Friendly recognition. Family medicine, dialysis, oncology, geriatrics, imaging. Yearly 104,509+ clinic visits, 7,113 day surgeries, 14,489+ admissions. Its Research Centre covers cancer, surgery, older adults and primary care.

Douglas Mental Health University Institute (CIUSSS West Island, 6875 LaSalle Blvd.): founded in 1881, WHO-affiliated, for child, adult and geriatric care with a focus on rehabilitation and community. 134,589+ interventions yearly. One of Canada's largest mental health research centres, with 64 scientists and 450+ students in 2024–2025, and McGill centres on schizophrenia, aging and suicide, plus a PAHO/WHO Collaborating Centre.

points: Instruction is in English, but most Québec clinical placements need English and French, so build skills early.

title: Vaccination/Immunization Requirements for Health Sciences Programs
points: Compulsory: begin once accepted, finish well before patient contact, with proof signed by a nurse or physician. No exceptions; otherwise you're asked to withdraw. Influenza and others may be required.
D.M.D., General Practice Residency and Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery applicants are tested for Hepatitis B. A positive "e" antigen or viral DNA result withdraws the offer.

Students seropositive for Hepatitis B, C, HIV or other blood-borne pathogens must tell the Dean or Director, and follow the provincial service's recommendations, which may restrict procedures and could mean withdrawing. Those who know they carry such pathogens should weigh this carefully.
With a contagious disease that risks patients, tell your supervisor; you may have to pause clinical work.

Medicine and Dentistry have further UGME policies, and Nursing its own list. Physical and Occupational Therapy need complete records and a mask fitting before the first clinical course, with a card submitted by the third clinical seminar.
