points: C passes in B.Sc.(N.) and B.N.(I). See p. 53.

title: Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory (S/U option)
points: Electives only, one a term, not required or complementary courses. Best for upper-level courses. Most awards need 27 graded credits. Once S/U, no grade can be assigned. See p. 36.

title: Standing in Undergraduate Nursing Programs
points: Satisfactory for U1–U3: CGPA 2.0+, at most 7 credits failed in non-clinical courses, no failed clinical courses (NUR1 230–236, 331–339, 431–435, 529–531), at most one clinical course at B or below or minimally meeting objectives, and professional behaviour under the Quebec Code of Ethics of Nurses, McGill's Code and the Faculty Code.
U0: CGPA 2.0+ and at most three failures, reset on entering U1. Otherwise the Committee decides, weighing your pattern, circumstances, reason for clinical failure and any code violations.

title: Probationary Standing
points: When allowed to continue with: CGPA 1.5–1.99 within allowed failures from Satisfactory; at most three U0 failures; or TGPA 2.5+ after Probation. Also an exceptional second weak clinical course, professional lapses with provisions, or readmission.
Maximum 14 credits a term. Keep TGPA 2.5 and reach CGPA 2.0 by the end of next year, plus any Committee conditions. See NSAO.

title: Unsatisfactory Standing
points: You must withdraw from the program, though you may be fine elsewhere at McGill; see NSAO.

Triggers: CGPA under 1.5; too many failures without permission; after Probation, TGPA under 2.5 with CGPA under 2.0 or unmet conditions; failed clinical without a repeat; unprofessional conduct or code violations without permission to continue; unsuitability for nursing; OIIQ license revoked; or no clinical access because of a criminal offence.

title: Interim Standings
points: After one term below Satisfactory. Continue, at 14 credits at most, with your advisor's review.

title: Clinical Support
points: Supports learning and patient safety; on your School file, not Minerva. Triggered by B to C or minimal performance in a clinical course, professionalism concerns, two or more terms away from clinical work, or a permitted clinical repeat.
Continue under a learning plan with coordinators; not progressing means an F. Only one in your program, apart from absence notices.

title: Appeals
points: Only decisions of Unsatisfactory or required withdrawal. Write to the Committee within 14 days with reasons and documents. Further appeals go to the Associate Dean and Director. See the Handbook.

title: Readmission – Unsatisfactory Readmit
points: Apply one year after leaving, in Minerva, or to NSAO if still at McGill, with a compelling letter and documents. It depends on resolving the causes, your capacity and seats, and you get one request. Courses on weak areas are recommended. You may have to restart nursing after poor results or a gap over a year. Applying within a year of withdrawal gets priority.

title: Examinations
points: University rules apply; see p. 62 and the Handbook.

title: Supplemental Examinations
points: For D, J, F or U with CGPA 2.0+ and Satisfactory Standing; apply in Minerva, NSAO decides. None after a deferred exam: re-register or substitute. At most two in the program, except specially.
Worth the original exam's weight or 100%, and may differ, so ask. Both grades count in your CGPA, and a failed supplemental counts as a failure. If you can't write it, repeat the course.

title: Deferred Examinations
points: Missed midterms for illness, crisis or religious observance: the instructor may reschedule, set alternative work, shift the weight, or give an alternate final.

Missed finals: apply in Minerva with documents by January 15 (Fall), May 15 (Winter) or July 15 (Summer). Summer courses like CHEM 212 have none. NSAO decides; you see an L. Free, written at the next chance: reading week for Fall, mid-August for Winter. If you can't, contact NSAO for WL; otherwise you get J, counted as zero.

title: Reassessments and Rereads
points: You can see and discuss marked work and get an impartial review. Evaluation details come in the first two weeks.

Reassessment: free, through NSAO, within 10 working days; a reviewer checks fairness, not regrades. Reread: written, for a fee; the grade can rise, fall or stay. Deadlines: March 31 (Fall), July 31 (Winter), August 31 (May). Computer-marked exams can only be reassessed.
One course a term. Not for supplementals or clinical courses, where you talk with your teacher and coordinator, with no formal appeal. Other faculties' rules apply to their courses.

title: Procedures Governing Reassessment/ Rereads
points: Reassessment is free; final exam and paper rereads cost a fee. Computer-marked exams can't be reread.

title: Time to Degree Completion
points: B.Sc.(N.) from U1: three years with summers, four at most. From U0: four, five at most. B.N.I.: two full-time or three part-time, four at most. Changes need the Program Director's approval and documented reasons.

title: Leave of Absence (LOA)
points: For maternity or parenting, health, or professional or military service, term by term, up to 52 weeks, through NSAO with documents. No tuition; you keep your ID, mail and libraries. Not for travel or money. Usually needs Satisfactory Standing.

Student Services can be opted into. Scholarships pause but stay renewable. Check loan rules with Student Aid; international students see ISS. Not returning after a year means withdrawing, with possible restart.
Return your certificate to the OIIQ on any interruption; it's returned free within a year. After that, register again with documents and fee.

title: Academic Integrity
points: See p. 22.

title: Pregnancy and Nursing Clinical Studies
points: Contact the Clinical Partnership Office. Some settings are excluded, such as OR, emergency, ICU, post-anesthesia, pediatrics and some psychiatric agencies. Follow your care provider; suitable placement isn't guaranteed, and graduation may be delayed.

title: Clinical Studies Portal Document Uploads Required
points: B.Sc.(N.) and B.N.(I) students must also meet the following.

title: OIIQ Registration
points: All students need an OIIQ license. See p. 33.

title: Faculty of Medicine and Health Sciences' Code of Conduct
points: Everyone must read it. Deadlines are on the clinical student portal.

title: Vaccination/Immunization Requirements
points: See p. 24. Yearly flu shots are mandatory. Complete immunizations (Hepatitis B in progress is fine) by your first clinical year: U1 for B.Sc.(N.), U2 for B.N.I., or you can't enter teaching hospitals.

title: Mask Fitting Requirements
points: Before NUR1 331 or 434, through Student Health Services, valid two years. If a mask can't fit, tell your instructor.

title: CPR
points: Keep CPR Health Care Provider certification throughout. The School often runs sessions.

title: SafeTALK
points: A mandatory half-day suicide alertness course for B.Sc.(N.) U1 and B.N.I. U2. Proof required; exemptions with prior certification or experience.

title: HSP net Authorization
points: The BC-run Health Sciences Placement Network coordinates placements. You must authorize use and disclosure of your name and profile, and use of your health information, for placements.

title: Flu Vaccine
points: Show proof each year.

title: Co-op Work Permit (International Students)
points: Practical work is mandatory, so non-citizens and non-residents need a co-op work permit as well as a study permit, paid or not, before clinical work. Apply with your admission letter, the program's co-op letter, an international student letter and a medical exam. See International Student Services.

title: Criminal Background Verification
points: Agencies need a self-declaration or formal check; no access means you can't meet course requirements. The OIIQ needs offences declared, and must be told of accusations during studies. Without a student license you can't continue.

title: Clinical Courses
points: Professional behaviour is expected always under the OIIQ Code, Faculty Code and McGill Code, with mandatory professionalism and interprofessional seminars. Register with the OIIQ first. Identify yourself as a McGill Nursing Student in charts, wear the badge (charged to your account), and follow uniform rules.

Attendance is mandatory; repeat absences may defer your clinical work. If below expectations you make a learning plan; if unsafe you leave the course with an F and meet the Program Director. Buy a stethoscope and equipment, and budget for travel. Expect days, evenings, nights and weekends.

Placements aren't by student choice, except NUR1 435, 530 and 531, and if you or close family work there, you've been a patient there, or SERTIH has limits. Blood-borne infections must be reported to your Program Director and go to SERTIH.

Outside the McGill network (NUR1 435, 531 only): Satisfactory Standing and CGPA 3.2+, some higher, judged on proposal, autonomy, progress and interviews. B.N.(I) students finish all U2 Fall and Winter courses before NUR1 434 or 435.

refs.label: Clinical courses must be taken sequentially as identified in the course of study (Bachelor of Science (Nursing) (B.Sc.(N.)) - Nursing (103 credits) (p. 1080) and Bachelor of Nursing (B.N.I.) -

title: Inter-University Transfer (IUT) Agreement
points: 3, or exceptionally 6, credits at another Quebec university while paying McGill, in Satisfactory Standing, through BCI. Follow the host's rules. C or better counts as pass, with no GPA effect; failures show as failures. Required courses must be equivalent. See p. 39.

title: Study Away
points: For courses outside Quebec, in Satisfactory Standing, usually U0's CHEM 212 at home, or an equivalent elective or required course. C minimum.

Steps: confirm it's outside Quebec; check the Course Equivalency System or request assessment; confirm the course runs and you qualify; avoid your graduating term. Apply in Minerva, and register at McGill too as a backup, dropping it later if all goes well.
Then register at the host, have the official transcript sent to NSAO whatever the grade, and check Minerva. Cancel in Minerva if you change your mind.

title: Registration with the Profession (Immatriculation or Licensing during the Course of Study)
points: Quebec law requires it ("immatriculation"), through the OIIQ. Patient access needs a Student Permit (B.Sc.(N.) and nurse practitioner students) or registered nurse status (B.N.I. after the exam).

B.N.I. students who pass must pay OIIQ fees, pro-rated then yearly, with no waiver, or they can't be in clinical settings. Carry proof in all clinical work, since patients, teachers and agents can ask.

You may do nurses' activities needed for your program, except adjusting the therapeutic nursing plan, supervised by a nurse who is present (O.C. 551-2010). Chart with your signature followed by "student n.", printing your name if unclear.

The OIIQ may revoke it after over a year out of the program, if you fail or are expelled, obtained it falsely, or act beyond what's allowed or against ethics. Interrupting suspends it; over a year revokes it.

title: Requirements for Licensure (Entry into the Nursing Profession)
points: OIIQ: 4200 Rue Molson, H1Y 4V4. It runs the professional exam. If you finished English high school before 1986, you pass the French Proficiency exam (OQLF, Charter article 35), available in your last two years. Not needed with a Quebec diploma after 1986 or three full-time years in French.

The OIIQ exam is approved under Canada's Mutual Recognition Agreement, so taking it helps; agreements change. Elsewhere, you're generally licensed where you trained first, may write more exams, and should contact the regulator early, especially international students.

title: Undergraduate Programs
points: B.N.I.: for DEC 180.A.0 holders, within three years of the DEC, on campus or online. B.Sc.(N.): for CEGEP Health or Natural Sciences or equivalent, for entry to practice.

title: Bachelor of Science (Nursing) (B.Sc.(N.)) - Nursing (103 credits)
points: Three years, or four with U0 sciences for high school graduates and mature students without science. Summer sessions included. Clinical work in community centres, hospitals, agencies and homes.

title: Bachelor of Nursing (B.N.I.) - Integrated Nursing (65 credits)
points: Part of a five-year Quebec plan, for 180.A.0 and 180.A.1 graduates, with 27 credits of Advanced Standing. Two university years, or three part-time, on advanced nursing and science, teamwork or autonomous practice with individuals, families and groups, health education and research. Online suits independent learners.

title: Minor Degrees
points: From units like Women's Studies or Psychology, generally 18–24 credits, most suited to transfers. Submit the form to NSAO; it's in the Handbook.

title: Program Accreditation
points: Both are fully accredited by the Canadian Association of Schools of Nursing.

title: Graduate Programs
points: M.Sc.A. concentrations: Advanced Clinical Practice, Direct Entry Nursing, Global Health, Global Health Direct Entry, and Mental Health, Neonatology, Pediatrics and Primary Care Nurse Practitioner, and Nursing Services Administration. Nurses with bachelor's degrees take the non-direct-entry ones. B.A. or B.Sc. graduates without nursing take Direct Entry, unique in Canada.

Certificates: Theory in Neonatology, Theory in Primary Care. Diplomas: Mental Health, Neonatal, Pediatrics and Primary Care Nurse Practitioner. For licensed nurses with a bachelor's and two years' experience in the field.
Ph.D. for researchers, academics and leaders, requiring master's study and a nursing degree.

title: B.Sc.(N.) Entrance Requirements
points: Detailed information about each admission category can be found at mcgill.ca/applying/requirements.

title: Quebec Diploma of Collegial Studies (Health Sciences/ Sciences)
points: For the 103-credit program: Biology NYA, General Biology II (00UK, 00XU); Chemistry NYA, NYB, Organic I (00UL, 00UM, 00XV); Math NYA, NYB (00UN, 00UP); Physics NYA, NYB, NYC (00UR, 00US, 00UT). Based on overall and prerequisite Cote R.

title: Mature Students
points: Age 23+, Canadian or Permanent Resident, with functions (calculus preferred) and two of biology, chemistry or physics with labs, at CEGEP or university, 70% or equivalent. See CEGEP advisors. Admits you to the 136-credit, four-year program, with no repeat of equivalent courses.

title: Applicants from Ontario
points: OSSD; usually the four-year program. MCV4U, two of SBI4U, SCH4U or SPH4U, and 4U English or French. Based on "Top 6" 4U and 4M courses, at least four 4U, and all prerequisites at 4U. All grades count. Most applied courses are excluded; up to two 4M arts are allowed.

title: Applicants from Canadian High Schools outside of Quebec and Ontario
points: A university-access diploma; usually four years. Grade 12 precalculus, two of Biology, Chemistry or Physics, and English or French. Based on "Top 5" Grade 12 courses, with all grades counted.

title: Applicants from other Universities or Colleges and Second Bachelor Degree applicants (Transfer Students)
points: Judged on pre-university and university work; 60 credits at McGill. Needs two calculus terms, two biology, two general chemistry, one organic, and two physics, with labs. At minimum, two calculus plus two of biology, chemistry or physics, finishing the rest in the program. Past degrees may give equivalence, especially Physiology and Pharmacology. Science and math must be within five years.

title: Applicants from the U.S. High School Programs (in the U.S. or other countries)
points: A college-track diploma with precalculus and two of Biology, Chemistry or Physics. SAT IIs in two of Biology, Chemistry, Math or Physics. Grades 10–12 count, especially relevant ones.

title: Applicants from outside Canada or the U.S.
points: Strong senior math and science; usually four years. Proof of English may be needed: TOEFL 233 (577 paper) or others. See mcgill.ca/applying/requirements.

title: Inter-Faculty Transfer Students (McGill University students)
points: Apply in Minerva. Satisfactory Standing and normally CGPA 2.70, 3.0 preferred.

title: Holders of a Bachelor's Degree
points: With a general Science or Arts degree by August 1, ask Service Point or the Welcome Centre. You may apply to the B.Sc.(N.) through Enrolment Services, or the Master's Qualifying Year through the School.

title: B.N. (Integrated) Entrance Requirements
points: DEC 180A.0 and 180A.1, within three years, based on overall and prerequisite Cote R. Follow the course sequence unless your advisor agrees.

title: Application Procedures
points: McGill's online application, with two program choices and a non-refundable fee, no waivers.

title: Application Deadlines
points: Fall: January 15 from outside Canada; February 1 from other Canadian schools and Quebec B.Sc.(N.) applicants; March 1 otherwise, including B.N.I. Winter, if open: November 1. No Summer. Special, Exchange and Visiting match Canadian or International dates.

title: Location
points: 680 Sherbrooke St. W., Suite 1800, H3A 2M7.

title: Program Description
points: 3–4 years with summers, on contemporary nursing issues, core skills and critical thinking. Qualifies you for licensing exams in Quebec, Canada and elsewhere. CASN accredited.

title: U0 Required Courses (27 credits)
points: The first year of the 136- or 137-credit four-year program.

title: U0 Complementary Courses (6 or 7 credits)
points: One calculus course and a 3-credit elective, then you enter U1.

title: Program Description
points: Online or on campus; register in the courses for the mode you were admitted to. See the School's B.N.I. page and p. 1078.

title: School of Physical and Occupational Therapy
points: On McGill's upper campus: educates rehabilitation professionals, and researches how to improve health, function and participation.

title: Occupational Therapy
points: Uses occupation as therapy to improve health-related quality of life for people with injury, disability or psychosocial problems, from infancy to old age. In mental health, it helps clarify functional diagnosis and supports coping and community life. See the Canadian Association of Occupational Therapists.

title: Physical Therapy
points: An autonomous, primary care profession that improves function, prevents and manages pain and impairment, and promotes fitness. Uses exercise, modalities, manual therapy, devices and lifestyle changes, in clinics, industry and the community.

title: Location
points: 3630 prom. Sir-William-Osler, H3G 1Y5.

title: Health Sciences: General Information
points: Adds health sciences details to the University Regulations: language, immunization, immigration and facilities. Your faculty may add more.

title: Admission
points: See each faculty's section.

title: Facilities
points: Facilities linked with McGill's health sciences.

title: Buildings
points: See the Building Directory for the six Schools, Centres and units.

title: McGill University Designated Teaching Hospitals
points: Teaching hospitals are closely tied to McGill and form its clinical departments.

McGill University Health Centre (MUHC): merged teaching hospitals giving advanced bilingual adult and pediatric care. Yearly: 519,000+ ambulatory visits, 32,600+ inpatients, 29,600+ surgeries, 2,800+ births. Sites: Glen (1001 Decarie Blvd.: Children's, Royal Victoria, Chest Institute, Cedars Cancer Centre); Montreal General (1650 Cedar Ave.); The Neuro (3801 University St.); Lachine Hospital (650 16th Ave.); CHSLD Camille-Lefebvre (637, 13e Ave.); Reproductive Centre (888 de Maisonneuve E., Suite 200); Adult Ophthalmology Clinic (5252 de Maisonneuve W.).

17,000+ people across seven missions: Medicine, Surgery, Neurosciences, Mental Health, Women's Health, Cancer Care, Children's. In 2024–2025: 3,793 nursing and related staff, 2,098 other health professionals, 3,493 research members, 1,414 physicians, 150 pharmacists, 339 managers, 2,237 office staff, 2,531 paratechnical and trades, 863 volunteers. Every physician is a McGill professor. It trains 5,200+ a year: 1,000+ residents, 2,500 nursing, 980 medical and 700 others.

Research Institute of the MUHC: 744 researchers, 1,490+ trainees and 1,476 staff, at Glen and the General, partly FRQS funded; rimuhc.ca. The MUHC is also the server lab for Montreal's OPTILAB cluster.

Jewish General Hospital (CIUSSS West-Central, 3755 Côte Ste-Catherine Rd.): since 1934, 637 beds. Yearly 22,000+ admissions, about 592,000 outpatient and 92,000+ emergency visits, 3,600+ births, 12,000+ surgeries. Known for oncology (Segal Cancer Centre), cardiology, neonatology, orthopedics, family medicine, aging and emergency. A Quebec centre for high-risk obstetrics and breast referral, and an early COVID-19 hospital. About 850 doctors and 300+ residents. Hosts McGill's Wainberg Centre for Viral Diseases and translational cancer, head and neck, and menopause programs. Its Lady Davis Institute leads in cancer, aging, epidemiology, nursing, cardiovascular, genetics and more.

St. Mary's Hospital Center (CIUSSS West Island, 3830 Lacombe Ave.): 271 adult beds, university-affiliated. In 2024–2025, 3,551+ births; first Montreal hospital with WHO Baby Friendly recognition. Family medicine, dialysis, oncology, geriatrics, imaging. Yearly 104,509+ clinic visits, 7,113 day surgeries, 14,489+ admissions. Its Research Centre covers cancer, surgery, older adults and primary care.

Douglas Mental Health University Institute (CIUSSS West Island, 6875 LaSalle Blvd.): founded in 1881, WHO-affiliated, for child, adult and geriatric care with a focus on rehabilitation and community. 134,589+ interventions yearly. One of Canada's largest mental health research centres, with 64 scientists and 450+ students in 2024–2025, and McGill centres on schizophrenia, aging and suicide, plus a PAHO/WHO Collaborating Centre.

title: Institutions Affiliated with McGill University
points: Since Quebec's 2015 reform, hospitals are grouped in CIUSSS or CISSS, and affiliation contracts are with these. Affiliated: MUHC; CIUSSS West Island; CIUSSS West-Central; CISSS Montérégie-Ouest; CISSS Laval; CISSS Outaouais; Shriners Hospitals for Children – Canada.

title: Clinical Facilities for Dentistry
points: The Undergraduate Teaching Dental Clinic is at Place Mercantile, 2001 McGill College Ave., Suite 100, where students train daily under staff guidance.

title: Facilities for Human Nutrition
points: Clinical Nutrition Research Unit, Macdonald Campus, since 1995: a 5,000 sq. ft. building for in-patient studies with controlled diets, unique in Canada. Body composition and sample tools, an exercise area, research kitchen and dining observation room, sensory food lab, data lab, and Canada's first food pharmacy. Self-funded; outside researchers contact the Director of Human Nutrition.

title: Research Centres
points: Alan Edwards Centre for Research on Pain: Duff Medical, 3775 University St., Suite 100. Centre de recherche en biologie structurale: Bellini, Room 435. Reproduction and Development: Glen, E-M0.3509. Brain, Language and Music: 2001 McGill College, 6th floor. Cystic Fibrosis Translational Research: McIntyre, Room 1014A.

Artificial Cells, Blood Substitutes and Nanomedicine network: McIntyre, Room 1004. J.D. MacLean Centre for Tropical and Geographic Medicine: Glen. Ludmer Centre for Neuroinformatics and Mental Health: 1010 Sherbrooke St. W., Suite 1210. Mark Wainberg Centre for Viral Diseases: Lady Davis Institute, Room F-318.

Climate Change and Health: 2001 McGill College, Suite 1177. Microbiome Research: Duff and RI-MUHC. Research in Neuroscience: Montreal General, L7-132. Translational Research in Cancer: Lady Davis Institute. International TB Centre (WHO collaborator): 5252 de Maisonneuve W. Cannabis Research. Studies in Aging: 6825 LaSalle Blvd., Verdun. Complex Traits: Bellini.

title: Research Institutes
points: Institute of Health Sciences Education: Lady Meredith House, 1110 Pine Ave. W., Room 205. Rosalind and Morris Goodman Cancer Institute: 1160 Pine Ave. W. The Neuro: 3801 University St. Victor Phillip Dahdaleh Institute of Genomic Medicine: 740 Doctor Penfield Ave.

title: Libraries
points: All McGill libraries and e-resources are open to faculty, staff and students; see mcgill.ca/libraries.
Schulich (physical and life sciences, engineering): Macdonald-Stewart Library Building, 809 Sherbrooke St. W., entered through Frank Dawson Adams's west lobby, with liaison librarians.
Osler Library of the History of Medicine: opened in 1929 with 8,000 rare works from Sir William Osler, now about 100,000, Canada's finest such collection. McIntyre, 3rd floor.
Macdonald Campus Library: Barton Building, 21,111 Lakeshore Rd., for agriculture, food, animal and plant science, nutrition, environment and bioresource engineering.

title: Fees: Health Sciences
points: Updated March 2026 and may change. See p. 44 and the Student Accounts Fee Calculator.

title: General Fees
points: Application: $136.08 for undergraduate programs, $190.51 for Medicine and Dentistry. Reconsideration: $40. Prepayment: Dentistry $500, Pre-Dentistry $400, Medicine $500.

title: Communication Sciences and Disorders Fees
points: Fee Amount M.Sc.A. ID Badge – First Year $39.78

title: Dentistry — Purchases of Equipment and Materials Fee
points: Equipment and supplies billed on your e-bill, estimated for 2026–2027: first year $400, second $17,000, third $4,100, fourth $2,500. Your August e-bill gives the breakdown.

title: Dentistry Extra Fees
points: White coat about $35. Supplemental or reread exam request $45.16 each.

title: Dental Clinic/Lab Maintenance and Improvement Fee (as of 2026–2027)
points: Fee Amount Second Year $1,317 Third and Fourth Years $2,634

title: Dentistry — Laptops
points: Courseware and exams are online, so a laptop meeting minimum requirements is required.

title: Dentistry and Medicine — Microscopes
points: A binocular microscope is provided in first and second year.

title: Medicine Fees
points: Books, lab materials, dissection kit, stethoscope and so on: about $1,500–$2,000 over the program. White coat about $50. CMQ registration $130 at the start of first year (September 30). Police check $115 on admission.

title: Medicine Extra Fees
points: Vaccines free at a CLSC. French Medical Workshop $385 per course, recommended, as all need working French for rotations. MCCQE $1,500, USMLE $1,600 USD (optional), CaRMS $300.

title: Medicine — Laptops
points: A laptop meeting minimum requirements for all four years.

title: Nursing Fees
points: Books, uniform, stethoscope: about $2,500–$3,500. Graduation pins $80–$200. Name badge about $26. OIIQ about $250. Transit to sites about $100 a month. Clinical Skills Kit varies.

title: Physical and Occupational Therapy Fees
points: Fee Amount Books and Other Equipment $1,000 Laboratory Materials approximately $80.00

title: Immigration Information
points: Non-Canadians studying six months or more need Québec and federal authorization before coming, starting with McGill's acceptance letter. Nursing students also need a co-op work permit. ISS sends a pamphlet and Handbook. Brown Building, Suite 5100.

title: Student Advising
points: Seek out advice actively. Your records, course choices, requirements and deadlines are ultimately your responsibility.

title: Your advisor
points: A faculty or staff member who guides you on academic and other concerns, workload, careers and difficulties, and links you to other resources. Nursing: see your Student Handbook.

title: Related Services
points: See p. 79 and p. 81.

title: Language Policy
points: Instruction is in English, but most Québec clinical placements need English and French, so build skills early.
Dentistry: working knowledge of both. Dietetics: both, with French proof for admission.
Medicine: English in Montréal, French at Campus Outaouais; working French from the start, with no alternative placements. You may be assigned a year-long clerkship in Gatineau or rural sites.

Nursing: written work in either language, French proficiency required for B.Sc.(N.) and Qualifying Year. Physical and Occupational Therapy: both needed; without French, fewer placements and possibly delayed graduation.

title: Proof of Proficiency in English
points: Not needed if English is your first language, you did Secondary V and a DCS in Québec, or studied five+ years in English.
Otherwise: TOEFL 90 iBT or 577 paper (varies), McGill Certificate of Proficiency, IELTS 6.5, MELAB 85%, or APIEL 4.

title: Proof of Proficiency in French
points: Clinical work requires French to learn safely and support patients. Essential for several Nursing degrees.
Physical and Occupational Therapy: all sites need both languages under the Charter of the French Language, so reach an appropriate level before placements.

title: Vaccination/Immunization Requirements for Health Sciences Programs
points: Compulsory: begin once accepted, finish well before patient contact, with proof signed by a nurse or physician. No exceptions; otherwise you're asked to withdraw. Influenza and others may be required.
D.M.D., General Practice Residency and Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery applicants are tested for Hepatitis B. A positive "e" antigen or viral DNA result withdraws the offer.

Students seropositive for Hepatitis B, C, HIV or other blood-borne pathogens must tell the Dean or Director, and follow the provincial service's recommendations, which may restrict procedures and could mean withdrawing. Those who know they carry such pathogens should weigh this carefully.
With a contagious disease that risks patients, tell your supervisor; you may have to pause clinical work.

Medicine and Dentistry have further UGME policies, and Nursing its own list. Physical and Occupational Therapy need complete records and a mask fitting before the first clinical course, with a card submitted by the third clinical seminar.

title: Undergraduate Prizes and Awards
points: (Eligibility subject to change)

title: McGill Alumnae Society Prize
points: At graduation, for excellence and high standing, preferring women.

title: Patricia Ann MacDonald Wells Van Daele Memorial Award
points: Since 2003, for professional program students or Rehabilitation Science master's students, for a project on aging or clinical education.

title: Women Associates of McGill Scholarship
points: On high standing, after a year of the B.Sc., preferring women.

title: Continuing Students
points: Up to the top 10% in each faculty make the Dean's Honour List, on combined Fall and Winter GPA. No money, but on your transcript.

title: Graduating Students
points: Dean's Honour List with at least 60 McGill credits and a CGPA in your faculty's top 10%. All awards are in the Calendars.

title: Degree Requirements for the B.Sc. (Rehabilitation Science) in Physical Therapy and the B.Sc. (Rehabilitation Science)in Occupational Therapy
points: 90 credits, all courses passed, Satisfactory Standing and a curriculum CGPA of 2.3. Full-time because courses are sequential. Rules may change, generally not mid-year.
Promotion periods: U1 and U2, September to end of August; U3, September to end of April.

title: Admission Requirements for the M.Sc. (Applied) in Physical Therapy or M.Sc. (Applied) in Occupational Therapy
points: Practice requires the M.Sc.A. in the same discipline. With CGPA 3.0+ you may be considered, starting in Summer after graduating, but it isn't guaranteed: three or more performance flags, or insufficient progress on skills, may block you.
Without this B.Sc., apply through a graduate Qualifying Year, or do the B.Sc. first.

title: Course Change and Withdrawal Policy for Physical and Occupational Therapy
points: See pp. 34. Programs are structured, so the Program Director approves changes. OCC1, PHTH and POTH courses are only for the School's students; leaving the program means leaving them.

You must start any withdrawal yourself in Minerva; telling instructors or stopping attendance doesn't count. After add/drop, drop complementary or elective courses by the deadline, or a missed exam gives J, which counts as zero permanently.
After the no-refund deadline, only in exceptional cases and not for poor work, you get W or WF, outside your GPA. If Minerva blocks an approved drop, get forms from Student Affairs.

refs.label: Fee refunds, if any, will be in accordance with Fees and Withdrawal from the University

title: University Withdrawal
points: See p. 40, and talk to the Program Director and Student Affairs first. If you registered but won't attend, you must drop within deadlines.
If required to withdraw, or if you abandon studies, the School proceeds and you can't be readmitted to either program. It may dismiss anyone judged incompetent or unsuitable at any time.

refs.label: Fee refunds, if any, for the term in which the student withdraws, will be in accordance with Fees and Withdrawal from the University
Upon withdrawal students are required to return their ID card to the University, as stated in Identification (ID) Cards

title: Credit System for Physical and Occupational Therapy Students
points: The letter grade is official, and class averages show on transcripts. See pp. 52–53 and the Rules and Regulations.

title: Satisfactory / Unsatisfactory Option
points: Can't be used for required courses, so normally not available.

title: General Information
points: See p. 62 and PASL.

title: Final Examinations
points: No mark is final until the Promotions and Review Committee (OTPRC or PTPRC) approves it and it's on your transcript; grades then appear in Minerva. See also pp. 22, 1002.

title: Interim Class Tests and Mid-Term Examinations
points: Requirements are given by the end of week one. No in-term tasks in the last 10 working days, except take-homes given 15+ working days before classes end, and tasks worth 10% or less. Missing midterms, labs or interprofessional sessions needs the Program Director's approval, possibly with documents.

title: Supplemental Examinations
points: With committee permission, after a failure. OCC1, PHTH and POTH: timed by the instructor, within 30 days of grades if feasible, or official periods. Campus courses: March and August. Apply in Minerva. Both marks count in your GPA.

title: Deferred Examinations
points: For serious reasons, with the Program Director's permission, at the next deferred period. Apply in Minerva, tell Student Affairs quickly, and send documents within a week. No supplemental after failing a deferred exam: re-register or substitute with committee permission.

title: Inter-University Transfer (IUT) and Transfer Credit Policies for Physical and Occupational Therapy Students
points: Needs the Program Director's approval first. Courses must match in content and evaluation, per the Course Equivalency System, without overlaps. See p. 39 and Student Affairs. Exchanges: see Rules and Regulations.

The host's letter grade rules and must meet program minimums, but stays off your transcript and GPA. To drop, use the host's method and update the IUT application. Outside Quebec, have an official transcript sent to Student Affairs; late ones move you to the next graduation.

title: Physical and Occupational Therapy Student Promotions
points: The OTPRC and PTPRC review records, conduct and performance, with final say on suitability, promotion and graduation. Read all program documents, updated yearly: Important Information, Rules and Regulations, Curriculum, Code of Conduct, and Required Skills and Attributes.
Full-time unless the committee allows part-time in writing. Only Minerva grades are official, not myCourses. Finish each promotion period before the next; at most one repeat.
C+ minimum in OCC1, PHTH and POTH, passing every component (individual, group, theory, practical). C for anatomy, physiology, complementaries and electives.

title: Student Athletes
points: See Important Information for Students for inter-university athletes and Sports Practicum students.

title: Probation, Withdrawal, or Dismissal from the School of Physical and Occupational Therapy
points: Failures or unprofessional conduct trigger a full review. Probation: CGPA under 3.0, a failed requirement, or an integrity or conduct incident, with monitoring and possibly remedial work.

Unsatisfactory, requiring withdrawal: CGPA under 2.30 (B.Sc.) or 2.7 (M.Sc.A. and Qualifying Year), two or more failed courses including a repeat, or a second incident. No readmission to either program.
Plagiarism, cheating and misconduct can mean dismissal; criminal activity goes to the committee and may show unsuitability. Leaving voluntarily removes you from program courses.

title: Student Advising in Physical and Occupational Therapy
points: See p. 1089, or contact the School.

title: Related Services
points: See pp. 79, 81. Ask an Advisor directs any undergraduate to the right place.

title: The Wellness Hub
points: Awareness, prevention and early intervention, with a Local Wellness Advisor for this School.

title: Campus Life and Engagement (New Student Experience)
points: Helps new students with the catalogue and new-student site, with workshops, advice and referrals.

title: Career Planning Service (CaPS)
points: Career advising, workshops, events and resources through graduation.

title: Becoming a Licensed Occupational or Physical Therapist
points: The bachelor's gives access to the professional master's in the same field.

title: Licensing Regulations
points: M.Sc.A. graduates can seek licensure worldwide; each place sets its own exams, courses or TOEFL. Quebec needs a permit from the regulator and working French, spoken and written (p. 70).
OTs elsewhere in Canada pass a National Certification Exam. PTs elsewhere have needed the Physiotherapy National Exam or proof of Quebec licensing since 1993.

title: Program Accreditation
points: The Professional Master's program has received accreditation status by Physiotherapy Education Accreditation Canada.
The Occupational Therapy program is accredited by the Canadian Association of Occupational Therapists.

title: Canadian National Offices
points: Canadian Association of Occupational Therapists: 2720 Queensview Dr., Unit 1142, Ottawa. Canadian Physiotherapy Association: 350 Sparks St., Suite 1209, Ottawa. Canadian Alliance of Physiotherapy Regulators: 1243 Islington Ave., Suite 501, Toronto.

title: Quebec Provincial Offices
points: Ordre des ergothérapeutes du Québec: 2021 avenue Union, bureau 920, Montréal. Ordre professionnel de la physiothérapie du Québec: 7151 rue Jean-Talon est, bureau 700, Anjou.

title: International Offices
points: Check each country's or state's requirements.

title: Clinical Placement Requirements: French Proficiency, Vaccination, and CPR
points: Clinical hours for membership are in the master's programs. Quebec's health system runs in French under the Charter, even at bilingual sites, so you need oral and written French for placements, at the level in the admission guides, before clinical work. Without it, placements are limited and graduation may be delayed. Keep CPR/AED at Health Care Provider level throughout.

title: Vaccinations
points: Finish before clinical courses, and start early, as schedules take months. Upload to the Wellness portal in September of U3 or Qualifying Year; the Hub must mark it Complete by March 1, for the M1 Summer term's two clinical courses. The Hub keeps your details confidential from the School.

title: Physical and Occupational Therapy Programs
points: Bachelor's in Rehabilitation Science lead to the M.Sc.A. The School stresses client-centred, evidence-based practice, clinical reasoning, ethics, teamwork and professionalism.

title: Admission Requirements for Undergraduate Programs
points: 90 credits, leading to the M.Sc.A. required for practice. McGill Admissions handles it: Service Point, 3415 McTavish St. See also Casper and French requirements. Those required to withdraw can't be readmitted.

Quebec DCS prerequisites: Biology 00UK, 00XU, 01Y5, 01YJ, NYA; Chemistry 00UL, 00UM, 00XV, 01Y6, 01YH, NYA, NYB; Math 00UN, 00UP, 01Y1, 01Y2, NYA, NYB; Physics 00UR, 00US, 00UT, 01Y7, 01YF, 01YG, NYA, NYB, NYC. Plus Casper and French proof.

After a year of college or university: two terms each of biology, general chemistry and physics, and one of organic chemistry, all with labs, plus differential and integral calculus, Casper and French. UK, Commonwealth, French Baccalaureate and IB: see Admissions.

title: McGill Inter-Faculty Transfer
points: At least 24 McGill credits, with two terms each of biology and general chemistry, one of organic, two of physics (or three at CEGEP) with labs, two of calculus, Casper and French.
Out-of-Quebec high school graduates in 120-credit Science need these too. With under 24 credits, or a degree by August 1, apply through Enrolment Services instead.

title: Fall Term
points: or MATH 140 Calculus 1.
or PHYS 131 Mechanics and Waves.

title: Winter Term
points: PHYS 142 is an alternative; CHEM 212 can be taken intensively in May. Also Casper and French.
Inter-faculty transfers: form on Minerva from March 1, Casper and French, all by April 1; incomplete or late files may be invalid. See p. 39.

You enter as U1. Up to 30 transfer credits, requested in your first term and processed by December; they must match McGill's in content and evaluation without overlaps. Courses are set by year, with no mixing, so the degree takes exactly three years. No switching between OT and PT; apply to the other's Qualifying Year in your final year.

title: Admission Requirements for Qualifying Year – Master of Science (Applied)
points: With a degree other than McGill's OT or PT B.Sc., complete a Qualifying Year first, applying through Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies. See SPOT's Admissions page.

title: Program Description
points: Health sciences for OT: occupation in daily life, community rehabilitation, client-centred and evidence-based practice, reasoning, ethics, teamwork and professionalism.

title: Required Courses (75 credits)
points: ANAT 321 or ANAT 323, not both.

title: Complementary Courses (15 credits)
points: Before U3, from Psychology, Management (personnel, private practice), Academic Writing, Sociology or Anthropology, French or English second language if needed (up to 6). Also a 3-credit Sports Medicine Practicum, by interview, and up to 3 of personal interest.

title: Program Description
points: Health sciences for PT: reasoning, diagnostics, evidence-based practice, community rehabilitation, teamwork and professionalism.

title: Required Courses (81 credits)
points: ANAT 321 or ANAT 323, not both.

title: Complementary Courses (6-9 credits)
points: Before U3, from Psychology, Management (personnel, private practice), Academic Writing, Sociology or Anthropology, and French or English second language if needed (up to 6).

refs.label: Students may take PHTH 301 Sports Medicine Practicum. (3 credits) as a U2 complementary course.

title: About the Faculty of Science
points: Professors and students work together, from cognitive science to cosmology, and you can join their research. Fifteen departments offer the B.Sc., with fieldwork, research projects, internships and cross-disciplinary work.

title: McGill's Faculty of Science
points: McGill's second-largest faculty: nine schools and departments, five affiliated, multi-department programs and a dozen-plus research centres. 5,000+ undergraduates, 1,000+ graduates and 260+ faculty. Ten Nobel laureates in its history: seven alumni, three faculty or staff.
Leading in Canada on astrophysics, climate, green chemistry, developmental biology, earth systems, biodiversity, nanoscience, social neuroscience, sustainability and AI.

Field study in East Africa, Barbados and Panama; Fessenden Professorships and Prizes for commercializing research; the $120 million Life Sciences Research Complex; Canada's first comprehensive Earth System Science Program; the Office of Science Education; Science Undergraduate Research Awards.

title: Programs and Teaching in Science
points: Leading researchers teach undergraduates, and independent study lets you contribute. All B.Sc. programs can include an internship, with Work Study and research jobs too. Admission is selective.

Two diplomas, all credits at McGill: Environment (30 credits, p. 870) for B.Sc. or B.A. holders, and Meteorology (30 credits, p. 1134), one year for math, engineering, physics and similar graduates. The B.A. & Sc. is joint with Arts (p. 428).

title: Academic Units
points: Units offering B.Sc. courses; some, such as Pathology, belong to other faculties. See p. 1107 for structuring your degree.

title: Location
points: SOUSA: Frank Dawson Adams Building, Room 23, 3450 University St. It advises B.A. & Sc. and B.Sc. students.

title: Prospective High School, CEGEP, and University Transfer Applicants
points: McGill's Admissions Office reviews files. You pick a Program Group when applying, which sets your program range and maybe requirements. Changing needs a competitive Intrafaculty Transfer after a year.

title: Current McGill Students
points: See Interfaculty Transfer (p. 39) and SOUSA.

title: Degree Advising and SOUSA
points: SOUSA houses degree advisors for the B.Sc. and B.A. & Sc., helping with planning, study away, readmission, transfers and hard times. Your advisor is named on your Unofficial Transcript; advisor.science@mcgill.ca.

Ask about Foundation, planning, requirements, rules, exchange, deferring exams, transfers and readmission. Write to the Associate Dean, Student Affairs for special requests; the Committee on Student Standing hears appeals.

title: Program Advising
points: In each department, not assigned. Ask about requirements, courses, registration problems, careers, graduate school and research.

title: First Year Advising
points: See Science's new student site. The B.Sc. is 120 credits with a mandatory Foundation Program (p. 1111); Advanced Standing from CEGEP, IB, A-Levels, AP or French Baccalaureate may exempt you, but you must still check you meet it.
U0 (97–120 credits needed): register for Foundation courses, with SOUSA's advice. U1 (96 or fewer): declare your program at registration, consulting a program advisor and your degree advisor.

title: Degree Requirements for the Faculty of Science
points: Advisors help, but you are responsible for courses, requirements and deadlines. Misunderstanding is no excuse.

title: Bachelor of Science (B.Sc.)
points: Meet all the requirements below.

refs.label: Time and Credit Limit for the Completion of the Degree

title: Bachelor of Arts and Science (B.A. & Sc.)
points: Joint with Arts (p. 150), with advising through SOUSA and Science's Associate Dean. See p. 430.

title: Diploma (Dip.) in Environment
points: One year full-time for graduates reorienting. 30 credits at McGill; C or better in required and complementary courses.

title: Diploma (Dip.) in Meteorology
points: An intensive year of theory and applied work for B.Sc. or B.Eng. graduates in physics, applied math or similar. 30 credits at McGill; C or better.

title: B.Sc./M.Sc. Track
points: Early admission for strong McGill undergraduates into a Science M.Sc. or M.A.

title: Program Requirements
points: 120 credits. Your Program Group limits your choices. Do the Foundation Program, or get exempted through Advanced Standing or Placement Exams (p. 1111). Then, usually at the start of U1, pick a structure (Liberal, Major, Honours or Joint) and specific programs.

title: Course Requirements for Bachelor of Science
points: C or better in required and complementary courses, including basic science. If you fail: pass a supplemental, do extra work if allowed, or repeat. Substitutions only in special cases.

Normally one repeat; failure means below C, or J or KF. A third try needs the Associate Dean's permission by email through your advisor; if denied there and on appeal to the Committee, you must withdraw. Failed complementaries can be replaced, with a D kept as an elective credit. A repeated required D gives credit once.

title: Course Overlap
points: No extra credit for content overlapping McGill, CEGEP, other university, AP, A Level, IB or French Baccalaureate work. Check exclusions with SOUSA or the department.
Double-prefix courses like LING 345 / COMP 345: take your own department's version if offered at once; otherwise whichever fits.

Statistics and computing from other faculties need the Associate Dean's permission (computing only exceptionally); Environment majors may take required statistics in Agricultural and Environmental Sciences. Arts students: computer course credit follows each course description.

Statistics: credit for only one listed introductory course; PSYC 204 blocks the list; only one intermediate course, except PSYC 305 with ECON 227D1/D2 or 257D1/D2; MATH 324 or 357 blocks the list. For other 500-level statistics, ask an advisor about overlap.

title: Courses Outside the Faculties of Arts and of Science
points: 6 credits a year, 18 in total, with prerequisites and the instructor's permission. See the Undergraduate Handbook, 3.2.2, for approved and restricted courses: restricted never count; others need the Associate Dean's approval by email to your advisor. Minerva may let you in, but excess or unapproved courses get flagged for no credit.

BIOT, EXMD and PHAR count as Science. Music is outside, except MUAR. RELG counts, except B.Th. or S.T.M. courses and those needing the Chair's permission. No credit for "how to" courses, such as software, SQL or COBOL, shop, drawing or professional practice. Outside computing and statistics only exceptionally.

May exceed 18 if needed for the program: Bieler School students, Software Engineering majors, and Liberal students in a Music Major Concentration (up to 36). The limit applies to the Nutrition Minor; take Science equivalents.

title: Correspondence, Distance Education, or Web-Based Courses
points: Transfer credit needs prior approval from the department for content and SOUSA for delivery (Handbook 4.5). Outside courses must come from an accredited degree-granting school, count there, and fit within credit limits. They can't meet program requirements, except for serious documented reasons.

title: Courses in English as a Second Language (ESL)
points: For those whose first language isn't English, with under five years in English secondary school. Up to 12 credits, including academic writing.

title: First-Year Seminars: Registration for First-Year Seminars in the Faculty of Science
points: For new U0 or U1 students, first-come, 25 at most: closer contact with professors, and current research methods. Only one.

title: First-Year Seminars
points: Arts seminars are open to Science students (p. 167).

title: Course Credit Weight
points: One credit is about 45 hours of class, lab and personal study.

title: Minimum Credit Requirement
points: As in your admission letter. Transfers need 60 McGill credits. Readmitted students follow the current requirements; after five years away, possibly 60 new credits and a new GPA, or fewer if approved.

title: Advanced Standing
points: 120 credits normally; up to 30 granted for DEC, IB, French Baccalaureate, A Levels, AP (declare scores of 4 or 5 at first registration), or college courses counted toward a diploma. A Science DCS normally exempts you from basic sciences; others may be too.
No credit for overlaps with past credit or exemptions. You may still choose to do 120 McGill credits, within repeat limits.

title: Equivalencies for Non-Basic Science Courses
points: CHEM 212, CHEM 222, PSYC 204 and others vary by CEGEP, and may need a higher grade. See the Transfer Credit site or your SOUSA advisor.

title: Residency Requirement for the B.Sc.
points: 60 credits at McGill, excluding Foundation, and normally two-thirds of departmental requirements, not counting a prior McGill degree. Study Away or Exchange can be exempted with department and Associate Dean approval; some departments have other rules. Diplomas: 30 credits.

title: Time and Credit Limit for the Completion of the Degree
points: With 96 or fewer credits to do: eight terms at most; Foundation students a year after first registering. Finish within 120 credits; you get credit up to the term you reach it. Going past either limit needs the Associate Dean's approval by email, for reasons like program change or part-time, then only required and complementary courses count. Those with Advanced Standing from IB, AP, A-Levels and similar may do 120 after admission (p. 55).

title: Overview of Programs Offered
points: Foundation (p. 1111); Liberal, Major, Honours and Joint by Program Group (p. 1112); Arts programs open to Science students (p. 1114). See p. 1107.

title: Science Foundation Program
points: 30 credits of basic science before your three-year program; Advanced Standing may exempt you. U0 students take these in first year; U1 students declare a program, with program and degree advisors.

title: Program Description
points: For those needing 97–120 credits; SOUSA must approve courses (newstudentadvising.science@mcgill.ca). 30 credits, including at least seven Approved Foundation Year Science courses.

title: General Math and Science Breadth
points: Six courses: 2 MATH and 4 of BIOL, CHEM or PHYS; or 3 MATH and 3 of BIOL, CHEM or PHYS.

title: Science Complementary
points: A seventh from the list. Missing grade 12 biology, chemistry or physics? Take one. Many take more to keep majors open; check department rules. Five courses a term at most. Some medical and dental schools have set requirements.

title: Degree Requirements — B.Sc.
points: To graduate, you need both the program's courses and the degree's requirements, including Foundation and structure (p. 1106). Fitting them together is your responsibility, and SOUSA's Degree Planning Guide helps.

title: List of Approved Foundation Year Science Courses
points: Choose as instructed. CHEM 120 isn't open after CHEM 115. One each of first and second calculus, and first and second physics.

title: Electives
points: Introductory Science or Arts courses; see the recommended list. Some other faculties' courses are allowed, with limits.

title: Bachelor of Science Programs (by Program Group)
points: Your Program Group, chosen when applying, sets your range. Changing is a competitive Intra-Faculty Transfer after a year.

title: Undergraduate Research Opportunities
points: Most B.Sc. students do research, at McGill, hospitals, other universities or in the field. See awards like USRA and SURA, the Dean's Multidisciplinary Undergraduate Research List, and Internships and Field Studies (p. 1117).

refs.label: Getting Involved in Research as an Undergraduate

title: Getting Involved in Research as an Undergraduate
points: Voluntary, for credit or paid; some are formal programs, others come from talking with professors. The Science site has tips.

title: Internships and Field Studies
points: Some include research (p. 1117).

title: Beyond McGill
points: Try foundations, agencies, hospitals, other universities or scholarly societies, including in other countries.

title: Research Project Courses
points: Supervised research for credit, under names like majors or honours project, advanced lab or independent study. They can help toward the Dean's Research List or B.Sc. Global Designation.

title: "396" Undergraduate Research Project Courses
points: Offered by all Science units, such as ANAT, ATOC, BIOC and BIOL 396, plus COGS, ENVR, HGEN, MDPH, NSCI, PATH and BASC 396, and FSCI 396, 397 and 398D1/D2. Electives, generally after a term, even outside your department, approved by supervisor and department.

title: Undergraduate Science Showcase
points: A yearly event where students present research and projects, open to the community.

title: Undergraduate Student Research Awards
points: Fund projects, usually in summer, at McGill and sometimes elsewhere.

title: Tri-Agency Undergraduate Student Research Awards: NSERC USRA, SSHRC USRA, CIHR USRA
points: Funded by NSERC, CIHR and SSHRC, for paid supervised research that encourages graduate study. For Canadian citizens, permanent residents and protected persons.

title: SURA: Science Undergraduate Research Awards
points: Since summer 2007, like USRA but open to international students too: full-time supervised research, funded by donors, supervisors and the Faculty.

title: Science Field Studies and Internships
points: Coordinates field semesters for all undergraduates, and internships for Science and B.A. & Sc. students, plus Arts students in Environment, Computer Science, Software Engineering, Geography, Math and Psychology. By appointment: 2001 McGill College, 646B.

title: Internship Program: Industrial Practicum (IP) and Internship Year in Science (IYS)
points: Industrial Practicum (4 months) for those groups; Internship Year (8, 12 or 16 months) for Science only. Requires full-time status beforehand, 27+ credits done, 12+ left, and CGPA 2.7. International students have restrictions. Two practica or an Internship Year add "Internship Program" to your Science degree name.

title: Field Study Semester Programs
points: Research-based 15-credit semesters in East Africa, Barbados and Panama, plus shorter courses in Biology, Earth and Planetary Sciences, and Geography.

title: B.Sc. Global Designation
points: Internships and study abroad can earn this at graduation.

title: Summer Studies in the Faculty of Science
points: Special summer courses; see Minerva for all.

title: Biology
points: Off-campus field courses.

title: Earth and Planetary Sciences
points: Off-campus field courses. Confirm with the instructor by January 31 for EPSC 231 and December 31 for EPSC 331 and 341; no late registrants, and withdrawals need a documented reason. EPSC 240 students may join 231 by requesting a permit.

title: Geography
points: One off-campus field course.

title: Examinations
points: See p. 62; applies up to 500 level. Tentative schedules come a month after classes start, and final ones after two. Don't plan to leave before exams end.

title: Browse Academic Units and Programs
points: Approved for 2026–27; some units belong to other faculties. See p. 1107, and p. 1111 if you're from outside Quebec.

title: About Biochemistry
points: Chemistry applied to biological processes in cells and molecules, since around 1900. It studies how proteins, nucleic acids, lipids, vitamins and hormones work in brain function, cell growth, signalling, inheritance and disease, and how reactions are regulated.

It underlies understanding of disease and treatment, and practical advances in medicine, veterinary work, agriculture and biotech, including protein function and genetic engineering. Specialties: neurochemistry, bioorganic, clinical, physical, molecular genetics, pharmacology and immunochemistry.

Liberal: flexible, with a minor or broader science. Major: specialized in the last two years, toward professional and research careers. Honours: adds U3 lab research; the B.Sc./M.Sc. track shortens a graduate degree. See p. 1107.

First year: lectures and labs, cell and molecular biology, and organic and physical chemistry. Then a second lab, research through BIOC 396, 462 and 491, and other complementaries. Graduates work in chemical and pharmaceutical R&D, government and hospital labs and management, or go on to research and teaching.

points: Microbiology studies bacteria, viruses, single-celled eukaryotes and parasites, their roles in disease, food, spoilage and water, and basic life processes, and how to harness them for antibiotics, vaccines and industry.

Research: microbial physiology and genetics, pathogenesis, virology, cellular and molecular immunology, parasitology. title: About Physiology
points: Rooted in biology, chemistry, math and physics, overlapping other biomedical sciences and feeding clinical medicine. Studies molecules to systems in vertebrates: cardiovascular, respiratory, gastrointestinal and renal, exercise, neurophysiology, endocrinology, immunology, biophysics and biomathematics, with links to many departments.
Careers in teaching, government and lab work, or medicine, dentistry and graduate study. All programs share a core, and U1 is identical except for the Joint programs, so you can decide later.

New students must contact the Student Affairs Officer for advising; returning students should check regularly, especially before final year. Complementary courses aren't electives: choose only from those listed (p. 36).

title: About Psychiatry
points: No B.Sc., but PSYT courses run through Science, for Arts, Science and graduate students, under their faculties' rules, including PSYT 400D1/D2.

title: Location
points: 1033 Pine Ave. W., Room 104.

title: About Psychology
points: Programs in Arts (p. 391) and Science. The science of mind and behaviour, both social (culture, groups, relationships) and biological (neural basis, including other species).

Lab experiments and systematic observation seek general principles of perception, learning, motivation, cognition and social life, using measurement and statistics. It draws on biology, linguistics, sociology, philosophy and math. A young science, closing the gap between theory and fact.

title: Undergraduate Studies
points: Teaches core knowledge, theory and method, not applied training. A bachelor's isn't a professional qualification: Quebec's Order of Psychologists requires a doctorate, some undergraduate courses, and French. Useful also for medicine, education, social work, communication sciences and business. Honours adds research, high standards, and small groups with faculty.

title: Graduate Studies
points: A career needs graduate study, usually a Ph.D., for universities, institutes, hospitals, agencies, government, companies or consulting. Branches: social, cognitive, physiological, experimental, clinical, child, industrial, educational and more. Admission varies; both Major and Honours can qualify with high grades and sometimes research. Check requirements during U2.

title: Information Meetings for New Students
points: Attend before registering: June for CEGEP entrants, August for others; B.Sc. students have a separate one. Bring transcripts and look at this catalogue and the schedule first. January entrants should see an adviser in early December.

points: A term or year at a partner, earning McGill credit and paying McGill tuition (billed as 15 credits a term). Over 150 universities in 39 countries; spaces vary, and some are faculty-specific.

points: All nationalities. Be full-time and degree-seeking, meet your faculty's criteria, and have a full year (24 McGill credits) by the start. One or two terms.

title: Transfer of Credits from Host Institution
points: Host grades aren't on your transcript or in your CGPA; it shows the exchange, transfer credits and exemptions. Start once registered, with syllabi, and finish soon after. Send an official transcript to officialschooldocs@mcgill.ca.

points: Apply and pay the host directly as a visiting student, for places without exchanges. Ask your faculty's Student Affairs Office and the host's admissions.

title: Funding Opportunities for Going Abroad
points: Awards and aid exist; see below and McGill Abroad.

title: Government Student Financial Assistance
points: On exchange you're full-time, so Canadians can apply for government aid, and Americans for Title IV loans within limits (ask Student Aid). On Independent Study Away, no aid through McGill; check with the host.

title: Scholarships and Awards
points: Renewable awards may continue for a year if you're full-time elsewhere. Annual in-course awards use only McGill grades, so exchange students miss them the next year.

title: Mobility Bursaries for Exchanges
points: Quebec's PMICSE funds need-based help for undergraduates approved for an eligible exchange, through Student Aid.

title: Enriched Educational Opportunities (EEO) Bursaries
points: Need-based help for field semesters, field courses, and unpaid off-campus internships and research, through Student Aid.
